rationale: 5.8.2 allows only one session per user, which is not the same as allowing only one active user on a workstation.
adjudicator_note: The matrix rule constrains the user, the source constrains the workstation; worth confirming at sign-off.

rationale: Single sessions and log off and on are covered but the requirement to log out or suspend a shift before a second user may log into that workstation is not.
Access can be restricted by POS terminal, implying terminal identity, but a unique workstation ID per device is not required.
Role-based and attribute-based authorisation are obliged but deriving the available modules from the device's workstation ID at login is not.
7.1.12 makes the role the carrier of permissions, so what a user sees follows the assigned role rather than the device.
adjudicator_note: Sits in tension with MOM-0006, where the workstation ID also determines available modules.

rationale: Roles group permissions but nothing obliges the visible product range at a POS to be scoped by role, which is what makes a restaurant till show only the F&B menu.
2.12.23 restricts product sale by 'Sale board type' and by specific POS workstation, but binding a workstation to a ticketing, F&B or retail sales board is not itself obliged.
adjudicator_note: 2.12.23 was not in this row's candidate list; its full text appears in other rows of the same chunk.

rationale: Opening the front end matching the workstation sales board at cashier login is missing.
7.1.12 requires configurable role-based access control with a Finance role, so entitlement follows the user rather than the workstation they log in from.
adjudicator_note: 7.1.12 is reused from an adjacent POS candidate set.

rationale: Roles and dynamic contextual permissions are required but automatic loading of a user's access at login on the admin web is not stated.
Roles are configurable and assignable to users but holding several roles simultaneously is not obliged.
Role-based access control is obliged but choosing or swapping between assigned roles at login, to see the corresponding privileges, is not.
The login behaviour distinguishing single-role from multi-role users is missing.
Accounting-grade recording of all platform transactions is required but classification down to individual user and tenant is not.
5.11.1 requires accounting-grade recording of all platform transactions and 5.11.2 balanced double entries, which is the transaction-level ledger used for reconciliation.
Journal entries and double-entry posting are required but a second ledger held separately from the primary ledger is not.
5.12.7 requires profit and loss, balance sheet, trial balance and general ledger reports to be generated from the ledger.
5.11.3 requires posted transactions never to be deleted or altered, which is the append-only ledger.
Balance-sheet reporting and payment reconciliation are required but automatic reconciliation of the ledger to produce the balance sheet is not.
Natural-language reporting exists in BI but a finance-specific AI reporting layer for accountants is not required.
A design intention to keep the data model AI-ready, with nothing testable attached.
All platform transactions are recorded as balanced debit and credit entries, which covers the listed sale, gateway and gift-card events.
2.9.11 requires tax profiles per product and 2.9.14 automatic tax calculation on sale, which forces per-item rather than basket-level VAT.
adjudicator_note: MOM-0030 and MOM-0031 state the same requirement twice.

rationale: 2.9.11 requires multiple tax rates and per-product tax profiles, so lines carrying different rates are taxed separately.
The posting rule that placing an order creates no ledger entry is a revenue-recognition rule no candidate states.
Automatic tax calculation on sale is required but receivables recognition triggered by payment capture is not.
Deferred revenue accounting is required but carrying the payment liability in a second ledger and reporting it by visit date is not.
Configurable recognition and automatic deferred-to-earned movement exist but recognition triggered by the visit or redemption is not required.
adjudicator_note: 5.12.15 requires recognition on ticket sale payment, which contradicts recognition at redemption.

rationale: The rule holding refunds out of the primary ledger until they are fully resolved is a ledger design rule no candidate carries.
Deferred revenue accounting is required but holding revenue in a separate ledger until the visit date so refunds and transfers stay clean is not.
5.12.8 requires configurable revenue recognition rules, with schedules configurable by product type.
Recognition schedules by product type and by sale site are required but immediate recognition for POS sales is not stated.
5.7.97 requires gift-card redemption accounting alongside liability, expiry and breakage recognition.
Recognition schedules configurable by product type exist but straight-line or per-visit recognition for annual passes is not named.
5.12.124 moves deferred revenue to earned on ticket expiry and 5.7.19 requires accounting treatment of unused and expired tickets.
Refund management and refund reporting are obliged but routing a POS refund through a refund service connected to the ledger is an architecture step the matrix does not require.
Refund types and approval workflows are configurable but time-banded rules disallowing refunds after a cut-off are not.
5.7.92 requires chargeback notification handling, dispute management, investigation and resolution tracking.
5.7.94 requires full and partial credit memos linked to invoices, refunds and adjustments with audit trails maintained.
Full, partial and pro-rata refunds with approval workflows are obliged but a refund percentage varying by time band before the event is not.
Self-service online refund requests are required and refunds are handled at the POS, covering both initiation points.
11.1.30 requires approval workflows for refund requests before they proceed.
19.2.82 requires self-service refund requests raised from the guest's own account.
Refund approval workflows plus operational notifications to staff about approvals cover notifying operations to approve, reject or query a request.
4.2.18 requires full and partial refunds.
Refund approvals and role-based privileges exist but an authorised override replacing the preset refund percentage is not obliged.
7.1.12 requires fully configurable roles with permissions grouped and assigned, which is what an unrestricted custom-role model asks for.
Case management with configurable statuses exists but client staff logging in to view and answer their own tickets and chats is not required.
22.8.26 requires a complete audit history of conversations, transfers, escalations, case creation and agent activity.
Historical lookup by ticket or item exists but access for a client's own contact centre to investigate reservation and ticket issues is not specified.
Reconciliation and period close are required but running settlement on a weekly or monthly cycle is not specified.
Automatic matching across statements, gateways and transactions is required but the ingest, parse, match, classify and auto-resolve pipeline is not.
Automatic matching is required but escalating only genuine mismatches to human review is not.
5.7.25 requires a configurable chart of accounts structure held in the platform.
5.7.24 requires maintenance and synchronisation of ERP chart-of-accounts structures and 5.7.4 entry of an external chart of accounts.
Deferred and recognised revenue reports are required but a finance dashboard carrying gross, net, recognised, deferred revenue and refunds together is not.
Revenue reporting is required but graphical charts with a period selector are not.
Multi-tenancy and active/inactive status exist but a legal-entities register listing each tenant site with its country and currency is not required.
5.7.24 and 5.7.4 require company code, GL account and related ERP codes to be held against the chart of accounts.
5.7.26 requires asset, liability, equity, revenue and expense account types.
5.12.101 requires multi-level chart of account structures, which is the parent-account hierarchy.
5.7.24 requires cost centre and profit centre dimensions alongside the GL account.
Automatic offset account posting is required but configurable transaction-to-account and payment-account mapping is not.
5.7.89 requires fiscal year and fiscal period management, which carries the country-specific year definition.
5.7.89 requires authorised users to open, close, lock and re-open accounting periods.
ERP integration is required but a console for managing external system connections is not.
All platform transactions are recorded and general ledger reporting exists but a transactions list with daily counts and totals is not required.
A pending or failed sync status per transaction awaiting an external integration is required by no candidate.

The matrix requires multi-level chart-of-account structures and product-level revenue reports but never obliges a transaction detail view that exposes CoA mapping, payment method and product detail on a single line.
No candidate requires transaction lines to carry a sale / deferred / redemption revenue state, which is a data-model requirement the matrix does not oblige anywhere in view.
The matrix requires balanced debit and credit entries to be created but omits the posted journal entry list view that lets a user read them back.
5.12.87 requires manual journal entry creation, which is exactly the manual booking capability asked for.
The matrix requires manual journal entry creation but omits the maker-checker gate that holds a voucher out of the ledger until a finance manager or director approves it.
adjudicator_note: Posting control with segregation-of-duties implications; worth confirming at sign-off which role holds approval authority.

rationale: The matrix requires revenue allocation reports and allocation methods but not a screen that charts recognized against unrecognized wallet revenue.
5.12.11 and 5.12.13 require revenue recognition rules to carry validity periods and support inheritance and cloning, which cannot be tested without the rule configuration surface this row asks for.
Recognition schedules are configurable by product type but immediate recognition of F&B revenue on sale is not stated.
adjudicator_note: 5.12.1 requires recognition according to accounting policies 'rather than immediately upon sale', which sits awkwardly with the minuted rule that F&B revenue is recognised immediately; worth resolving at sign-off.

rationale: 5.12.4 requires annual memberships to be recognised over defined periods but does not fix the monthly straight-line method nor the recognition of the residual balance at membership expiry.
5.7.62 requires package revenue allocation and 5.12.111 the percentage method, which together require splitting a package price across its constituent products.
The matrix covers allocation across products within a package but omits allocation across legal entities or venues, which needs a legal-entity dimension on the allocation.
5.12.111 requires fixed-percentage allocation only; the fixed-amount split mode is not obliged.
Reconciliation of card against ticketing payments is obliged but a single payments screen consolidating every gateway and on-site tender is not.
4.2.19 requires automatic reconciliation of transactions between POS, online sales, payment gateways, banks and financial records, which is the matching capability described.
4.2.19 requires the automatic reconciliation to identify discrepancies, which is precisely the gateway-versus-internal variance flag asked for.
adjudicator_note: 4.2.19 was surfaced as a candidate on the adjacent reconciliation row rather than on this one.

rationale: 4.2.19 obliges reconciliation but says nothing about the mechanism, so the monthly file-based comparison rather than per-transaction API checks is unspecified and drives the integration design.
adjudicator_note: Source explicitly rules out a per-transaction check; confirm settlement file format and cadence with each gateway at sign-off.

rationale: No candidate requires bulk refund processing; refunding thousands of transactions in one action is a batch capability the matrix does not oblige.
No candidate requires bulk selection of refunds by event or date across both online and on-site bookings.
The matrix requires approval workflows for refund requests but not an approval gate over a whole selected refund batch before it is processed.
adjudicator_note: 11.1.30 appears in the neighbouring refund-screen candidate set, not in this row's own candidates.

rationale: The matrix requires self-service refund requests and a refund approval workflow but omits the finance and operations queue screen and its three outcomes - accept, request more information, auto-deny.
No candidate requires a consolidated shift or session view showing open and closed sessions per workstation with expected cash and card totals.
5.9.2 requires a blind cashier close-out with over-shorts captured, which is the same process.
5.9.6 requires an alert whenever the expected and actual till values differ at end of shift and 5.9.2 requires over-shorts to be recorded, which is the shortage and overage flag.
adjudicator_note: 5.9.6 comes from an adjacent row's candidate set.

rationale: The matrix requires an alert on a till variance but does not oblige the configurable option to block shift closure until the discrepancy is resolved or explained.
5.9.8 requires configurable supervisor approval for opening and closing a cashier's session, which is the authorization asked for.
adjudicator_note: 5.9.8 is drawn from an adjacent row's candidate set.

rationale: 5.9.9 requires a session-closing report with totals per payment type including cash denomination, which is the denomination-itemized closing receipt.
The matrix requires the shift closing report to be generated but not its automatic distribution by email to finance and leadership.
8.7.23 requires real-time analytics generically; the live till monitor showing per-workstation cash status and open and close codes, and the refresh feed behind it, is not obliged.
A supervisor may withdraw cash from a float mid-day but a configurable drawer limit prompting the cashier to unload excess cash is not obliged.
5.8.8 requires the mid-day withdrawal to be traced but does not state that the unloaded amount is held separately and folded into the final shift-close reconciliation.
Mid-day cash withdrawal and end-of-shift variance alerts are obliged but a mid-shift partial hold state preserving the removed cash for reconciliation is not modelled.
5.9.3 requires an end-of-shift report for cashiers with consolidated amounts by payment means and product type, which is the cashier shift report in the end-of-day set.
The matrix obliges end-of-day close-out of each cash register but does not require a distinct till report in the end-of-day report set.
No candidate requires a sales-by-location report; reporting sales broken down by selling location is not obliged anywhere in view.
5.9.3 requires amounts collected by means of payment on the end-of-shift report, but a standalone end-of-day payment type summary is not obliged.
The matrix covers cash register close-out but not a cash management report in the end-of-day set.
5.9.6 requires an alert on a till variance but no variance report is obliged as part of the end-of-day set.
adjudicator_note: 5.9.6 is reused from an adjacent shift-close candidate set.

rationale: No candidate requires a refund report; refund activity reporting is not obliged in the end-of-day set.
Consolidated per-cashier end-of-shift reporting and end-of-day register close-out are obliged but a single end-of-day consolidated report across the site is not.
No candidate requires cash variances to post automatically to a dedicated overage/shortage ledger account, which is a chart-of-accounts and posting-rule requirement.
5.12.7 and 5.7.73 require a Profit and Loss statement and 5.7.55 site-level P&L, which is the automatically generated P&L with revenue by category against cost of sales.
5.7.74 requires balance sheet reporting and 5.12.7 lists the Balance Sheet among the standard financial statements.
5.7.72 requires trial balance reporting and 5.12.7 requires Trial Balance and General Ledger reports, which is the trial balance and ledger view.
5.12.2 requires deferred revenue accounting and 5.7.77 and 5.12.122 require deferred revenue reporting and aging, which is the revenue and deferred-revenue analytics asked for.
5.7.55 requires site-level profit and loss reporting, which necessarily reports revenue performance per site.
adjudicator_note: 5.7.55 is reused from the adjacent P&L candidate set; it is not among this row's own candidates.

rationale: No candidate requires a consolidated financial approval centre or controls screen listing transactions with exceptions or variances awaiting review.
The matrix requires daily, weekly and monthly reconciliation and product reports but does not oblige scheduled automatic generation and distribution of finance summary reports.
5.12.7 explicitly lists the Cash Flow Statement among the standard financial statements the system shall generate.
The matrix requires named financial reports but nothing obliges the operational and review-related reporting pillar, which the source itself leaves unenumerated.
adjudicator_note: The source names this pillar without listing its reports; the scope should be pinned down at sign-off.

rationale: 5.7.25 requires a configurable Chart of Accounts and 5.7.24 requires maintenance and synchronisation of the COA structures used by ERP and finance systems, which is the native plus externally mapped requirement.
19.1.24 requires a self-service white label configuration portal and 19.1.19 tenant-specific branding, which is the no-code builder module.
19.1.1 requires the mobile app logo to be changeable through configuration, which is the logo upload asked for.
Tenant branding is configurable but nothing obliges a set of selectable colour themes for the guest app.
19.1.3 requires configurable app icons, which is exactly this row.
19.1.5 requires configurable fonts, which covers custom font upload for the guest app.
No candidate requires a live preview of branding and layout changes before they are published from the builder.
No candidate requires size, format and pixel constraints on assets uploaded through the builder, which is what protects the app layout from a tenant's oversized artwork.
No candidate requires uploaded fonts and images to be validated at the point of upload.
No candidate requires the builder to explain its upload restrictions to the tenant admin; this is interface copy the matrix does not oblige.
Logo and home screen navigation are configurable, but the layout builder's control of header, footer, bottom navigation icons and their colours is not obliged.
19.1.10 requires configurable promotional banners but not control over banner sizing.
19.1.11 requires configurable promotional content blocks, which is the activation of promotions and blocks from the builder.
No candidate requires a configurable tiered refund policy per business, which is a rules engine keyed on time before visit and determines the refundable amount.
20.4.1, 20.4.6 and 20.4.8 require a module marketplace with per-module pricing, installation and removal, which is module enablement per tenant under licence.
adjudicator_note: These ids come from an adjacent marketplace candidate set; confirm the named modules (Ticketing, Membership, Events, Attractions, Virtual Queue, F&B, Retail, Parking) are each licensable units.

rationale: Lost and Found and AI Concierge exist as features, but nothing obliges them, multi-language and integrations to be toggleable add-ons per tenant.
No candidate requires newly built integrations to appear automatically as available add-ons inside the builder.
No candidate requires a review and publish gate as the last step before a tenant's builder configuration goes live.

22.10.23 allows the mobile home screen and navigation to be configured, but the home page composition - logo, banner and the four category tabs Tickets, What's On, Plan Your Visit and Map - is not obliged.
The matrix knows attractions, experiences, shops and dining as product families but does not require the guest app to present them as the six browsable explore categories.
1.4.7 requires products to be published to the Mobile App channel and 2.1.3 keeps the eligibility and pricing rules in the back office, so what the guest app offers is back-office driven.
adjudicator_note: Both ids are reused from adjacent candidate sets.

rationale: 1.1.105 requires stored value card management and 5.12.23 and 5.12.24 the load and usage accounting behind it, which is the money card in the guest profile.
The matrix stores every purchase and delivers tickets digitally, but a My Tickets view listing the guest's purchased tickets in the app is not obliged.
19.2.18 lets a guest change a visit date but no candidate requires a My Reservations view listing bookings, the tickets inside each and their details.
1.6.7 transfers ownership on a resale, but the alternative of renaming the ticket holder while ownership stays with the purchaser is not covered.
5.3.15 holds membership status, benefits and renewal history, but the guest app membership view with linked members and a digital membership card is not obliged.
19.2.55 requires an interactive venue map with attractions and shops plotted, but dining and restroom layers and tenant customisation of the map are not obliged.
No candidate requires image and format guidance for tenants uploading venue maps; the matrix has no asset-guidance requirement at all.
5.6.15 requires estimated waiting times to be continuously calculated and displayed and 5.6.7 requires real-time updates, which is the per-attraction wait time in the app.
5.6.30 exposes queue APIs to third-party systems but does not oblige an inbound interface for a client's camera or sensor platform to feed queue data in.
19.2.69 covers the guest raising a lost item request but omits back-office matching, marking an item found and tracking it through to guest collection.
22.7.4 requires reusable post-visit survey templates and 19.2.71 guest feedback management, which is the post-visit review and feedback survey.

2.6.33 requires prices to be displayed in a selected foreign currency while payment is taken in the base currency, and 2.7.35 calls this a courtesy conversion, which is the display-only mode described.
Dynamic currency conversion is obliged on the payment terminal but not at the online gateway with the booking record held in the venue's base currency.
adjudicator_note: 2.6.33 requires online payment to be taken in the base currency configured in the base system and gateway, which reads against charging the guest in their own currency at the gateway; worth resolving at sign-off.

rationale: 4.2.8 requires exchange rates to be updatable automatically on a configured frequency, which obliges a live external rate source rather than static master data.
4.2.8 allows manual rate maintenance but does not oblige a configurable margin applied above the market rate, which the client treats as a revenue line.
4.2.8 covers manual or automatic rate updates but not the two modes as a client-selectable choice, and the margin option is still missing.
adjudicator_note: Restates MOM-0218 and MOM-0219 together; the three could be consolidated at sign-off.

rationale: The POS may accept foreign currency and the website may display it, but parity of display and charge logic between POS and guest app is not obliged.
2.7.35 requires use of the base system currency for transactions and 2.6.33 requires payment against the base currency, which is the accounting record asked for.
The previously cut tail of 6.1.67 lists 'Foreign Currency Sales' among the Required Reports, which is the dedicated foreign-currency collections report asked for.
adjudicator_note: 6.1.67 was not in this row's candidate list; its full text appears in other rows of the same chunk.

rationale: No candidate requires a virtual waiting room that activates above a configurable concurrent-buyer threshold, which is the load-gating architecture for high-demand on-sales.
Tenant branding and estimated wait times exist in the matrix, but neither attaches to a waiting room, which the matrix does not have.
Resource attributes and time-slot availability are managed, but nothing obliges a resource booking to decrement a capacity-based inventory, which is what stops a cabana being sold twice.
No candidate requires a planned itinerary to be tied to the guest's ticket purchase and stored as a personal visit profile.
3.1.1 requires the dynamic QR code flow in which the ticket shows as a blurred, unusable code until activation, which is the temporary non-scannable code asked for.
adjudicator_note: 3.1.1 describes activation after registration; confirm at sign-off that the clarifying trigger is on-site location or system state as the minutes state.

rationale: 3.6.4 requires combo bundles, pre-configured or guest-assembled, which is the multi-component package sold together.
adjudicator_note: 3.6.4 is reused from an adjacent bundles candidate set; the discount element is inherent to a combo.

rationale: 5.6.36 requires wait times to be estimated from historical and real-time operational data but names neither a third-party queue API nor camera and people-counting sensors as the two supported sources.
The matrix requires white-label branding configuration but does not fix the boundary that the app's structure and layout are immutable and no new custom components may be added.
adjudicator_note: This row is a scope limit rather than a capability; it belongs in the solution description as much as the matrix.

rationale: Dated, timed and seated products are all sold but nothing obliges the checkout flow to reshape itself according to the configured product type.
Multi-tenancy and cross-channel synchronisation are obliged but nothing requires every channel of a tenant to share one database so a guest's login and session is continuous.
7.1.14 requires users, permissions, configuration and data to be isolated between tenants and 7.1.53 separate authorization policies per tenant, which is the independence asked for.
adjudicator_note: 7.1.14 is reused from an adjacent POS candidate set.

rationale: 22.10.23 allows mobile home screens to be configured but nothing obliges the Employee App to route a user straight to their role's home screen with no role-selection step after login.
18.2.1 gives the employee a work order inbox but no role-based dashboard aggregating task counts, work orders and inspections scoped to the user's access.
The matrix evaluates employee attributes when granting access but does not require the Employee App's entire navigation set, approvals and inventory included, to be filtered by the user's role.
Work orders, inspections, approvals, stock and attendance are each required, but the Task & Assets module and an Employee App venue map are not.
Several notification types are required but nothing obliges notifications to be categorised into those needing action and those that are informational.
8.4.39 requires semantic search over operational data generally but not a search across tasks and incidents inside the Employee App.
17.4.1 requires work order creation but not staff-logged tasks carrying a priority and a scheduled date and time.
Work order inbox, acceptance and rejection are obliged but the lifecycle states created, assigned, in progress, review and closed are never defined and the review stage has no counterpart.
Start and completion of a work order are captured but no resolution-duration timer or elapsed-time metric is obliged.
The matrix tracks stock levels across locations but does not require an Employee App item lookup by name or barcode scan showing availability across stores and warehouses.
Goods receipt is required, but the requisition, department-head approval, purchase order creation with vendor quotation comparison and issue to the requesting department are not in view.
15.1.28 requires minimum stock levels and 15.1.33 shortage alerts, but nothing obliges the breach to raise a draft requisition for review before it enters the purchasing workflow.

The matrix requires approval workflows for named action classes such as price overrides and configuration changes, but not one generic multi-step engine configurable against arbitrary actions such as new product creation.

The matrix requires approval workflows for price overrides and configuration changes but not this four-stage chain from IT/Operations through Operations Manager, Finance and CEO and back to IT for channel publication.
Approval workflows are required but the action set is never enumerated, so Return and Request More Information as distinct outcomes beside Approve and Reject are not obliged.
11.1.72 requires AI-generated approval recommendations, which is the AI summary shown beside the request on the approval screen.
The matrix versions workflow definitions but does not require the approval screen to display the trail of who approved at each stage.
11.1.4 routes approvals by role and hierarchy but nothing obliges the chain and its assignees to be configurable per workflow type down to venue-level managers and supervisors.
18.9.2 requires users to view assigned shifts and 18.9.1 to clock in and out, which is the roster and attendance surface asked for.
1.2.37 integrates approved leave into resourcing and 18.6.1 gives an approval inbox, but leave request submission from the Employee App is not obliged.
No candidate requires break windows to be logged so a replacement can be scheduled and a position is never left unstaffed.
Announcements and AI operational queries are required but not a resources surface giving staff their supervisors and venue information such as opening hours.
8.9.5 gives the command centre real-time visibility of incidents and disruptions, but live ride and attraction status in the Employee App is not obliged.
The matrix covers the guest side of lost and found only; staff logging a found item from the Employee App and surfacing it for claim is not obliged.
This is an open action item to confirm a venue-map guidance standard against a UX benchmark, not a requirement on the system.
Gates are configurable and device connectivity is monitored, but no venue-wide overview graphing attendance alongside each gate's open, closed, offline or maintenance state.
Gates, access points and locations must be configurable across multiple venues, but nothing obliges a visual map of them showing each venue's turnstile layout.
The gate, access-point and location model is required but no management view reporting how many physical gates sit at each location.

3.2.74 in full only names turnstiles and handhelds as selectable venue hardware and 2.1.18 monitors registered devices; neither obliges an inventory view in which each access device is added and assigned to a gate.
Turnstile integration and hardware selection are required, but not onboarding a device by choosing its integrated model and entering connection details such as an IP address.
16.4.19 requires device connectivity to be monitored, which is the real-time health view across the estate.

Access control device integration and passback detection are required, but nothing specifies a push interface over which devices send alarms such as power loss and network loss instead of being polled.
Device monitoring is required but not the onward surfacing of vendor-pushed fault events as operator alerts and reports.
Connectivity is monitored but no automatic notification reaches the operations team when a turnstile drops offline.
Many kinds of access rule are required but no dashboard listing them with their draft or active status.
3.2.7 requires configurable validity rules and entitlements changeable without development and 3.2.11 administrator configuration of all access rules.
3.2.70 requires multi-park entry rules with re-entry and crossover tracked separately, and 3.2.7 the configurable entry entitlements behind one-entry-per-day versus unlimited re-entry.
3.2.55 requires exits to be counted at the turnstiles and states that a scan can be required at exit, which is the configurable choice described.
The previously hidden tail of 3.2.73 requires the operator to change a turnstile between available modes including entry, exit and free rotation, which is exactly the configurable mode set asked for.
Passback attempts must be detected and a scanned code invalidated, but no configurable time window within which a second scan of the same ticket is refused.
The full entitlement list in 3.2.7 includes Required exit before re-entry as a configurable entry rule, alongside anti-pass-back, so the matrix already obliges the exit-before-re-entry option.
3.2.20 requires the ticket status to be updated to used once it is scanned at the access control device, which keys usage to the scan rather than to passage.
The complete scan history the investigation would rest on is required, but no candidate gives security a manual resolution path to re-admit a guest whose scan registered without passage.
1.1.80 requires date range validity on a ticket and 3.2.31 the access control check that enforces it.
Blackout dates are required for memberships and seasonal and event access policies exist, but no general blockout calendar excluding named ticket types on holidays and special event days.
1.1.62 requires entitlement consumption tracking and 3.2.60 the remaining count to be decremented and enforced at each control.
3.2.70 requires access rules covering multi-park access with crossover tracked separately, which is the crossover rule described.
3.2.70 explicitly covers whether a second park may be entered on the same day as the first entry.
Validity from first use and fixed validity periods are required, but nothing chooses between consecutive usage days from the first scan and flexible use within a longer window.
3.2.12 requires an adult ticket to be scanned as a pair with a child ticket to enable entry, which is the companion rule.
3.2.72 requires a group product configured for n admissions where one scan unlocks the device for that number of people.
3.2.72 has the group ticket scan incrementing against a configured admission count and 3.2.29 lets one QR admit multiple guests, which is rotating admission until the headcount is used.
3.1.2 requires a unique QR per issued ticket and 3.2.76 real-time validation of each at entry, so a group's members can be admitted independently.
3.3.25 requires simulation and testing of access policies prior to deployment, which is the virtual scan before publishing.
Dynamic QR credentials are required, but no per-event decision fixing whether that event is sold exclusively on dynamic QR or also on standard tickets.
Both credential styles exist in the matrix but nothing obliges them to coexist in a mixed configuration within one operation.
adjudicator_note: Restates the per-event mode gap raised on MOM-0327.

rationale: No candidate allows a named ticket type such as a VIP invitation or reseller ticket to opt out of dynamic QR inside an otherwise dynamic event.
Expired permissions are revoked automatically and a resold ticket's credential is invalidated, but nothing obliges the prior credential to die on a refund, exchange or reissue.

Barcode, QR, RFID and NFC media are enumerated and can be linked to an entitlement, but facial or biometric credentials are not listed as a media type and no board defines how each is associated with a ticket.
2.16.17 requires several media types to be linked to the same entitlement simultaneously, which allows either one media or several in parallel.
The system must validate several media types and can choose the most suitable one automatically, but no administrator setting fixes the verification method used for a given ticket at the gate.
Unique randomised access codes must be generated, but no issuance or encoding profile defines what information is embedded in the credential.
3.2.4 requires media to be swapped with the attached information transferred and 2.1.11 the kiosk to collect a ticket booked on any portal, which is the on-site conversion described.
Third-party scans are recorded uniformly and validity is checked at the gate, but nothing obliges tickets issued outside TICVAI by an approved partner to be imported and made valid.
adjudicator_note: Pairs with the pre-generated partner ticket batch raised on MOM-0652; both need the externally-issued ticket to exist in the access control system.

rationale: Hotel room card and property management system integration and identity verification are required, but no room-number lookup that issues a zero-value ticket or wristband to the hotel guest.
3.2.61 requires an interface to the hotel property management system for in-room billing, which is charging an on-site purchase to the room.
No candidate requires each supported media type to be proven working against each gate and device before go-live.
3.2.43 defines Face Pass enrolment through the app, ticket counters or annual pass counter with one facial profile per annual pass, which is the permanent membership credential.
3.2.44 defines Face Tag as temporary facial data deleted once the ticket is fully redeemed, which is the short-lived enrolment described.
A ticket or wearable may hold stored value and be spent contactlessly, but paying by presenting an enrolled face is not required anywhere.
Turnstile integration and hardware selection are required, but neither the connection details nor the light and sound feedback the turnstile gives are configurable.

3.2.74 names handheld devices as supported access hardware and 3.2.18 and 3.2.47 require reading foreign barcodes and phone tickets, but nothing configures a standalone handheld and the media it may read.

Offline validation and reconnection sync exist for the employee app and event check-in, but nothing obliges an access control device to queue scans while offline and reconcile them centrally when it reconnects.

The full 3.2.70 requires crossover entries to be tracked separately from entry and re-entry and 6.1.69 lists Entry by Ticket Type, but no admission-profile view splits entries into general, group, re-entry and crossover for group and B2B partners.
Entry reporting by ticket type exists but no attendance breakdown attributed back to the school or group booking that bought the tickets.

The untruncated 6.1.69 now obliges People Count, Ticket Count by Gate, Ticket Count by Site and Gate Utilization, but these are reports rather than a live dashboard pairing attendance per venue and gate with that gate's online or offline state.
The hidden tail of 3.2.73 requires an operator to change turnstile mode between entry, exit and the other modes during operation, which is the intra-day reconfiguration asked for.
3.1.6 requires a complete scan history with gate, location, timestamp, device, operator, validation result and entry attempts, which is the lookup view's content.
3.3.6 lets authorised users temporarily bypass restrictions and 3.2.73 gives the attendant podium control of the turnstile, which is the manual admission described.
3.3.6 requires full audit logging of every override and 3.1.6 the scan history against which it is recorded.
3.3.1 and 3.3.7 require permissions granted dynamically on attributes and context rather than fixed roles, which is attribute-based access control.
3.3.20 requires access restrictions based on occupancy levels, which is refusing an otherwise valid ticket while the venue is at its ceiling.
Suspicious QR usage patterns and duplicate use must be detected, but no assessment view presents the flagged tickets and threats for an operator to work through.
In-park attendance is calculated in real time and exits and crossover are counted, but no live per-venue monitoring view brings entry, exit and crossover activity together.
adjudicator_note: Overlaps the live operations dashboard gap raised on MOM-0367.

rationale: 2.16.17 links several media to one entitlement, 3.2.19 records the scan identically whatever the media, and 3.2.4 swaps media while carrying the attached information across.
adjudicator_note: The future credential types the source names, a hotel room key and a city transit card, are not enumerated as media anywhere in the candidates.

rationale: The matrix obliges configurable colour palettes, homepage layouts and a white-label portal but not packaged venue-type themes (stadium, theatre) with a live preview of the guest site.
2.6.1 in full specifies the B2C homepage and purchase flow but not selectable product card layouts of stacked, staggered and horizontal.
19.1.24 requires a self-service white-label configuration portal, with 19.1.4 and 19.1.5 obliging configurable colours and fonts from a menu of options.
21.5.18 obliges a seat view preview but not a 3D rendering of the actual view from the selected section.
1.4.24 in full generates a seat map from CAD files and drawings, but does not make an uploaded CAD file with defined sections the prerequisite for a 3D seat view.
21.2.1, 21.2.5 and 21.2.6 oblige importing and publishing a standard seating map from PDF, CSV or Excel, which is the easily configured 2D seat map.

The matrix obliges interactive maps, mobile food ordering and queue status in the mobile app but not their availability to a browser guest who has not installed the app, nor 3D venue maps, parking or directions.
16.1.1 and 16.2.7 oblige registration and inventory of devices, with 16.8.42 and the other 16.8 integration rows naming printers, scanners, handhelds and gate hardware.
16.1.1, 16.2.7 and 16.4.20 oblige registering, inventorying and monitoring devices centrally, which is add, update, activate/deactivate and monitor.
16.1.1 obliges device registration and 16.2.8 categorisation, which is the directory for adding and classifying devices; 15.1.37 covers serial-number tracking.
16.2.10 assigns devices to users and locations but the matrix does not model a workstation grouping several peripherals as the assignment target.
16.9.52 requires venue-specific device management and 16.2.11 device location records, which is provisioning a device for a venue or location.
Status monitoring and assignment are obliged separately but nothing requires a consolidated 360-degree device view presenting both.
16.2.10 obliges device assignment but not reassignment of a device to a different workstation when one fails.
Lifecycle and registration rows are obliged but deactivating a device with a logged reason is not.
16.1.1, 16.1.2 and 16.5.29 oblige registration, enrollment and lifecycle status tracking, which is this lifecycle view.
16.2.7 maintains device inventories and 16.5.29 lifecycle status, which obliges counts by assigned, under maintenance and in stock.
Inventory and assignment are obliged but not a breakdown of how many devices of a type are allocated to ticketing, retail or F&B versus held in store.
7.6.2 in full is serial-number management for rental items; purchase date, supplier and manufacturer remain unobliged fields on the device asset record.
16.2.9 maintains ownership records but the matrix does not oblige a responsibility field separate from ownership.
16.2.11 maintains device location records but the matrix does not oblige a visual map of each device's installation location.
16.3.15 requires reusable device configuration templates, which is the template library associating the correct drivers for a device type.
This is a documentation action item -- a request that the template's attribute list be written up and shared -- not a behaviour of the system.
16.3.14 requires remote configuration of devices, which is deploying a device type's configuration across workstations in one action.
16.3.16 maintains configuration versions and 16.3.17 supports rollback, which covers driver version tracking with comparison and rollback.
16.4.20 monitors device status and 16.9.53 provides device dashboards, which is the single-screen live online/offline view.
16.4.18 obliges device health monitoring but does not name the hardware metrics -- CPU and memory usage, storage, temperature -- the health view must show.
16.4.19 requires device connectivity monitoring, which covers network issues affecting readers and turnstiles.
16.4.21 obliges battery monitoring only 'where applicable' and does not require health metrics to be retrieved through the manufacturer's SDK rather than by physical inspection.
adjudicator_note: Open question in the source: dependent on the vendor SDK exposing the data; restates MOM-0446.

rationale: 16.4.22 obliges device performance monitoring but not the specific metrics of successful versus failed ticket validations and scan response time.
16.4.23 requires device alerts and 16.4.21 battery monitoring, which covers configurable alerting on low battery or a device going offline.
16.4.23 obliges device alerts but not escalation and notification management for alerts that go unresolved.
16.5.24 requires preventive maintenance schedules and 17.2.1/17.2.2 maintenance plans and scheduling, which covers quarterly, half-yearly and seasonal cycles.
17.2.5 requires maintenance calendars, which is the calendar of upcoming service needs.
16.5.26 requires device maintenance work orders and 17.4.1 work order creation, which is raising a work order from a logged fault.
Nothing obliges a device diagnostic workspace giving the assigned engineer a working view to investigate and resolve a fault.
16.5.28 tracks device warranties and 16.5.27 maintains maintenance history, which is exactly what this asks for.
16.5.25 obliges corrective maintenance tracking but not return-to-service on resolution or analytics on corrective actions over time.
16.6.30 requires firmware management, which obliges a library of available firmware versions per device.
Firmware and software update management are obliged but compatibility and update-policy rules restricting firmware to compatible models are not.
16.6.31 obliges remote firmware deployment but not a deployment wizard with phased rollout and scheduling.
16.6.31 obliges remote firmware deployment but not a live monitor of rollout progress flagging update failures such as an offline device.
16.6.34 obliges update rollback and 16.7.38 device audit logs, but an update history giving traceability of what was deployed, when and to which devices is not explicitly required.
16.7.38 and 16.7.39 require device audit logs and device access logs, which is this requirement.
16.9.54 requires device analytics and 16.2.7 device inventories, which obliges totals of active and inactive devices across venues.
16.9.51 requires tenant-specific device management and 16.9.52 venue-specific device management, which is managing devices across venues from one platform.
Device analytics and location records are obliged but not a location-wise operational breakdown within the analytics.
16.9.54 obliges device analytics but not availability, fault rate or a top-failure-reason breakdown such as communication timeout, power issue or firmware error.
17.2.7 requires maintenance SLA tracking, which covers configurable SLA tracking for devices under extended maintenance.
16.9.56 requires device management webhooks, which is the webhook and event notification to an external system this asks for.
11.1.7 makes approval workflows available for configuration changes but the matrix does not oblige an approval workflow for adding a device.
16.9.58 obliges device incident management but not automatic severity classification of an incident.
17.2.7 requires maintenance SLA tracking and 16.4.22 device performance monitoring, which is SLA and service performance tracking for devices.
16.9.60 obliges device management reporting but not AI-driven insights across the full device estate.
16.4.18 and 16.4.21 oblige health and battery monitoring but not retrieval of those metrics through the manufacturer's SDK in place of physical inspection.
adjudicator_note: Restates MOM-0414; score once in the traceability matrix.

rationale: The matrix assumes B2B sales exist and reports on them, but nothing obliges bookings transacted on a partner's own platform to be written back into TICVAI.
adjudicator_note: This is the API consumption model; the inbound booking interface is the architectural gap.

rationale: 2.7.49 requires commission rules to be stored per partner agreement and 2.7.55 requires commission to be reported per partner, which together require per-ticket commission calculation.
2.7.49 requires B2B partner agreements to store pricing rules, commercial terms and allowed products, which is the partner profile asked for.
adjudicator_note: 2.7.49 is reused from an adjacent B2B candidate set.

rationale: 2.7.49 requires credit limits, payment terms and settlement rules per partner and 5.7.65 requires advance payment accounting, covering the three settlement modes.
2.7.34 and 3.5.7 require a B2B portal with its own credentialled access and user hierarchy, which is the portal option described.
Commission rules and commission reporting are required per partner, but nothing obliges commission tracking to behave identically whether the sale came through the portal or the API.
No candidate requires bulk generation of a batch of tickets with a validity window exported as QR codes in a file for a partner to import and resell.
5.7.98 requires commission calculation, settlement and reporting generally, but nothing obliges the three B2B distribution models to share one downstream pricing, commission and reporting path.
The matrix requires a marketplace of modules with pricing and install/uninstall, but not that certified third-party ticketing integrations are catalogued and activated through it.
The matrix sells dated, non-dated and seated event tickets but does not establish Admission, Admission plus Dated, plus Timed and plus Seated as the core product progression.
The matrix manages event resources, templates and time slots but does not define an Event/Resource product category that may be dated, timed, seated or non-seated with an optional resource.
Nothing in the matrix collapses the event, seated and resource classifications into one product category; the matrix still treats resources as their own concern.
The matrix requires fixed and dynamic group ticket types and check-in entitlement control but omits shared versus individual QR issuance for a group and partial check-in tracking.

The matrix supports membership renew, upgrade and freeze through chat but does not define the Season Pass product as non-dated with start and end dates, mandatory profile capture, and cancel and extend workflows.
1.1.52 requires redeemable product entitlements but no gift voucher product with both value-based and product-based forms redeemable online and in-venue.
No candidate requires identity and entitlement to be modelled as separate entities; this is a core data-model decision the matrix does not oblige.
3.6.30 covers multi-park passes and annual passes as priced products, but tiered annual passes with configurable blackout dates are not obliged.
The matrix has QR credentials and multi-attraction reservations but does not require one code to carry conditional entitlements across attractions with usage counted per attraction.
2.16.17 requires multiple media types to be linked to the same guest account and entitlement simultaneously, which is the ticket-as-virtual-entitlement model.
adjudicator_note: 2.16.17 names QR, RFID, membership card and mobile wallet but not a bank card as a token medium; worth confirming at sign-off.

rationale: 2.16.17 requires several media per entitlement and 1.1.50 several entitlements per ticket, which is both directions of the many-to-many asked for.
12.1.25 requires access rights to be assigned by venue zone, which is exactly the venue and zone level grant rather than a universal key.
Add-on purchases and media swap are obliged but the post-entry choice between issuing a new code and extending the entitlement on the existing wristband or QR is not.
1.4.7 requires products to be publishable to Website, Mobile App, POS and other channels and 2.1.11 covers kiosk and POS collection, which is the channel set named.

2.1.3 requires all product eligibility and pricing rules for each sales channel to be held centrally in the system rather than in the external channels, which is the centralised per-channel price matrix.
adjudicator_note: 2.1.3 is reused from the adjacent price-publication candidate set.

rationale: 2.1.3 keeps per-channel pricing rules inside the system and 1.4.7 requires products to be published to selected sales channels, so a published price is what each channel sells at.
2.3.1 requires offline POS operation but nothing obliges inventory to be pre-allocated as a quota per offline-capable node, which is what prevents overselling while disconnected.
Offline mode with automatic upload and reconciliation on reconnection is obliged but reallocation of unused node quota back to the pool is not.
21.5.13 requires real-time seat availability but says nothing about network-based zoning where POS terminals on a shared network hold common seat state, which is the resilience architecture proposed.
No candidate requires a per-venue setting controlling whether offline zoning is applied automatically or enabled by the client.
21.1.2, 21.1.4 and 21.1.9 require section, seat and reusable venue template builders, which is the per-venue seat-map builder asked for.
The matrix requires manual builders and spreadsheet import but not AI-assisted layout generation from AutoCAD/DXF or OCR of PDF exports, nor any automation target.
adjudicator_note: The 90-95 per cent automation figure is an aspiration in the minutes, not a testable acceptance criterion; it should be restated before sign-off.

rationale: 21.2.6 requires seat map import from Excel but not the paired PDF seating diagram as a second input to the same import.
Events with seat maps and shared inventory are sold, but the modelling decision that an event is simply another product category rather than an entity of its own is not stated.
The matrix requires zone-based access rights but not that each product carries its own venue and zone permission configuration.
The matrix manages resource time slots and several queue types but does not require each internal experience at a venue to be its own product carrying its own capacity and access model.
Multi-tenancy and policies spanning venues and departments exist, but the six-level Tenant, Organization, Region, Branch, Venue, Department hierarchy is not defined anywhere.
7.1.14 requires users, permissions, configuration and data to be isolated between tenants, which is the separation asked for.
Venue-specific access policies are required and 7.1.52 allows policies to span departments, but department-level data isolation inside a venue is not obliged.
Policies and resources span venues, attractions and departments but organizations, geographical regions and branches are not managed levels within a single tenant.
Duplicate identification and active/inactive statuses are obliged but counts of active, inactive and duplicate profiles on a CRM dashboard are not.
22.2.20 requires guest lifetime value to be calculated and displayed from revenue, visits, memberships and loyalty engagement.
Guest profiles hold the histories and search exists across operational data, but a CRM guest directory searchable across customer profiles is not obliged as a surface.

Guests may be linked to corporate accounts, tour operators and travel agencies and segmented automatically, but segmentation by acquisition source across individual, corporate, group, travel agent and OTA is not obliged.
The untruncated 2.15.2 does capture both nationality and country of residence, but user-defined profile fields with per-field unique and required flags are still not obliged.
2.12.7 gives the required flag per field but no uniqueness constraint per field.
Group relationships and group leader management exist, but a group profile entity with its own name, description and contact person configured independently of the individual profile is not obliged.
2.12.7 explicitly allows mandatory guest parameters to be configured as either mobile number or email address, which is the one-of-two rule.
22.2.6 requires linking family members, dependants, guardians and spouses into household relationships while keeping individual profiles.
Family ticket products carry configurable composition and age rules, but nothing ties the CRM family unit to those product configurations so the two stay consistent.
The profile linking model exists for guests and corporate accounts, but its extension to operations-team entitlement relationships is not obliged.
adjudicator_note: The source states the intent in one line without defining what an operations-team entitlement relationship is; this needs sharpening before it can be tested.

rationale: 4.3.26 requires shared family wallets with rules on who may spend and redeem, which is exactly a parent top-up drawn down by a linked child credential.
20.1.1 requires self-service registration and 2.7.49 stores partner commercial terms, but capture of company address, trade licence and VAT certificate during onboarding is not obliged.
2.7.49 holds an approval status on the B2B partner agreement and 18.6.2 requires authorised users to approve or reject requests, which is the admin decision on a submitted corporate profile.
Operators may create customers and duplicates can be identified and merged, but nothing requires a guest-checkout purchase to create a profile automatically unless it matches an existing one.
22.2.8 requires duplicate guest records to be detected using configurable matching rules on email, phone and other identifiers, which is the matching described.
adjudicator_note: Fuzzy name similarity is not named in 22.2.8; confirm the configurable rule set includes approximate name matching.

rationale: 22.2.9 requires authorised users to review, merge and split duplicate guest records while preserving transaction history, which is the duplicate review and merge screen.
Merging is restricted to authorised users reviewing manually, but nothing prohibits an automatic merge or makes the customer's consent a precondition.
No candidate requires the customer to be notified by push or email when the system flags their profile as a likely duplicate.
Merging is required to be a deliberate action by an authorised user, but customer confirmation as the gate on the merge is not obliged.
adjudicator_note: Same contradiction as MOM-0540: 22.2.8 permits automatic merging.

rationale: Review and merge by an authorised user is required, but not a standing admin queue that tracks flagged duplicates regardless of whether the customer has replied.
22.13.11 requires campaigns, newsletters and surveys to validate guest consent before sending and 7.3.9 requires consent preferences to be stored per channel.
Consent withdrawal, deletion and anonymisation workflows exist, but a data-subject-request module handling access and correction requests as tracked cases is not obliged.
The Case Management & SLA subdomain gestures at request handling but no candidate requires a data-subject request to be tracked through submitted, in progress and completed.
adjudicator_note: The full text of 22.3.4 is a conditional-logic rule and 22.3.1 is a journey builder, neither matching their 'Case Management & SLA' subdomain; the 22.3 numbering may be misaligned and should be checked at sign-off.

rationale: 22.14.2 requires real-time dynamic segments that update on purchases and behaviour and 22.14.9 segmentation by spend level and order value, which is the rule-based segment builder.
The matrix obliges static segments and segment activation into reporting but not rule-based segment criteria such as purchase value bands, product-specific purchases or recency.
No candidate requires import of a static customer or segment list from CSV or Excel; the matrix's import rows are all seat maps and its customer-data rows are exports.
No candidate requires a Google Analytics integration feeding browsing, cart abandonment and checkout drop-off into the platform's own reporting.

Nothing obliges native capture of on-site behavioural events (browsing, cart abandonment, checkout drop-off) into the platform's own reporting store; the analytics rows assume the data is already there.
adjudicator_note: Implies an event-capture and retention design decision that should be settled before BI sign-off.

rationale: Abandoned cart journeys and dynamic segments exist, but behavioural events such as app session, campaign open and survey completion feeding segments straight into marketing automation are not obliged.
5.4.9 requires configurable tiers such as Bronze, Silver and Gold with spend-based progression and 5.4.7 loyalty points for configured transaction types, which is accrual by product and spend tier.
5.4.10 requires each loyalty tier to carry benefits such as discounts, multipliers and priority access, applied automatically.
A family wallet with a designated owner and linked accounts is obliged but modelling loyalty and wallet as customer-linked entities so both inherit family sharing is not.
22.1.19 obliges campaign attribution across revenue, 22.4.17 revenue attribution per campaign and 22.9.24 click and conversion reporting, which together require the same tracking.
Per-campaign configurable success criteria or target thresholds against which campaign performance is judged are required by no candidate.
22.3.1 requires the visual journey builder with events, conditions and actions and 22.3.6 requires abandoned-cart recovery triggering, which is exactly the touchpoint cited.
The matrix gestures at journey audience targeting only through AI recommendations and never obliges binding a journey to a selected segment or attaching an optional incentive such as a coupon code.
Nothing obliges eligibility filters (minimum cart value, product type) on abandoned-cart triggers, so the trigger would fire for every abandonment.
The three-level per-module permission model (edit and view, view-only, hidden) is not required anywhere in the candidates; only unrelated domain-specific role rows exist.
Nothing obliges hiding an entire module from a role that has no access; the module rows cover licensing lifecycle, not role-based visibility.
Screen-level visibility driven by role definition within an accessible module (officer versus admin) has no candidate requiring it.
The matrix requires role-based access only inside individual domains (sandbox, developer, AI) and never obliges a platform-wide RBAC configured per role and per module.
Role permissions exist for developers but nothing obliges sub-permissions inside a module so a role can reach Campaigns but not Journeys.
No candidate requires shipped default role templates that administrators can then customise.
22.8.2 requires a complete history of guest conversations across all channels in the CRM profile and 22.8.1 names WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook Messenger and web chat.
22.8.25 puts conversion rates and sales generated on the chat analytics dashboard, but attribution of those conversions to each conversation channel is not obliged.

Configurable SLAs and case categories and priorities exist, but the named conversation queues - reservation, general, membership and billing, technical support - and intent-based routing into them are not obliged.
22.3.1 requires cases to be created from website, mobile app, call centre, CRM and internal users, which is logging from both the guest side and the admin side.
22.3.2 requires configurable case categories and priorities and 22.3.6 escalation driven by priority and SLA breach, which is the case record and its escalation rules.
adjudicator_note: The channel on the case is implied by 22.3.1's origination list rather than stated as a stored field.

rationale: 22.3.13 requires automatic survey triggering on visits, purchases, support interactions and completed experiences by rule, which is the same configurable multi-point triggering.
22.6.14 requires badges, achievements and progress tracking in the app and 19.2.74 digital badges, which is the badge and status tier scheme described.
22.6.11 requires gamification activities to feed the loyalty engine with points, tier upgrades and benefits, which is exactly this row.
22.10.1 requires multiple websites, portals, app experiences and microsites to be managed from one centralised CMS, which is the multi-site and multi-venue administration asked for.
Seat maps exist as a capability but nothing requires the product page to choose between a seat map and a standard admission flow according to the product type.
Reusable venue and layout templates exist for seat maps, but not a library of CMS page components per venue type reusable by swapping imagery and data.
This is an open action to settle a layout decision and confirm it with the client, not a requirement on the system.
Interactive seat selection and legends are required, but colour-coding the map by price tier in the B2C booking flow is not obliged.
This is an action item assigning documentation of the RBAC matrix to a named owner, not a system behaviour to be tested.
22.3.16 automates case tasks and escalation workflows, but no candidate obliges a dashboard carrying total cases logged, cases now due and case load per agent.
adjudicator_note: The 22.3.x rows sit in a Case Management and SLA subdomain but several, including 22.3.9, are in full text marketing-automation requirements; the first pass cited 22.3.9 as case reporting.

rationale: Case escalation workflows are automated, but no candidate requires an SLA target to be defined and attached per case type.
22.2.17 requires the guest profile to display support tickets, escalations and resolution history and 5.3.34 requires cases to be linked to the profile, which is the agent's single customer view.
22.2.1 requires the consolidated guest profile to carry communications and support interactions across all channels and 2.12.32 the full activity audit history.
22.3.1 enumerates the originating channels a case may be created from, which is the logging source being captured.
22.3.2 requires configurable case categories and subcategories, which is exactly the classification asked for.
22.3.10 requires a complete case audit trail of assignments, status changes, escalations, communications, approvals and resolutions.
2.13.20 requires a staff-assist screen to create, change or resend tickets on behalf of guests linked to the CRM case ID, which is acting on bookings from the case.
22.3.16 automates compensation offers following complaints, but nothing lets an agent initiate a refund or goodwill payment from the case screen itself.
Department-based and configurable approval workflows exist, but no candidate lets an agent raise an approval request from a customer-service case and see it return to that case.

Employee push notifications and internal operational messaging are required, but nothing obliges a cross-department escalation raised on a case to surface on the receiving department's staff mobile app.
22.3.4 requires Resolved and Closed case statuses and 22.3.10 requires resolutions to be recorded in the case audit trail.
Missing an AI summariser that compiles the actions taken on a case into a review digest; 18.10.1 provides a generic employee AI assistant only.
22.8.25 obliges a chat analytics dashboard, but no supervisor-scoped view covering the contact centre as a whole across channels and case types.
Conversation volumes and agent performance analytics are required for chat, but no case-volume breakdown by category - general support, refund, ticketing, membership - with current status.
Automatic rule-based case and conversation routing is required, but the agent attributes the rules would route on - skill set, language, availability and current workload - are not obliged to exist.
22.3.3 allows manual as well as automatic assignment but does not require the proposed assignment to be previewed and overridable before it is confirmed.
Case escalation and recovery automation exist in the Case Management and SLA subdomain, but no configurable SLA policy is obliged to be defined per case type.
22.8.18 obliges agent assignment and workload balancing for chat queues and 22.8.6 an agent workspace, but no case workload view from which a supervisor reassigns cases to level the load.
22.3.6 requires automated and manual escalation workflows driven by SLA breaches and unresolved duration, which is further escalation and monitoring of unresolved cases.
22.8.25 requires resolution times and agent performance analytics for chat, but no quality-management scoring of an agent's outcome against the case SLA.
22.7.8 requires CSAT surveys and reporting for customer support interactions and 22.3.9 puts customer satisfaction metrics on the case dashboard.
Case volume and complaint trends are reported but no week-over-week period comparison is obliged.
A pending-approvals inbox is obliged, but a B2B overview listing every partner with status and documentation state is not.
Linking to corporate accounts, tour operators and travel agencies is obliged, but a partner profile with a configurable partner category and customisable fields is not.
A white-label B2B portal with master and sub-agent hierarchy and its security controls are obliged, but partner self-registration through review and approval is not.
Nothing obliges the back office showing the outstanding next steps on a partner application, since the application workflow itself is not required.
3.5.7 obliges a master and sub-agent user hierarchy with role controls on the B2B portal, which is multiple agents selling for one partner.
No candidate obliges territory or market distribution rights limiting the regions a partner may sell into.
2.7.49 stores allowed products and sales channels on a partner agreement but obliges no brand/venue association that scopes which venues a partner may sell.
Partner pricing rules and multi-venue tickets are required, but nothing obliges a multi-venue partner setup carrying distinct pricing per venue.

The matrix obliges a partner registration approval workflow and agreement document storage but not a compliance document repository (trade licence, VAT certificate) with review/accept/reject/resubmit states.
3.5.7 requires role controls in the B2B portal but stops short of action-level rights such as whether a partner may refund or reschedule.
Approval status is stored on the partner agreement but the four-state lifecycle lead/submitted/active/suspended is not enumerated.

The underlying partner data is required and a CRM 360 view exists for guests, but no consolidated partner 360 screen combining profile, contacts, rights, documents, access and approval status is obliged.
adjudicator_note: 2.13.43 'CRM 360 View' is a guest-side view; it should not be read as partner coverage at sign-off.

rationale: 2.7.32 obliges commission definition per B2B client, reseller or distribution channel, which is what a per-ticket OTA commission is.
Bulk B2B purchase is required but not the offline model of pre-generating a QR-coded ticket batch at agreed rates with a validity window and exporting it as CSV for a non-integrated partner.
Agreements and their approval status must be stored, but no overview listing all active and pending B2B agreements is required.
2.7.49 requires agreements to store contract dates and commercial terms, which is the term and value being asked for.
2.7.32 obliges per-partner discounts defined on selling targets and tiers, which is the tiered volume-band discount described.
2.7.32 requires the commission rate to be configurable per B2B client or reseller, which is the commission/margin configuration asked for.
Credit limits, balances and settlement terms must be held and alerted on, but no periodic monthly invoicing run against the approved ceiling with cheque or bank-transfer settlement is obliged.
2.7.8 requires real-time B2B top-up with automatic balance updates and 2.7.40 the display of balance and dues, which together are the prepaid draw-down model.
Quotas are stored on the agreement and stock reservation exists for retail inventory, but nothing obliges ticket inventory to be ring-fenced to a named partner.
2.7.38 requires entry of limits on quantity of tickets, transactions or amount per day/month for a B2B guest, which is the booking cap asked for.

A per-partner commercial dashboard is required, but no single overview screen presents partner profile, agreement and payment information together; 5.4.32's one-view obligation covers guest wallets, not partners.
2.7.55 obliges per-partner sales, revenue, refunds and credit metrics but omits order volume, reservations and tickets held on booking but not yet issued.
2.7.40 requires management of B2B order cancellation and refund and 2.7.55 requires refunds and cancellations to be reported per partner.
Payments due, balance and outstanding balances must be displayed, but no partner statement of account presenting opening balance, transaction activity and closing balance for a period is obliged.

5.7.90 requires reconciliation across bank statements and ticketing transactions with manual matching, exception handling and discrepancy reporting, which is the reconciliation and exception management asked for.
adjudicator_note: 5.7.90 sits in the F&B accounting subdomain; confirm at sign-off that it is read as covering B2B partner postings too.

rationale: No candidate obliges a partner dispute case workflow (raise, evidence, adjudicate, credit) reachable from the B2B operations view.
AI-generated dashboards are required in general but no AI partner-performance view surfacing trends, risks and opportunities across the partner base.
The matrix requires notification behaviours but never obliges them to be delivered by one centralised communications module that all other modules plug into.
adjudicator_note: Architectural decision minuted as confirmed; worth an explicit matrix row because per-module notification logic would still satisfy every candidate.

rationale: Sending over email, SMS and WhatsApp is required but no communications dashboard reporting delivered, pending and failed counts per channel.
Post-visit survey templates are required but nothing obliges trigger conditions keyed to a business event state such as the ticket actually having been scanned rather than merely purchased.
22.9.21 requires automatic fallback to an alternative channel when the preferred channel fails, which is exactly the routing and fallback rule.
22.9.8 obliges per-guest consent status and opt-in/opt-out preferences and 5.3.5 names newsletter opt-in on the profile.
Failed deliveries and retry attempts are monitored for API event delivery, but no delivery queue that automatically retries failed guest communications until they succeed.
AI-generated dashboards are obliged but not a scheduled AI-generated monthly marketing report built from communications data.
adjudicator_note: Minuted as a 'could be extended' note rather than an agreed commitment.

rationale: Nothing obliges a group-sales pipeline of inquiries, opportunities and confirmed bookings, nor a sales-team dashboard over it flagging items needing attention.
adjudicator_note: The inquiry and opportunity entities do not appear anywhere in the candidates; this is a data-model gap, not just a missing screen.

rationale: School and family/group sales are recognised, but no configurable customer-category taxonomy with school subcategories such as curriculum or nationality is obliged.
Group sales and real-time inventory exist, but no package builder that assembles admission, meals and workshops for a group against live resource availability.
No candidate obliges a quotation object at all, so nothing requires successive negotiated revisions to be kept as versions.
Configurable and versioned approval workflows exist generically, but no discount-threshold approval is obliged on a group quotation.
Nothing in the candidates requires an accepted quotation to convert into a confirmed booking, carrying its priced lines across.
Corporate, school and group selling are each required separately, but nothing obliges one shared inquiry to quotation to approval to booking flow across all three.
Tour and group reservations are required but no operations view listing the group arrivals expected for a given day or period.
Nothing obliges a group deposit to be tracked, let alone flagged as outstanding on the arrivals view.
Group reservations and qualification-checked resource assignment exist, but nothing obliges a named guide or educator to be assigned to a specific incoming group before arrival.
No candidate requires individual participant details to be captured against the members of a group booking.
2.8.8 requires staff to create a reservation without payment and issue a secure payment link that updates it, and 4.2.11 requires the emailed link to complete the purchase online.
Configurable timeouts are obliged on the cart reservation, but no configurable expiry is set on the payment link itself.
adjudicator_note: 4.2.11's phrase 'the validity of the feature should be configurable by sales channel' is ambiguous and may be intended as link validity; worth clarifying at sign-off.

rationale: 7.4.47 requires reserved inventory to be released automatically when payment is not completed within the configurable timeout, with expired and released statuses.
Turnstile scanning and check-in entitlement control are required, but no group check-in status held separately from the access-control scan for a dedicated group counter.
Unique, multi-use and dynamic QR codes are all required, but no single group code that admits a defined headcount is obliged.
Waiver templates and status validation are required but no dashboard showing which templates are published or draft and how completion stands across customers.
22.12.5 requires guardian authorisation and parental consent workflows for minors, which is the signatory rule being configured.
22.12.3 requires the system to determine automatically which waiver is needed from the purchased products and configured rules.
22.12.11 requires ticketing, POS, mobile app, check-in and access control to validate waiver status before participation and 22.12.12 to deny entry without one.
No candidate requires waiver template versions to be retained, so there is nothing obliging the system to show which version a guest actually signed.
adjudicator_note: Legally significant: without template versioning a signed waiver cannot be evidenced against the wording in force at the time.

rationale: Multiple waiver templates are required and approval workflows exist for pricing, but no approval, testing and publication gate is obliged before a waiver template goes live.
Waiver status is validated at the point of use and multi-channel sending exists, but no tracking dashboard showing completion per participant alongside the channel the waiver was sent on.
Expired waivers are identified automatically, but no staff verification workspace that checks completeness and signatory validity and flags missing or invalid waivers for action.
1.1.49 and 4.4.10 require product lifecycle management in the catalogue and 1.1.36 the Draft, Pending Approval, Approved and Published states that track setup through to publish.
The lifecycle states themselves are required but no dashboard presenting products grouped and counted by state.
