The state list is obliged but not a visual workflow rendering of it, and the source's 'scheduled' state does not appear among the matrix states.
adjudicator_note: Matrix state list (1.1.36) and the source's workflow differ: the source has Scheduled, the matrix has Suspended, Expired and Archived.

rationale: No candidate requires a product to carry an owning department or team, which approval routing and access would key on.
1.1.14 requires approval to publish a ticket onsite or online but stops short of per-channel publication controls on each product.
Published and Active states are required but nothing obliges a scheduler that starts and stops selling a product automatically at configured times.
6.1.65 requires every product master-data change to be logged with user and reason and to pass an approval process, and 1.4.9 requires version history of pricing and rules.
1.4.9 requires version history of all product configurations and 1.4.10 the restoration of a previous version, which is the rollback and recovery asked for.
1.4.16 requires affected tickets, reservations, memberships, events and integrations to be identified before a product change is applied.
adjudicator_note: 1.4.16 does not name promotions among the affected objects the source lists; a one-word addition would close it.

rationale: Impact is identified before a change is applied but nobody is obliged to be notified, so admin and customer-facing teams get no advance alert.
Effective from/to validity exists for pricing rules, but no product change can be staged to take effect only from a chosen future date.
Nothing requires already-sold tickets to be insulated from later product or price changes; the nearest row requires the opposite.
adjudicator_note: 1.4.4 directly contradicts this minuted decision - it requires product property changes to be propagated to already-sold tickets. One of the two must be corrected before sign-off.

rationale: This is an action item recording that Softlabs still owes a refinement of the workflow, not a behaviour the system must exhibit.
2.1.1 requires sales channels to be created with all required data, 2.1.2 their per-channel configuration, and 1.4.19 assignment by channel, location and venue.
1.4.19 requires products to be assignable to specific sales channels, which is the restrict-or-publish-everywhere control asked for.
8.5.10 requires channel-based pricing, which is exactly pricing online differently from onsite or counter.
Nothing obliges inventory to be either pooled across channels or split by percentage or quantity per channel, which is a capacity data-model decision.
No candidate requires automatic migration of unsold allocation between channels when one channel sells out.
adjudicator_note: Depends on the channel-allocation model gap raised on MOM-0735; minuted as a new request from the client rather than an existing expectation.

rationale: Channel-based pricing must exist but nothing obliges it to be configured through a single grid of guest variant against channel.
2.1.2 requires a sales schedule to be configured for each sales channel, which is start-sell and stop-sell timing per channel.
Per-channel eligibility rules and booking cut-off periods exist, but no minimum lead time that blocks same-day online purchase of a given experience.
A per-channel sales schedule is required but no cut-off expressed relative to a timed show's start, nor the rule that onsite selling otherwise runs to sell-out.
The resale marketplace and commission reporting are required, but no configurable commission rate is obliged to be set on a resale transaction.
1.6.2 requires configurable resale eligibility rules keyed on ticket status, usage status and business policies, which is what bars an expired ticket from being listed.
adjudicator_note: 1.6.2's rule dimensions do not name a minimum lead time before the validity date; worth adding that dimension explicitly.

rationale: Multi-venue selling is required but the booking site is not obliged to present a location selector for choosing among them.
An availability calendar and responsive booking flow are required, but not a horizontal near-term date strip with the full calendar as fallback.
Time-slot booking is required but not an inline add-on with a theme or cuisine sub-selection that narrows the slots offered.
Rescheduling a ticket under policy is required, but not conflict detection across a multi-ticket cart nor shifting the whole booking to a new date in one action.

1.2.10 covers checking a resource out to a guest for a rental period, 7.4.52 the deposit lifecycle for rented assets and 7.6.13 the rental reporting set, which together constitute the rental module described.
7.6.1 requires rental products to carry an Active/Inactive status and 15.1.8 requires those statuses to be managed, which is what the products screen lists.

The full 7.6.1 configures an Inventory Quantity per rental product and 7.6.2 a unique serial per item, but no candidate presents serialized and pooled as alternative tracking models a product is assigned to.
The full 7.6.1 configures a Product Category on each rental product and 15.1.6 supports variants, but nothing requires the category view to count the variants beneath it.
7.6.2 provides serial-number tracking, but nothing makes the tracking model a per-product setting of serialized, pooled or a combination of the two.
adjudicator_note: Configuration face of MOM-0763; 7.6.2 was returned as a candidate on MOM-0815 rather than here.

rationale: The full 7.6.1 configures a Rental Location per product and multiple rental locations, but does not define that location as where an item may be picked up and where it may be returned.
Missing cross-location returns, where an item collected at one location is handed back at another; no candidate addresses the return location at all.
The previously cut part of 7.6.1 configures Minimum and Maximum Rental Duration per product, so only the fixed one- and two-hour duration blocks remain unrequired.
The full 7.6.6 makes ID Number a configurable mandatory capture field, but nothing covers holding a physical Emirates ID as collateral and returning it with the item, nor age restrictions.
Age-based eligibility rules exist for tickets and entitlements, but no candidate applies them to rental products.
7.6.6 requires customer information capture in the rental flow with configurable mandatory fields, which is this requirement.
adjudicator_note: The candidate text is truncated at configurable mandat...; confirm the field list is per product.

rationale: 1.4.6 requires an approval workflow before a product is published, which is a human gate rather than an automated completeness check of pricing, duration and inventory configuration.
The full 7.6.3 now covers out-of-service item management and maintenance blocking and 7.6.2 the per-item statuses, but no candidate rolls those counts into a per-product overview by status.
7.6.2 holds a per-unit status and 7.6.11 the maintenance history, but neither expresses condition as good, in repair or in maintenance on a serialized item search.
7.6.2 requires complete rental history per serial number and 7.6.11 maintenance history, but purchase or acquisition date for the unit is not held anywhere.
adjudicator_note: 7.6.2 was returned as a candidate on MOM-0815 rather than here.

rationale: The full 7.6.1 requires an Inventory Quantity to be configured per rental product, which is quantity-based stock, but no candidate states that pooled items carry no individual identity.
Maintenance periods can be scheduled, but no candidate requires a status change to carry a reason and an estimated return-to-service date.
7.6.3 maintains available inventory by location, but allocating a stock quantity to each pickup station is not obliged; 15.2.4 is warehouse bin management, not rental stations.
15.5.3 covers transfers between venues, but not movement of rental stock between pickup locations within one venue.
15.1.16 requires damaged inventory to be tracked and 7.6.9 requires return status of Returned Damaged, Lost or Maintenance Required with damage notes, which keeps recorded stock accurate.
adjudicator_note: Neither row names stolen as a status; confirm theft is handled as loss.

rationale: Missing an inventory intelligence and rebalancing view that surfaces availability and shortages station by station so stock can be moved before it runs out.
adjudicator_note: This is the decision surface that makes the transfers in MOM-0784 useful.

rationale: The full 7.6.7 requires the calendar view to display Available Inventory, Reserved Inventory and Maintenance Blocks, but not total, rented and returned counts per item and per location.
7.6.13 requires a Rental Revenue Report, but nothing places revenue alongside inventory status on the real-time availability view.
5.6.9 requires advance booking, same-day booking and booking cut-off periods for queues, but no minimum advance time and maximum advance window set per rental item.
Booking cut-offs and same-day booking exist as queue settings, but not as per-rental-item availability rules.
adjudicator_note: Same rule set as MOM-0789; one rental availability-rules row should carry both.

rationale: Opening and closing times exist for queues and access rules vary by operating hours, but no candidate sets operating hours per rental station or pickup point.

7.6.7 requires time-slot rental with an availability engine and 7.6.3 requires available inventory to be maintained by product, date, time slot and location, which is exactly rentable windows with per-slot inventory.
adjudicator_note: Both rows were returned as candidates on sibling rental rows rather than here; the candidates offered are generic time-slot rows.

rationale: 7.6.7 requires a calendar view over time-slot rentals and 1.2.28 resource time slots and availability, but neither obliges a per-item booking timeline running across the day.
adjudicator_note: The 7.6.7 calendar view text is truncated at Daily V...; confirm whether a per-item timeline is already in it.

rationale: Missing blockout dates that make a specific rental item unavailable on chosen days; the candidates are resource types and back-office login rows.
1.2.29 requires availability management with conflict detection and 7.6.3 requires overbooking to be prevented, which is the double-booking and overlapping-slot check.
Missing allocation of rental capacity by sales channel through inventory holds and buffers; the candidates only forecast by sales channel.
adjudicator_note: Channel-level holds decide who can sell the last unit; it is an inventory rule, not a report.

rationale: 5.5.21 releases unused entitlement reservations automatically, but no configurable rule returns unused channel-held rental capacity to general availability.
Attendance is forecast from historical and real-time booking trends, but no candidate visualises rental booking trends and projected demand for availability planning.
7.6.4 requires rental pricing models including flat rate, tiered, dynamic and peak/off-peak, which covers both fixed and dynamic pricing.
Missing a top-products-by-revenue ranking on the rental pricing screen; 7.6.13 lists a rental revenue report but no ranked view.
Rental pricing models and channel-based pricing both exist, but no candidate defines a pricing profile as a price valid over a date range optionally limited to named channels.
7.6.4 requires fixed duration bands of 30, 60, 90 and 120 minutes with tiered pricing, which is the duration-based tiering described.
adjudicator_note: 7.6.4 was returned as a candidate on MOM-0800 and MOM-0804 rather than here.

rationale: 7.6.4 requires peak and off-peak rental pricing and 8.8.11 covers peak, off-peak and weekend price variation, which is calendar-based dynamic pricing.
Demand-based and inventory-based pricing are required, but no candidate bounds the resulting price with configured minimum and maximum limits.
adjudicator_note: Price floors and ceilings are the guardrail on every dynamic pricing row in 8.5, not just this one.

rationale: 7.6.5 requires deposit collection as a fixed amount or a percentage, by card pre-authorisation, cash or wallet, which is this requirement.
1.2.9 requires collection and return of the deposit to be handled at check-in and check-out and 7.6.5 requires full refund processing, which is release on return.
7.6.5 requires partial refund and forfeiture of a deposit, which is deducting a damage charge and returning the balance.
7.6.10 requires automatic late fee calculation and grace period configuration, but not extension pricing for a guest who chooses to keep the item longer.
7.6.10 requires manager approval for fee waivers but does not allow the waiver to be full or partial, expressed as an amount or a percentage.
The full 7.6.6 specifies the customer-facing voucher booking flow, but no candidate requires staff at the rental station and the guest online to run the same underlying flow.
Missing the rental booking dashboard and its four counts - total reservations, upcoming rentals, online bookings awaiting collection, and items currently checked out.
adjudicator_note: Awaiting collection is a state no candidate recognises: booked and paid but not yet handed over.

rationale: The hidden tail of 7.6.6 requires Group Rental Support with demographics collected per participant, configurable participant forms and group reservations, and 7.6.8 assigns and links a serialised item at each check-out, which together is the linked group booking with per-member items.
adjudicator_note: The group waiver signed by all members, mentioned in the source evidence, is not covered by either row.

rationale: 7.6.6 in full covers group rental participant forms and demographics but no waiver, and 22.12.6 lets one person sign for many rather than requiring every member to sign.
Missing a pre-payment commercial summary of a rental booking listing every charge including the refundable deposit; 6.1.68 only reports deposits after the fact.

7.6.14 requires a full audit trail over booking creation, reservation changes, check-out, check-in, deposits and refunds, but no candidate presents it as a reservation timeline showing products, timings, amounts paid and deposit status.
adjudicator_note: 7.6.14 is not among this row's own candidates; its full text appears as a candidate on MOM-1247 in the same chunk.

rationale: Check-out and check-in of rental resources and their linkage to a guest are required, but no fulfilment screen counts bookings by in-progress and checked-out status.
7.6.8 validates the booking on arrival, but does not extend that check to payment status and inventory availability before the item is handed over.
Missing a pre-handover condition inspection checklist; 7.6.11 in full covers preventive, corrective and damage maintenance, not a per-rental serviceability check.
Safety inspections and safety documentation exist as a domain, but nothing requires a handover checklist covering the safety equipment that must accompany a rented item.
adjudicator_note: Issuing a helmet with a bicycle is a liability control; it should be an explicit matrix row rather than inherited from general safety inspections.

rationale: 7.6.8 requires the specific serial-numbered unit to be assigned and linked to the reservation at check-out, but manual selection from available units is not covered and 7.6.15 records QR/barcode equipment assignment as not currently in the solution.
adjudicator_note: 7.6.8 and 7.6.15 contradict each other on whether scan-based equipment assignment is in scope; resolve this at sign-off.

rationale: 15.1.9 tracks inventory levels in real time, but no candidate gives a live view of every item currently out on rental and how long it has been out.
Check-out and return times are captured, but no candidate presents booking time, handover time and expected return time together as a per-item timeline.
Missing in-rental extension requests and the extension pricing applied when a guest keeps an item longer than booked; 7.6.13's full report list only reports late fees after the fact.
7.6.8 links a scanned serial to the reservation at check-out and 7.6.2 can mark an item Damaged, but nothing replaces that link mid-rental with a substitute item.
Missing the fast-swap rule restarting the rental timer when a faulty item is returned within a short configured threshold.
Missing operator discretion to grant a no-charge time extension or buffer on one booking after a mid-rental equipment swap.
Missing rental incident logging that records a reported fault such as a brake malfunction against the booking on which it occurred.
7.6.10 requires automatic late fee calculation and overdue notifications and 7.6.13 an overdue rental report, which is flagging bookings past return and charging accordingly.
adjudicator_note: Both rows were returned as candidates on sibling rental rows rather than here.

rationale: Missing a grouped view of an active rental that spans several items, as opposed to one row per item.
adjudicator_note: Depends on the group booking construct missing at MOM-0815.

rationale: 7.6.13 includes a rental utilization report, but incident trends have no source because rental incidents are not captured at all.
7.6.9 requires the rented item to be scanned, the reservation retrieved and the return recorded, and 7.6.10 requires automatic late fee calculation, which is the return process described.
7.6.9 requires the return to capture condition status, damage notes and optional photos, which is the post-rental condition inspection described.
7.6.9 records damage notes and a Returned Damaged status on return and 7.6.11 routes it to damage repair, which is recording damage found on a returned item.
Missing partial return of a multi-item booking, where some items come back and the rest stay outstanding; 15.2.12 is warehouse partial picking, an unrelated sense of partial.
adjudicator_note: Depends on the group booking construct missing at MOM-0815.

rationale: Late fees, damage fees, deposits and deposit refunds are each processed or reported separately, but no candidate settles them into one final calculation before the deposit is released, for an individual or a group.
Missing a per-rental completion report closing the return process; the full 7.6.13 lists operational, financial and customer report suites but no closing document per rental.
17.2.1 requires preventive maintenance plans and 7.6.11 requires maintenance periods to be scheduled for rental items with preventive maintenance as a named type.
4.5.15 requires periodic inventory counts and 15.1.24 physical stock counts, which is the recurring count that surfaces a shortage against the recorded level.
adjudicator_note: 15.1.27 (stock variance reporting) supplies the shortage comparison; it was returned as a candidate on the cash-variance rows.

rationale: Work order creation and lifecycle management are required, but no candidate provides the maintenance calendar view or states that a task is assigned to a named department or person.
18.2.1 gives users a mobile inbox of work orders assigned to them and 18.2.2 lets them accept one, which is this requirement.
Missing capture of the cost and expense of each repair against the item repaired; 5.7.26 only establishes expense account types in the ledger.
adjudicator_note: Without per-repair cost there is no source for the lifecycle cost in MOM-0852 or the spend figures in MOM-0855.

rationale: Maintenance history is maintained, but no candidate accumulates cost over the year to give a lifecycle cost per rental item.
7.6.2 moves an item between Under Maintenance and Available and 7.6.11 blocks rental while under maintenance, so clearing maintenance returns it to the bookable pool.
15.1.21 requires inventory write-off management, which is retiring an item that is no longer viable and booking its write-off value.
adjudicator_note: 15.1.21 does not say the write-off value is recorded; confirm the financial amount is captured, not only the status.

rationale: 17.7.1 requires maintenance dashboards, but not the three specific figures asked for - assets predicted to be at risk, upcoming maintenance cost and total maintenance spend.
adjudicator_note: At-risk assets implies a predictive model; upcoming and total cost depend on the per-repair cost missing at MOM-0851.

rationale: 7.6.13 lists rental utilization and revenue reports, but no candidate consolidates them into a rental command center, and on-time return rate, damage rate and maintenance trends are not defined as metrics anywhere.
adjudicator_note: On-time return rate and damage rate need definitions (numerator, denominator, grace treatment) before they can be built or signed off.

rationale: 8.9.10 obliges operational dashboards and drill-down analytics generally but not rental per-product performance, inventory utilization or equipment performance views.
8.9.10 obliges dashboards and historical performance analysis but not rental duration/extension analytics or damage, loss and deposit summaries.
8.2.42 obliges capacity forecasting dashboards, but neither it nor 8.9.10 requires rental channel and location performance reporting.

7.6.15 in full lists AI utilisation reports and maintenance scheduling only as recommendations not currently covered; no row bounds AI in the rental module to reporting and maintenance recommendations.
19.2.55 obliges an interactive venue map for guests but not the representation of rental booths/stations on an operational live venue map, nor a booth/station configuration capability feeding it.
adjudicator_note: Raised in the source as an open question about whether a booth/station configuration module exists.

rationale: 7.6.1 in full configures a Rental Location attribute and multiple rental locations, but does not model a booth or station as an entity distinct from the retail and F&B outlet configuration.
8.7.28 obliges data drill-down but the matrix does not require the itemized dashboard component set (chart type library, drill-down tool, heat map) TICVAI documented.
adjudicator_note: 21.5.24's heat map is a seat-selection heat map, unrelated to the dashboard component library.

rationale: Missing the POS sign-in detail of offering a short swipeable row of recently used cashier tiles instead of the full cashier list; no candidate addresses the login screen.
5.8.3 requires counting and saving each denomination separately, but nothing requires a note or coin image beside each denomination to speed entry.
5.8.3 requires each denomination count to be entered and saved but does not specify direct numeric entry as an alternative to repeated increment taps.
Missing an automatic hardware readiness check at shift start covering printer, cash drawer and terminal connectivity; 2.13.8 only says a drawer can be connected.
adjudicator_note: Device Management has device status monitoring rows that were not offered here; the shift-start checklist is still unspecified.

rationale: Missing the POS home screen's required content - terminal or gate identity, logged-in cashier, shift start time and denomination summary; no candidate describes the POS landing screen.
Missing the remaining POS home screen elements - hardware status, notifications, profile and a global search bar; 22.10.23 configures guest mobile app home screens, not the POS.

Scanning a sale and connecting a cash drawer are required in isolation, but no candidate obliges the quick-action set on the POS - scan by QR or RFID, recall a held sale, open drawer, reprint and void.
adjudicator_note: Recall of a held sale in particular is not covered by any candidate.

rationale: 2.13.21 requires all PLUs, ticketing and non-ticketing, to be sellable on the POS, but not a module menu presenting ticketing, F&B and retail as navigable sections.
Transaction history exists as a matrix line but only as a heading; nothing requires it to open full screen to cope with hundreds of transactions a day.
adjudicator_note: 1.1.112 is a bare heading with no shall statement behind it.

rationale: 7.3.2 gives search and filtering in the management back office, but no candidate requires the POS transaction history itself to be filterable by date and time, product and customer name or contact.
adjudicator_note: This is the customer-service lookup path at the counter, distinct from back-office search.

rationale: Unified guest search by name, email and phone is required, but nothing places it inline on the cart screen or obliges linking or creating a profile without leaving the cart.
Missing the interaction rule that the background dims when a side panel or modal opens; no candidate addresses POS visual behaviour.

Missing the workflow constraint that every discount and promotion is applied on the cart screen and none on the payment screen; the candidates configure promo codes without saying where they are applied.
adjudicator_note: Agreed by all present in the minute, so it should be a firm matrix row rather than a design note.

rationale: Missing capture of the end user's own details, such as name and date of birth, on a ticket or membership bought on their behalf; 5.3.4 defines guest uniqueness on the profile, not the ticket.
adjudicator_note: Collecting a child's date of birth on a ticket has consent and minor-data implications worth raising.

rationale: Missing the separation of the purchasing party recorded on the sale from the person the ticket is for; the candidates only require that a sale is recorded at the register.
Multi-tender and split checks are required, but no candidate governs how a split is initiated, so the no-enable-step interaction is not obliged.
Missing order-type selection - dine-in, takeaway or delivery - on the F&B POS flow; 5.12.106 is accounting type selection and shares only the word selection.
adjudicator_note: Order type drives tax, service charge and fulfilment routing, so it is more than a screen option.

rationale: 4.6.35 requires end-to-end order status including Ready and Collected and 4.7.5 requires buzzers, but no candidate requires a guest-facing order-status board driven by the kitchen display.
adjudicator_note: The minute also rules out taking a name or phone number, which no candidate addresses.

rationale: Special-request notes and table assignment are required, but party size, seating-area preference and the reservation deposit option are not obliged by any candidate.
Missing colour-coded table status - vacant, occupied, reserved - and filtering of the table view by that status; the candidates are account search and unrelated pass management rows.
4.9.6 allows a restaurant floor plan to be created and edited, but says nothing about rendering it to scale with real table shapes across several dining halls.
Order and modifier data reaches the kitchen display and order statuses exist, but nothing requires kitchen or cashier status updates to flow back and drive the guest-facing board.
adjudicator_note: 4.6.35 was returned as a candidate on MOM-0897 rather than here.

rationale: 2.12.18 requires refunds to the original payment mode or as wallet credit and 4.6.10 refunds across multiple tenders, which covers original tender or store credit at POS.
adjudicator_note: Both rows were returned as candidates on MOM-2326 rather than here; store credit is termed wallet credit in 2.12.18.

rationale: 5.7.91 requires the refund lifecycle to track reason, approver, method, status and timestamps, which obliges a reason on every refund.
5.7.91 tracks a refund reason but does not add a free-text note beside the preset codes for documenting edge cases such as refunding an already-validated ticket.
18.1.4 requires data to synchronise when connectivity is restored and 2.3.1 requires POS offline mode, which together oblige automatic catch-up without a manual sync.

The full 2.3.1 requires the functionality lost in offline mode to be defined and offline transactions to be reconciled on reconnection, but not that the cashier's transaction view narrows to locally completed transactions while offline.
Missing a POS-side reports view summarising sales and revenue by ticketing, F&B, retail and other categories; the candidates are forecasting and seat-section reporting rows.
adjudicator_note: Central sales reporting in 8.7 exists; whether the counter needs its own view is the open question.

rationale: Missing a terminal health view on the POS; every candidate here is about restricting permissions by POS terminal, which shares the words but not the meaning.
adjudicator_note: 16.4.20 (device status monitoring) covers central device health but was not offered; a POS-local view is still unspecified.

rationale: Missing an outlet performance view on the POS showing that outlet's sales, tax and average values; 2.7.55 is a B2B partner dashboard, a different audience and scope.
Missing an attraction-utilization view surfaced at the POS; the candidates cover access validation and membership sales, not utilization reporting.
Missing a notifications panel on the POS; the candidates concern menu management and guest consent preferences.
Missing a peripheral and hardware test screen that validates the attached devices before the shift begins.
Missing deployment information at the terminal - software version, installed build and sync status; the candidates are POS permission rows.
adjudicator_note: Device Management (domain 16) may own version and build tracking centrally; the POS-side display is still unspecified.

rationale: Configurable and attribute-based permissions exist generally, but no candidate makes visibility of POS revenue and sales reporting a per-role switch a client can turn on or off.
Access to financial data can be restricted by permission and by venue or terminal, but nothing narrows a cashier's reporting to the rows they personally billed.
adjudicator_note: Filtering by the acting user is row-level security, a different mechanism from the object-level restrictions in 7.1.31.

rationale: The full 7.1.12 requires configurable roles including Venue Manager and 7.1.36 attribute-based scoping, but no candidate grants an outlet manager reporting visibility for their own outlet from the POS.
A till variance alert and configurable supervisor approval on session close are required, but neither obliges a reason code from a defined list plus a comment before the shift may close.
Approvals can be routed on value and risk, but no candidate routes a flagged cash variance to a supervisor or provides PIN-based approval at the terminal.
adjudicator_note: PIN approval at the POS is a different authentication path from the MFA-protected approvals in 11.1.60.

rationale: Missing the rejection loop on a cash variance - recheck, resolve, resubmit - and the rule that the shift stays open until the variance is approved.
The minute records this as an open question about what should happen when no supervisor is available, with no decision taken.
adjudicator_note: Needs deciding: blocking a cashier indefinitely is not viable, so a logged-and-deferred fallback will probably become a real requirement.

rationale: 5.9.2 requires a blind cashier close-out with over-shorts captured, which is precisely withholding the expected total from the cashier while finance retains it.
adjudicator_note: 5.9.6 requires an alert when expected and counted values differ; if that alert reaches the cashier it defeats the blind close in 5.9.2. Flag the conflict at sign-off.

rationale: 20.3.2 covers licensing by POS quantity, but licensing counted per access-control point is not among the licensing models offered.
Missing module-based licensing that charges separately for optional modules such as B2C, B2B and the mobile app; the candidates price by user, POS or venue only.
adjudicator_note: Domain 20.3 may hold a module-based model that the lexical search did not return; verify before logging.

rationale: 20.3.1 licenses on a Venue Size Index but never defines its inputs; the four factors named here - POS and access-point counts, annual visitor volume, and required integrations and modules - are unspecified.
The Venue Size Index exists as a licensing basis but no candidate defines the small, medium, enterprise and enterprise-plus bands it resolves to.
20.3.5 requires licensing based on transaction volumes, which is the per-ticket fee model offered as an alternative to an upfront licence.
adjudicator_note: 20.3.5 says transaction volume rather than per-ticket; confirm a per-ticket unit is intended.

rationale: Missing a two-sided charging model in which a tenant pays a subscriber licence while the B2C guest is separately charged a platform fee at checkout.
adjudicator_note: Recorded in the minute as market context from India rather than an agreed decision; confirm whether it is in scope at all.

rationale: 23.1.1 requires a centralized repository for images, videos, documents and marketing materials across channels, which is exactly this requirement.
23.1.8 requires historical versions with comparison, rollback and restoration, which is version control over assets.
23.1.9 requires configurable approval workflows for asset publication, which is the publish approval asked for.
23.1.11 tracks licensing terms and expiration dates and 23.1.3 carries an expiry-date metadata field, which is asset expiry management.
23.1.12 tracks where assets are used but the matrix does not oblige AI-generated replacement recommendations with their downstream impact.
23.1.14 obliges asset usage analytics but not an overview dashboard totalling assets by type (images, videos, documents, brand assets).
23.1.2 requires configurable folders and collections, which obliges browsing assets organized into folders and subfolders.
23.1.2's collections and categories oblige logical groupings of assets over the same underlying files.
23.1.3 requires configurable metadata including campaign, which links each asset to its campaign or category.
23.1.2 requires configurable tags and classifications and 23.1.5 searching by tags, categories and filters, which is the tagging-for-search this asks for.
23.1.5 requires searching assets using keywords, metadata, tags, categories and filters, which covers search by name, description or tag.
The matrix obliges the underlying metadata, rights and version records but not a consolidated 360 asset detail view.
23.1.14 obliges usage analytics but not an activity view tracking additions, updates, missing metadata and duplicates.
23.1.8 obliges historical versions but not a persistent digital asset ID that survives version changes.
23.1.7 obliges AI tagging and classification but not AI identification of duplicate assets.
23.1.6 requires AI semantic search using natural language queries, which is finding an image by its visual content rather than filename or tags.
23.1.13 obliges distribution of approved assets to channels but not automatic generation of per-channel renditions in the required sizes and formats.
23.1.7 requires AI to automatically generate tags, keywords and classifications for uploaded assets.
adjudicator_note: The confidence score attached to each proposed tag is not named in 23.1.7.

rationale: 23.1.6 obliges natural-language semantic search but not image-to-image visual similarity search against stored assets.
The matrix obliges AI classification of uploads but not duplicate/near-duplicate detection flagged for a keep, replace or discard review.
23.1.8 obliges version history but not a digital asset ID that persists across version increments.
adjudicator_note: Restates MOM-0958; treat as one requirement in the traceability matrix.

rationale: 23.1.12 tracks where assets are used but the matrix does not oblige a replacement-impact analysis shown before a version change is confirmed.
23.1.13 obliges distribution to channels but not per-channel rendition-processing status showing ready versus missing.
23.1.7 obliges AI tagging but not AI quality checks flagging low resolution, missing information, unsupported renditions or inconsistent formatting with recommended fixes.
23.1.9, 23.1.11 and 23.1.3 together oblige approval status, ownership, licensing terms and usage-rights metadata per asset, which is what this governance capability asks for.
23.1.9 obliges approval workflows but not a governance overview counting assets pending approval against those already approved.
23.1.3 and 23.1.11 oblige an owner metadata field and ownership tracking but not the four distinct roles of business owner, content owner, rights owner and approver.
The matrix records licensing terms and usage rights but does not oblige controls defining and enforcing where and how an asset may legally be used per channel.
23.1.9 requires configurable approval workflows for asset publication, which defines who must sign off before publishing.
The matrix obliges approval workflows and distribution of approved assets but not a combined publication-eligibility check over approval status, rights and channel permissions.
23.1.10 obliges secure sharing and 23.1.9 approvals but not role-based permissions over discover, preview, download, edit, approve, share and manage actions.
23.1.11 tracks expiration dates and 23.1.12 usage locations but nothing obliges flagging assets whose rights are expiring together with where they are in use.
23.1.11 tracks ownership and licensing but the matrix does not oblige an audit trail of ownership, rights and permission changes with who changed an expiry and when.
The inputs are obliged but not a consolidated governance/risk view using AI to surface upcoming issues and recommend action.
23.1.13 obliges distribution of approved assets to channels and 23.1.12 tracking where assets are used, which is this distribution board's substance.
23.1.13 obliges channel distribution but not configuration of how much of an asset and which rendition each channel consumes.
Nothing obliges scheduled automatic replacement and propagation of outdated or expired assets across all live locations.
23.1.14 obliges distribution and performance analytics but not delivery monitoring of availability errors and broken references.
10.2.7's game reader and 10.2.13's tap-before-play validation oblige exactly this reader-per-game tap model.
10.2.1 obliges pay-as-you-go from digital wallet credits for games and 10.2.7 prices defined per game.
10.2.11 and 10.2.12 oblige tickets giving free play on specific games, with other games left to wallet payment.
10.2.8 obliges a ticket to play all games/rides and 10.2.11 unlimited free play, which is the unlimited-play entitlement.
10.2.12 obliges limited counted free plays on specific games and 10.2.7 packages of specific games with entitlement validity.
The full candidate text covers free tickets and entitlement-granted free play but not a game configured as fully free requiring no payment or entitlement at all.
10.2.19 requires reader themes controlled from the back office and 10.2.7 prices defined per game and shown at the reader.
8.9.4 displays operational status of attractions and rides but the matrix obliges no gaming configuration view listing every game and ride with active/offline status.
10.2.6 in full defines reader types linked to attraction types such as video games, skill games and rides, but that is reader configuration, not a game directory categorising games by type.
8.9.4 displays a maintenance state and 10.2.7 in full covers game pricing and packages; nothing lets an operator control a game availability or place it in maintenance for a defined period.
10.2.6 makes the credit type accepted at a reader configurable and 4.3.5 defines cash, bonus and redemption credit types.
4.3.5 makes wallet credit usage criteria configurable and 10.2.7 requires bonus deduction first, which is the configurable consumption priority.
10.2.6 links attraction to reader and 10.2.7 gives the reader access to a particular game, which is the game-to-reader mapping.
10.2.7 requires creating packages with specific games and defining entitlement validity, which is package entitlement configuration per game.
7.1.29 monitors configuration changes and 11.1.36 approves them, but no row obliges a dependency log linking related gaming configuration changes.
10.2.6 obliges configurable reader properties including credit acceptance and 10.2.18 the retap delay, which is this reader configuration board's substance.
10.2.18 requires a configurable delay between taps precisely to stop a card being charged again immediately.
16.2.7 and 16.9.53 oblige a device inventory and device dashboards but not a reader-specific management dashboard and directory.
10.2.6 obliges configurable readers with an attraction linked to each, and 16.2.10 device assignment, which is reader setup and reader-to-attraction assignment.
adjudicator_note: The source makes this conditional on the vendor SDK being integrated; the matrix states no such dependency.

rationale: 10.2.20 requires a reader for the customer to check balance, which is the balance-check tap this asks for.
4.3.5 obliges paid, bonus and redemption credit types with configurable rules and 10.2.5 free game/ride credits, which is the financial side of gaming this board manages.
4.3.5 in full names cash, bonus, redemption-ticket and rides credit as wallet types, but no row requires a per-customer profile view presenting paid, bonus, free-game and redemption credit together.
10.2.22 requires a configurable bonus granted on a top-up amount, which is the bonus-on-top-up threshold rule.
10.2.22 makes bonus usable only for games/rides and not F&B or retail, configurably, and 4.3.5 supports credit usage criteria.
4.3.5 in full makes only the usage criteria between credit types configurable; validity and expiry specifically for bonus credit is not obliged.
10.2.5 requires adding free game and ride credits to the guest wallet and 10.2.11/10.2.12 free-play entitlements, which is free-game credit management.
5.3.17 obliges wallet balances with top-ups and refunds and 4.3.35 audit of adjustments and reversals.
4.3.5 in full supports bonus credit as a wallet type but no row lets an authorized supervisor grant a discretionary bonus by card tap.
4.3.35 requires complete audit logs for wallet top-ups, payments, refunds, transfers, adjustments and reversals, which is the transaction ledger.
10.2.13 requires real-time validation of card balance, bonus and entitlements before the game starts, which is this tap-time check.
10.2.8, 10.2.11 and 10.2.12 oblige all-game, unlimited-specific-game and limited-count entitlement types configurable per product.
10.2.21 sets expiry from last recharge or activity and 2.14.11 membership validity rules, but nothing obliges card activation rules defining validity from first top-up or a fixed activation date.
10.2.17 requires normal and VIP prices per game shown on the reader, which is pricing differentiated by customer profile.
10.2.15 requires peak/non-peak game pricing based on specific date and time, which covers date-range rates.
10.2.15 requires peak/non-peak pricing for games and rides by date and time, which is weekday/weekend and time-of-day pricing.
10.2.15 obliges date and time based game pricing but not exception rules excluding a price on specific dates such as New Year's Eve.
10.2.16 requires a retry prompt after play that deducts a lower price than the original, which is this discounted retry offer.
10.2.4 obliges redemption-ticket credits usable for prizes but the matrix does not define points earned from gameplay based on score or level achieved.
10.2.7 in full requires prices to be defined for each game, which is the cost side, but not how many redemption points a game grants.
10.2.21 tracks card expiry from last recharge and activity and 1.1.105 stored value card management, which is card and wallet lifecycle tracking.
10.2.21 requires card expiry based on last activity or last recharge, which is the rolling-expiry option, alongside a fixed date.
10.2.21 covers last-activity tracking for expiry but the matrix does not oblige card replacement, blocking or suspension.
10.2.13 in full is device-side tap validation; the command-centre rows oblige real-time sales monitoring but not taps, rejected plays, wallet value consumed or per-game play counts.
16.4.20 monitors device status, covering reader status, but nothing obliges tap-validation logs recording which card was used on which reader and when.
No candidate in full requires the reason a tap failed, such as no entitlement or insufficient balance, to be logged for analytics.
1.1.62 requires entitlement consumption tracking and 5.5.20 real-time consumption tracking across modules, which is the entitlement-consumption monitor.
16.4.19 monitors connectivity and 2.3.1 offline mode, but nothing obliges an offline synchronization and queue monitor for gaming readers.
8.9.10 obliges alerts within the operations dashboard but not operational alerts arising from live gameplay monitoring.
8.9.10 obliges historical operational performance analysis but not gaming aggregates of total games played, unique players and paid versus value-credit usage.
16.8.47 and 16.3.13 oblige NFC reader integration and device configuration management but not reader protocol configuration including lighting and display behaviour exposed via the SDK.
No candidate row specifies the platform's user authentication mechanism; JWT-based authentication within the multi-tenancy design is unaddressed.
adjudicator_note: 16.7.35 is device authentication, a different subject.

rationale: 2.6.20 mentions single sign-on registration on the guest website but the matrix does not oblige a policy-based SSO system for platform users.
adjudicator_note: 2.6.20 scores high only on the shared term; it is guest-facing, not administrative SSO.

rationale: 7.1.12 requires configurable role-based access control grouping permissions into roles assigned to users.
Audit trails are obliged in several domains but no row sets the seven-year retention period the source requires.
adjudicator_note: Retention period drives storage and archival architecture; fix the number at sign-off.

rationale: 5.6.x obliges an on-site virtual queue and 2.13.31 queue management integration, but nothing obliges a built-in web traffic queue in place of a third-party tool.
adjudicator_note: 2.13.31 frames queue management as an integration, which sits against the source's decision to build it in; confirm at sign-off.

rationale: Nothing obliges back-office throttling of traffic entering the site.
8.9.6 monitors infrastructure health but no row obliges server-load monitoring through external infrastructure tooling such as Terraform.
7.1.12 in full names a Venue Manager role in the RBAC list but no row requires monitoring dashboards to be scoped by tenancy so that manager sees only their own venue traffic.
The matrix's virtual queue is an on-site guest queue; nothing obliges a web waiting room that preserves a guest's connection under peak load.
5.6.7 and 19.2.37 oblige estimated wait times for the on-site virtual queue, not for a web load queue.
Nothing obliges releasing queued guests into the site in controlled batches sized to available load capacity.
6.1.4 requires order confirmations to be emailed and 2.6.3 e-ticket purchase confirmation templates, which is confirmation and ticket delivery on a completed transaction.
Nothing obliges liveliness checks and observability enabling a standby system to take over on component failure.

2.6.65 in full does set an availability target and backup and disaster recovery under Non-Functional Requirements, but it is 99.9% scoped to the consent solution, not a platform-wide 99.99% target with performance and load testing.
adjudicator_note: Contradiction worth raising at sign-off: the only availability figure in the matrix is 99.9%, while the source aligns on 99.99%.

rationale: 3.1.5 requires access devices to validate codes with secure offline cryptographic validation without continuous connectivity, and 2.13.38 offline access validation.
3.1.9 in full is BLE and geofence activation of guest credentials; optional BLE verification that the scanning staff member is physically at the gate is not obliged.
3.1.3 obliges periodic QR refresh but neither the 15-30 second interval nor its configurability is required.
adjudicator_note: 3.1.3's example is 30-60 seconds against the source's 15-30 seconds; reconcile the interval at sign-off.

rationale: 3.1.5 and 2.13.38 oblige offline validation of the ticket credential on the scanning device.
adjudicator_note: Restates MOM-1094 from the POS device's side.

rationale: 18.1.4 obliges synchronization once connectivity is restored and 2.3.1 offline POS operation, but no row requires validation results to be persisted in a local device database while offline.
18.1.4 obliges sync when connectivity returns but not batched replay in the sequential order the events occurred.
Nothing obliges each synced record to carry both its original recorded time and its sync time.
2.3.1 obliges offline POS operation but nothing requires product configuration, pricing and rules to be held locally on the device for performance.
adjudicator_note: Left open in the source; decide in the HLD.

rationale: 10.1.2 syncs recipes in real time or at intervals but no row obliges POS configuration to sync to the local device in real time whenever it changes.
2.3.1 obliges automatic switching to offline mode but not defaulting to an online catalogue with automatic fallback to the last-synced copy.
Nothing obliges retaining only an encrypted masked card representation such as the last four digits.
adjudicator_note: Card-data retention is a security and compliance obligation; confirm against PCI scope at sign-off.

rationale: Nothing obliges limiting the stored masked card value to identification of which card was used.
adjudicator_note: Qualifier on MOM-1123; score with it.

rationale: 2.3.1 in full requires automatic upload and reconciliation on reconnect but not a local device database, sequential sync ordering or dual recorded and synced timestamps.
2.3.1 requires the ability to switch automatically to offline mode on server outage or network loss, without cashier intervention.
2.3.1 obliges offline POS mode and 18.1.4 synchronization when connectivity is restored, which is automatic restoration and sync of pending transactions.
2.3.1 in full requires functionality lost offline to be defined but not a visible offline mode indicator or greyed-out unavailable functions in the UI.
This defers a design decision to a later UI/UX session; it states no testable system behaviour.
2.1.15 alerts when a machine stops working but the matrix does not oblige a POS alert when a whole venue goes offline.
2.1.4 requires full integration of sales channels with capacity information available to all operators in real time, which is central inventory for capacity-managed products.
2.3.1 in full allows only configured product types to be sold offline, but does not require an offline sale of a capacity-based product to be blocked with a clear notification.
10.1.3 syncs recipe orders into inventory but nothing obliges F&B stock depletion to be computed at day's end from recipe usage rather than in real time.
adjudicator_note: 15.1.9 requires real-time inventory tracking, which conflicts with the source's end-of-day F&B depletion; the F&B/retail split needs confirming.

rationale: 15.1.9 requires inventory levels to be tracked in real time, which is what retail stock control across store and warehouse asks for.
No candidate row obliges consistent localization of the website, the POS interface (including Arabic-only product names and menus) and the mobile app.
Multi-tenant support is obliged for seat and API access but no row requires platform dashboards and observability with tenant-level visibility for venue managers.
adjudicator_note: Restates MOM-1069 at platform level.

rationale: This is a process commitment to choose a recommended observability platform during HLD/LLD, not a system behaviour to test.
This is a commitment to share a screen inventory document, an extraction artefact of the meeting rather than a system requirement.
The matrix obliges white-label configuration for guest-facing apps but does not establish that the POS/tablet application is excluded from white-labelling and carries TICVAI's own branding.
19.1.24 requires a self-service white-label configuration portal, which obliges the B2C and B2B apps to be white-label by design.
Configurable headers, footers and colour palettes are obliged but calendar customisation per client is not.
Time-slot reservations and seat assignment are obliged as features but the matrix does not establish three ticket types with distinct purchase flows.
Quantity restrictions are obliged but the admission purchase flow's step sequence, starting at a quantity selector, is not.
Seat assignment and real-time availability are obliged but not the day-then-time-then-seat step order of the purchase flow.
This is guidance about how to treat a shared reference system during design, not a behaviour of the product.
Price records carry approval and activation states, but no pricing overview dashboard listing every pricing setup and its current status.
2.9.6 requires multiple price-list templates to be created and maintained and 2.9.17 prices to differ by sales channel and guest category, which is a price list per channel, segment or category.
2.9.8 requires prices to be regrouped by category such as full, reduced and complimentary and 2.9.6 several rate items within one list, which is the price-category and rate-type sub-grouping.
2.9.6 requires rate items with their associated amounts to be added, amended or disabled within a price list, which is the rate structure setting the amount.
2.9.6 requires items and their rates to be added to a price list, which is the association of categories, products and rates that apply together.
The matrix carries a bundles area but none of the candidates oblige a bundle price to be configured across multiple components and their add-ons.
2.9.17 obliges different prices by country and market but not a different settlement currency per market or venue.
Nothing obliges a precedence order among category-, item- and segment-level prices, which is what decides the amount actually charged when several could apply.
adjudicator_note: This, MOM-1185 and MOM-1188 are three facets of one missing pricing-precedence requirement and should resolve to a single matrix row.

rationale: 2.9.6 requires price-list templates to be copied as well as created, archived and amended, which is cloning an existing list and adjusting it.
Nothing requires a completeness check that confirms a pricing setup is valid and ready to go live.
Individual pricing rules such as minimum and maximum are required but no overview listing every rule with its status and any conflicts between them.
8.5.9 requires customer-segment pricing, which is the per-segment rule being described.
2.9.15 requires dedicated pricing structures for memberships and member-exclusive products and 4.1.23 the automatic application of member benefits.
2.9.17 requires pricing models based on nationality, residency, country and market, which is resident versus non-resident pricing.
8.5.10 requires channel-based pricing, so each of POS, B2C, kiosk and B2B can carry its own price.
Event-based pricing is required but not price variation by venue or by individual attraction.
Tiered volume discounts are obliged inside B2B commercial agreements but not as a general quantity-band rule that applies automatically as a sale's volume rises.
5.3.7 requires purchase history and ongoing orders to be held and accessible on the customer profile.
4.1.22 requires points to be earned through purchases and 5.3.16 the earned, redeemed and balance ledger behind redemption.
8.5.5 requires seasonal pricing, which is a different rate either side of a season boundary date.
Seasonal and event-based pricing are required, but no general effective-from date on a price change that binds every purchase made on or after it.
Missing the conflict-resolution rule for simultaneously applicable prices - a configurable hierarchy determining which rule supersedes another rather than an automatic lowest-price-wins default.
8.5.8 requires time-slot pricing, which is prices varying by show, session or slot.
1.3.1 requires performances to be created as events and 2.6.15 and 1.3.33 time slots to hang off those events and be bookable.
Nothing obliges pricing rules to carry a priority that decides which one wins within a single sale.
adjudicator_note: Restates the precedence gap already raised on MOM-1171 and MOM-1185.

rationale: 2.9.12 requires a product tax property selectable as tax exclusive, tax inclusive or tax exempt.
2.9.11 requires tax profiles to be held for different products, but nothing allows a tax to be attached once at category level and inherited.
2.10.1 requires a transaction fee applicable to orders taken over specific channels such as the call centre and to modifications and cancellations, which is the fee concept held apart from tax.
No candidate requires a delivery or shipping fee to be derived from the address entered at checkout.
Transaction-level fees are obliged and resale fees are configurable by product and ticket type, but no general fee that can be levied at item or ticket level on an ordinary sale.

The full 2.9.11 requires multiple tax rates, per-product tax profiles and rule-based automatic calculation, but stops short of compound tax-on-tax where one tax is levied on a base that already includes another.
2.9.11 obliges tax profiles to conform to local regulation, but nothing makes the tax base configurable by region between the full pre-discount price and the discounted price.
Missing a monetary precision and rounding rule, so currencies needing three decimal places are not protected from having the third decimal rounded away.
2.9.12 requires a product tax property of exclusive, inclusive or exempt, and the exempt option is exactly this requirement.
2.9.19 requires configurable approval workflows with audit trails over price creation, modification, activation and publication.
1.4.9 requires version history of all product configurations including pricing, which is the successive-version record of each increase or decrease.
2.9.9 requires bulk price changes across a whole category and global changes, which is the flat across-the-board adjustment asked for.
Nothing obliges new catalogue items and their prices to be loaded in bulk from a file.
1.4.9 requires the full version history and 1.4.10 the restoration of a previous product configuration, which is the rollback of a price update.
No candidate protects an already-sold ticket from a later price change, which is the guarantee the guest keeps the price and terms bought.
adjudicator_note: 1.4.4 requires product property changes to propagate to already-sold tickets, which is the opposite of this minuted confirmation; same conflict as MOM-0730.

rationale: 3.5.4 and 3.6.16 require buy-one-get-one and buy-x-get-x-free promotions, which is the quantity-based promotion asked for.

The full 2.9.6 allows several price types on a list, limits on a price and batch rate changes, but no tiered rule prices the second and subsequent children in one transaction differently from the first.
Early-bird pricing appears only as an AI recommendation; nothing obliges configurable phases each carrying their own discount level and inventory quota.
8.5.31 only requires AI early-bird pricing recommendations; with no phased early-bird construct obliged, nothing makes the price revert to full once the phases are exhausted.
8.5.4 and 8.5.12 require availability-based and inventory-based pricing, which is price moving as capacity is consumed.
adjudicator_note: Neither row names the configurable consumption thresholds the source describes (for example a step at 50% sold).

rationale: 8.5.40 requires AI-generated pricing recommendations from market trends and 8.2.56 forecasting dashboards to act on ahead of a demand shift.
adjudicator_note: External demand signals such as weather, which the source used as its example, are not named as forecast inputs.

rationale: 8.5.44 requires simulation of pricing scenarios before activation, which is the preview of impact before going live.
Upgrade transactions must be recorded and attributed to a sales channel, but no dashboard reports upgrade volume and upgrade revenue over a period.
Upgrades and their price differences are required, but nothing defines which source product may be upgraded to which target product.
No candidate contemplates a downgrade path, so neither the permission to downgrade nor the refund treatment it implies is required.
Upgrades before and after purchase are required and access control checks validity at the gate, but no validity and usage-status eligibility check gating the upgrade itself.
1.1.21 requires automatic calculation of the price difference on an upgrade and 2.14.12 the same for a move to a higher membership, which is crediting what was paid and charging the balance.
Upgrading before or after purchase is required but no configurable window limiting how long after use, or up to what cut-off in the day, an upgrade stays available.
2.11.6 requires the upgrade price difference to be calculated on a pro-rata basis and 2.14.12 the same for a membership plan change.
2.11.7 requires the person type on a ticket to be changed during an upgrade and 1.1.21 the difference to be calculated, which is the child-to-adult correction at the gate.

The full 2.14.12 requires plan-to-plan upgrades with configurable upgrade pricing, but no distinction between a direct single-path quick upgrade and a flexible upgrade where the guest picks among eligible targets.
19.2.16 and 19.2.25 require ticket and membership upgrades to be supported in the guest mobile app, so the guest need not come on site.
Group ticket products carry configurable sizes, pricing, quotas and approvals, but whether a group ticket may be upgraded at all is not one of the configurable settings.
Barcode, QR, RFID, NFC and wallet media are all required, but the media list is not a business-configurable abstraction and face recognition is not named among ticket media.
Unique ticket ID generation is required but its format is not configurable by prefix, suffix and length.
adjudicator_note: 3.2.5 requires the ID sequence to be randomised, which may constrain how far a configurable prefix/suffix/length format can go; worth reconciling at design.

rationale: 2.16.17 requires several media types to be linked simultaneously to the same guest account and entitlement, which gives the fallback behaviour described.
Issuance into Apple and Google Wallet after purchase is required, but no design controls over the pass template's background colour, header and footer.
The untruncated 6.1.68 requires Reservations by Date and a Booking Status Report, but these are reports rather than a day dashboard combining today's order count, confirmed guests and booking status.
2.12.1 requires the order to carry its named customer and each selected item, which is what the order detail shows.
2.9.4 requires a configurable holding time for capacity-based products, after which uncompleted purchases release the capacity.

5.5.25 maintains Active, Reserved, Consumed, Expired and Cancelled statuses for entitlements, but no booking-level lifecycle beginning at draft and running through reserved-awaiting-payment to completed.
Per-channel product, eligibility and pricing rules are required, but nothing governs which actions - create, upgrade, cancel - each channel is permitted to perform.

The full 7.3.6 requires B2B and B2C, individual and group and segment tags including Corporate Groups and School Groups, but nothing links a booking to that category so the category determines which extra fields are collected.
An order may hold mixed ticket, retail and F&B lines, but the line is not obliged to show the inventory hold or remaining availability behind it.
Missing a pre-finalisation completeness check that payment, customer details and capacity are all satisfied before an order is committed.
Automated reservation reminders and pre-arrival communications are required, but no staff-facing view listing bookings nearing expiry for follow-up.
2.6.41 requires rescheduling to obey the reschedule policy and 5.6.23 cancellation by guests or staff to obey policy, which is the policy check before the action proceeds.

The full 1.3.51 requires multiple partial payments against one invoice and 7.6.14 an audit trail of deposit transactions, but no single financial status is held on the booking distinguishing deposit required, part paid and fully paid.

The full 7.6.5 requires fixed and percentage-based deposits with capture, hold and release workflow and 1.3.51 partial payment with a pay-by date before the visit, but neither obliges a deposit-plus-balance schedule for bulk school or corporate bookings.
Marketing consents and opt-ins must be stored on the guest profile, but nothing obliges them to be presented and captured in the checkout flow.
22.2.4 requires the guest's preferred communication channels to be held and 22.9.8 lets the guest set them, which is the email-versus-phone preference.
22.13.17 requires consent reporting showing consent status, communication preferences and compliance metrics, which is the contactable list marketing needs.
1.6.2 requires configurable resale eligibility rules across ticket type, event, venue, status and business policy, which is what this board configures.
Nothing bounds the price a reseller may ask, so no floor or ceiling relative to the original price is required.
1.6.11 requires configurable marketplace commissions and resale fees by venue, event, product, channel or ticket type.
Automatic eligibility and capacity validation before resale confirmation is required, but no human approval step that can gate a listing.
Ownership transfer on a completed resale is required, but nothing obliges the proceeds to be settled back to the original seller, which is a payout flow the matrix never asks for.

1.6.8 requires the original credential to be invalidated and a new one issued to the buyer and the full 3.2.5 that ticket IDs are unique and randomized, but nothing obliges the virtual ticket ID itself to persist unchanged through a resale.
1.6.7 requires historical ownership records to be maintained on every resale transfer, which is the ownership change log.
Missing the guarantee that downstream reporting and finance continue to reference one stable ticket ID after a resale; 1.6.5 only synchronises resale inventory with ownership records.
Eligible holders must be able to create and manage listings through a configurable, white-labelled marketplace, but no allowed price range is enforced when the seller sets the price.
adjudicator_note: The missing price-range rule is the same gap raised on MOM-1258.

rationale: 1.6.6 requires buyers to browse, search, filter and purchase resale tickets and 1.6.8 a new credential to be issued to the new owner.
1.6.15 requires reporting of resale revenue and commissions, which is the market fee retained on each transaction.
Listing status is tracked through its lifecycle and resale reporting exists, but no dashboard presenting all listings split by active, sold, expired and pending.
Wallet credit types and their expiry are configurable, but a foundation screen defining which wallet types exist and how they are configured is not obliged.
Outstanding balance reporting exists for gift cards, but an operational dashboard giving an overview of all live wallet balances is not obliged.
Outstanding and unredeemed balance reporting is obliged, but total wallet value as a dashboard metric is not.
Redeemed value is reportable for gift cards, but total wallet spend is not obliged as a wallet dashboard metric.
No candidate obliges a total recharge or top-up activity metric on a wallet overview.
2.6.35 in full covers money-card load, top-up, unload and balance, but the accounting rule that loaded money sits as a liability until consumed is still absent.
5.12.24 obliges revenue recognition on money card usage and 5.7.3 the revenue account held per product, which is recognising the spend against that product.
Family and membership wallets are each obliged individually, but a configurable library in which the business defines new wallet types is not.
Nothing obliges classifying a wallet type into a category such as individual, corporate or member.
No candidate obliges configurable provisioning rules setting the event at which a wallet is created.
A primary account holder is obliged for family wallets only; a general wallet ownership and account association model is not defined.
4.3.26 obliges rules defining who may spend, top up, redeem, transfer and view balances on a shared wallet, which is the parent and child example.
Nothing obliges defining which currencies a given wallet supports.
Configurable top-up limits are obliged for automatic reload, but a maximum balance a wallet may hold is not.
4.6.11 obliges accepting foreign currency and 4.2.8 managed exchange rates, which is conversion and crediting in local currency.
4.3.5 obliges multiple credit types within a wallet including cash and bonus credit with configurable usage rules, and 4.3.22 gift card conversion.
Credit types and their usage rules are obliged, but classifying each as monetary spendable funds or a non-monetary entitlement is not.
Top-up, payment and refund actions are obliged as capabilities, but a feature profile enabling or disabling each action globally or per wallet type is not.
Usage criteria per credit type and membership benefit management are obliged, but marking granted benefit credit as spendable yet non-refundable and non-cashable is not.
No candidate obliges a wallet lifecycle status of active, suspended, blocked or closed; the lifecycle rows cover tickets, resources and devices.
The validity rows revealed in full (1.1.9, 1.1.78, 1.1.79) are ticket validity periods; nothing obliges every wallet to carry a validity period.
Nothing in the full candidate text obliges an automatic sweep of a residual wallet balance to a finance-designated account once validity lapses.
5.4.32 and 4.3.24 in full only display and store vouchers and credits; no row sets the scope of an expiry sweep across monetary balances, non-monetary credits and vouchers.
A wallet account is a searchable identifier, but issuing each wallet a unique wallet code in the way a ticket number is issued is not obliged.
2.1.21 obliges wallet operations linked to RFID, QR, wristband or membership card and 3.2.8 validation of those media types, which is the configurable media association.
Nothing obliges a review and publish step summarising a completed wallet-type configuration before it goes live.
Wallet top-ups appear on campaign dashboards, but an operational top-up dashboard covering both successful and failed top-ups is not obliged.
Cash, card and voucher payment data is captured for reconciliation, but a funding-by-source breakdown of wallet top-ups is not obliged.
Balance reporting by accounting period exists for gift cards, but day, month and year totals on a wallet top-up view are not obliged.
4.3.22 obliges wallet funding through cash, card, online payment, gift card conversion, manual adjustment or configured rules, which is the funding method configuration.
No candidate obliges role-based permissions over staff funding of a guest wallet.
adjudicator_note: Depends on the platform-wide RBAC model flagged missing at MOM-0576.

rationale: Payments are pushed to bulk reconciliation and top-ups update in real time, but nothing obliges a manual staff top-up reconciling against the finance ledger.
adjudicator_note: Recorded in the minutes as an open question for finance rather than a settled rule.

rationale: 5.12.101 obliges multi-level chart of accounts and 5.7.2 and 5.7.3 account storage for every revenue and payment type, which ties transactions to an account entry.
5.7.74 obliges balance sheet reporting within the accounting subdomain, which is the financial statement reporting asked for.
Outstanding balance and liability exposure reporting is obliged for gift cards only; wallet balances are not required to be reported as a customer liability.
4.3.30 obliges configurable wallet limits including daily top-up limit and single transaction limit, which is the minimum and maximum top-up configuration.
Nothing obliges restricting which funding payment methods are available on which channel, such as cash top-up on-site only.
4.3.28 in full is automatic top-up below a threshold with configurable limits, not an approval gate; supervisor approval is obliged only for cashier sessions.
Wallet refunds and full or partial order refunds are obliged, but reversing a wallet top-up back to the original tender is not specified.
Value-based approval routing exists in governance, but nothing obliges manual verification before a top-up reversal is processed.
4.3.30 obliges configurable maximum balance, daily spending, daily top-up, single transaction and user-specific limits, which is the velocity control asked for.
Wallet transaction history and credit reporting exist per wallet, but a funding audit trail queryable across accounts for a chosen period is not obliged.
Wallet funding by configured business rules and membership benefit management exist, but issuing a credit as a consequence of a purchase under wallet or credit-type rules is not obliged.
4.3.5 obliges configurable usage criteria per credit type and 10.2.22 a bonus usable only in one category and not in F&B or retail, which is this scoping.
4.3.19 obliges a first-expiry-first-out usage strategy on the credits in a guest's wallet.
Guests can view their credits, balances and expiry dates, but a per-transaction or per-lot expiry breakdown, and the rule that they cannot choose the lot, are not stated.
10.2.22 obliges a configurable top-up bonus such as 100 plus 25 and 4.3.5 bonus credit as a credit type, which is the tiered incentive.
4.3.5 obliges configurable rules defining the order in which credits in a wallet are used, which is bonus credit ahead of base credit.
4.3.6 obliges a configurable expiry period for every credit type stored in the wallet, so bonus credit can carry its own validity.
4.2.22 obliges mixed payment using any combination of wallet balances, cards and other tenders in one transaction, which is split tender.
4.3.23 in full obliges partial usage of a gift card balance but not the configurable alternative of requiring full redemption in a single transaction.
Credit reporting includes balances and expiry due dates, but a customer-level admin view for managing upcoming expiries and extensions is not obliged.
No candidate obliges a simulation or test mode for validating a wallet configuration with sample transactions before it is published.
4.3.38 obliges child cards drawing on the parent card's stored value and 4.3.26 the shared family wallet, which is exactly this funding model.
4.3.38 obliges parent-to-child store value distribution and 4.3.30 user-specific limits, which is a per-child cap on the family balance.
4.3.26 obliges rules on a shared family wallet defining who may top up, spend, redeem and view balances under a primary account holder.
Corporate account relationships are obliged, but a corporate wallet whose funds are segregated across departments is not.
4.3.23 obliges gift card balances in the wallet with activation, redemption and balance inquiry, which is the monetary gift card.
1.1.52 obliges redeemable product entitlement management and 19.2.39 voucher storage, which is a voucher redeemable only against a named product.
Gift card redemption is obliged but configuring whether it may be redeemed online, on-site or both is not.
Sales are reportable by attraction, F&B, retail or location, but wallet spend specifically by department, category and partner is not obliged.
The same sales reporting exists by outlet, but wallet spend broken down by sales channel such as B2C against POS is not obliged.
No candidate obliges a wallet payment policy setting rules such as a minimum spend before the wallet may be used as a tender.
2.1.21 obliges wallet operations linked to RFID, QR, wristband, membership card or guest profile and 3.2.4 swapping media, which is wallet-to-media association.
Credit expiry is configurable and a visual policy builder exists for access control, but a wallet risk policy bundling validity, expiry and refund rules is not obliged.
8.3.46 obliges risk scores assigned to transactions and 4.3.32 AI detection of suspicious wallet activity.
Detection of high-risk transactions is obliged, but routing them to an operations queue for manual cross-verification, rather than auto-approving or auto-declining, is not.
Liability reporting for gift cards and revenue recognition reports exist, but an on-demand finance view of total outstanding wallet liability against revenue recognised is not obliged.
This records that a flow diagram is still being revised and will be shared later; it states no system behaviour.
This is a planning commitment to produce wireframes for review, not a requirement on the system.
The matrix requires real-time monitoring of F&B sales and consolidated reporting across outlets but does not oblige a dedicated F&B Command Center surface.
4.5.25 requires consolidated reporting across outlets and 8.9.8 real-time monitoring of F&B sales, which together oblige total sales across outlets.
The matrix monitors F&B sales and transaction performance but does not oblige an order count as a reported measure.
The matrix obliges consolidated outlet reporting but does not name average order value as an F&B operational measure.
The matrix requires kitchen productivity analytics but does not oblige average preparation time as a reported measure.
The matrix requires kitchen productivity analytics but does not oblige a live kitchen load measure.
The matrix requires top-selling products in retail analytics but does not oblige top-selling items on the F&B command centre.
The matrix requires operational alerts in the operations command centre but not on the F&B command centre.
No matrix row obliges an outlet type taxonomy (fine dining, quick service, coffee) with features configurable per type.
adjudicator_note: All four lexical candidates are POS logon rows and are unrelated.

rationale: No matrix row obliges outlet type to drive feature availability, such as suppressing table booking for quick-service outlets and requiring a table layout for fine dining.
No matrix row obliges outlets to be linked to a main department, sub-department, cost centres and status - the organisational spine that the department breakdowns elsewhere depend on.
The matrix requires real-time inventory tracking but does not oblige recipe-based depletion to be configurable per outlet as real-time or end-of-day.
No matrix row obliges per-outlet operating hours and named service periods (breakfast, lunch, dinner, late night).
No matrix row obliges revenue analysis by service period or time slot.
The matrix requires each product to be tagged with a valid channel and segment but does not oblige items to be enabled or disabled per sales channel per outlet.
4.6.33 requires configurable kitchen routing to stations, printers and KDS screens, which is substantially this station-to-device mapping.
4.6.33 requires routing rules that direct items to stations and devices based on product, category and modifier, which is substantially this requirement.
The matrix covers refund approval workflows and configurable workflows generally but omits void approval and the amount thresholds and user privileges that trigger them.
