The matrix requires recipes linked to menu items but does not oblige a menu and product command centre tracking menu, recipe and product counts.
The matrix requires recipes linked to menu items but does not oblige exception flagging of products with no mapped recipe or unavailable ingredients.
No matrix row obliges a menu builder defining the POS front-end layout per outlet with categories and item tiles.
adjudicator_note: Candidates 21.3.x are seat-map layout rows from venue mapping and must not be traced to POS menu layout.

rationale: No matrix row obliges configurable POS button sizing for fast-selling items.
This records that the mock-up layout is indicative and the UI may change, which is a review note rather than a requirement.
The matrix requires an item master and unit-of-measure management but does not specify F&B product creation capturing pricing type, inventory-tracking toggle, recipe linkage and preparation time.
7.4.18 requires a product code to be auto-generated from a business rule, which is substantially the auto-generated PLU on product creation.
adjudicator_note: 7.4.18 names an 'AK code'; confirm at sign-off that this is the PLU the source means.

rationale: The matrix carries modifiers as a subdomain but does not oblige free versus chargeable modifiers or minimum and maximum selection rules.
The matrix supports combo products with component-level inventory but omits component selection with upgrade options at additional cost.
The matrix requires recipes with ingredients, quantities and automatic recipe costing but omits yield, selling price and margin on the recipe or BOM.
No matrix row obliges automatic substitution of an alternate ingredient when the primary is out of stock.
The matrix requires production sheets and batch production runs but not aggregation of recipe requirements to forecast prepared-item quantities.
The matrix supports configurable roles and device-based restrictions but does not oblige outlet-level scoping of a user's data visibility, which is an access-architecture decision.
This records two candidate implementation approaches still to be evaluated rather than a testable requirement.
adjudicator_note: Open design decision behind the outlet-scoping requirement (MOM-1396) - it should be resolved and then written as a requirement before sign-off.

rationale: Nothing covers extending administrative outlet or venue data scoping to ticketing and event-specific access; this is the same access-architecture gap as the F&B outlet restriction.
adjudicator_note: Candidates 3.3.18, 3.3.40 and 3.3.41 are guest admission access policies, not back-office data scoping - they must not be traced here.

rationale: The matrix requires kitchen productivity analytics but not a live kitchen command centre showing order counts, items pending or firing and station status.
No matrix row obliges course-wise ordering that groups items by course and controls when each course is fired.
No matrix row obliges a fired timer on a kitchen ticket measuring elapsed time since the order was sent.
With no kitchen ticket timer required anywhere, its reset on course completion has nothing to sit on.
The matrix allows a restaurant floor plan to be created and edited but does not oblige a live visual map showing table status across areas.
No matrix row obliges tables to be tagged with a customer category such as VIP to drive service priority.
The matrix supports advance table reservations but nowhere defines the table status flow Available, Ordered, Table Closed and Reserved.
This records a deliberate scope exclusion - no Cleaning table status - rather than behaviour the matrix could cover.
adjudicator_note: Worth carrying to sign-off as an agreed exclusion so it is not reintroduced.

rationale: The matrix supports table reservations but does not specify what a reservation captures or that the system recommends a table.
No matrix row obliges a reservation deposit that is adjusted against the final bill.
4.9.17 requires automated waitlist management with notification when tables become available, which is substantially walk-in and waitlist handling.
The matrix requires end-to-end order status tracking but not a per-table activity log of seated, drinks ordered, food ordered, sent to kitchen and course served.

The matrix carries a bare CRM 360 View row but does not oblige a single unified guest profile shared across ticketing, F&B and retail with duplicate avoidance - the cross-module identity model is left unspecified.
adjudicator_note: This is an architectural decision from the workshop; worth confirming which matrix row the client considers authoritative for the unified profile.

rationale: The matrix requires unified search by name, phone and other identifiers but not automatic matching of a guest to an existing profile by name and mobile across channels.
The matrix generates low-stock and out-of-stock alerts and records consumption but does not oblige a stock command centre showing stock value alongside recipe-based ingredient consumption.
The matrix tracks batches and compares theoretical to actual consumption but omits planned versus actual versus yield quantity and batch losses.
4.7.3 requires manual recording of F&B wastage and 4.6.31 mobile recording of waste and spoilage, which is substantially per-item wastage capture.
The matrix supports warehouse replenishment generally but does not oblige an outlet-raised requisition against the central warehouse.
The matrix requires consolidated and roll-up reporting across outlets but does not oblige food cost and gross margin in that roll-up.
The matrix obliges consolidated outlet reporting but not breakdowns by sales channel and by hour of actual F&B trading.
adjudicator_note: Candidates 8.2.25 and 8.2.13 forecast by sales channel - they do not cover actuals.

rationale: The matrix supports role-based permissions but does not oblige dashboards to be scoped by role so that an outlet manager sees only their own outlet.
The matrix requires inventory management and stock alerts but not a combined F&B and Retail inventory overview reporting total value, item counts and out-of-stock items.
The matrix supports item categorisation but does not oblige inventory figures to be broken down by department and sub-department.
15.1.1 requires a centralised item master, 15.1.2 item categorisation and 15.1.7 unit-of-measure management, which together cover these item master attributes.
The matrix requires unit-of-measure management but does not oblige pack-size conversion between units (carton to pieces, case to litres to millilitres).
4.5.35 requires FIFO, LIFO and weighted average costing methods, which covers the two methods the source mandates.
adjudicator_note: 4.5.35 also offers LIFO, which the source does not ask for - confirm whether LIFO stays in scope.

rationale: The matrix requires warehouse master, zones and locations but does not oblige a customisable multi-level warehouse hierarchy or direct receipt at an outlet or kitchen.
15.1.38 requires expiry date tracking and 15.1.35 batch tracking, which together give expiry maintained at batch and date level.
15.1.28 requires minimum stock levels and 15.1.33 stock shortage alerts, which is substantially notifying staff when stock reaches the minimum threshold.
This records a scope exclusion - not implementing every granular warehouse status - rather than behaviour the matrix could cover.
adjudicator_note: It directly contradicts matrix rows 15.2.10, 15.2.11, 15.2.12 and 15.2.13, which require picking lists, picking validation, partial picking and packing operations. Must be reconciled at sign-off.

rationale: This is a design principle recorded from the workshop, not a testable requirement.
15.3.2 requires supplier classification, which is substantially categorising suppliers as F&B, retail, engineering and so on.
The matrix requires a supplier master and supplier performance tracking but omits holding supplier compliance documents and linking item categories to a supplier.
15.3.5, 15.3.6 and 15.3.10 require purchase requisitions, procurement approvals and purchase orders, which is the requisition to approval to PO flow.
15.3.7 requires RFQs and 15.3.9 comparison of supplier quotations, which is substantially comparing prices from multiple suppliers before ordering.
15.3.10 requires purchase orders, which covers a regular PO with standard item, quantity and price entry.
The matrix supports contract purchasing but does not oblige contracted pricing to be fixed for a period and auto-applied to subsequent orders.
The matrix requires purchase orders but does not oblige a service PO covering non-inventory items and services such as equipment maintenance.
15.3.16 requires procurement spend analysis, which is substantially visibility of spend by category, supplier and contract.
This describes the purpose of the delivery tracking tool used to validate the build, not behaviour of the product the requirements matrix governs.
adjudicator_note: Extraction artefact from the project-governance part of the minutes.

rationale: This is an open action to finalise a design rather than a requirement in its own right.
adjudicator_note: Tracks the unresolved design behind the role-based dashboard requirement (MOM-1421).

rationale: Self-service white-label configuration and module enablement are required but B2B use of the same mobile application is not.
A scoping description of the reference application (three to four flows) with nothing testable in it.
19.2.10 requires the app to support ticket purchases, which is the admission ticket flow.
Mobile seat selection and assigned seating are required but the select-time-then-select-seat two-screen sequence is not.
An open question to be settled before wireframing, not system behaviour.
A process commitment to share the screen list ahead of a walkthrough.
A meeting-process invitation to flag frames or devices in advance.
A project-sequencing note about when wireframing starts.

The matrix requires real-time, historical, forecasting and embedded analytics but never states that the BI capability must be built natively into the platform rather than delivered by integrating a third-party tool.
adjudicator_note: Build-versus-integrate is the single largest architectural decision in this minute; it should be an explicit matrix row.

rationale: Missing the commercial constraint that reporting be delivered with no ongoing third-party BI subscription or licence cost falling to the client.
adjudicator_note: Commercial rationale behind MOM-1453; may belong in the contract rather than the matrix.

rationale: 8.7.23 asks for real-time analytics but fixes no refresh behaviour, so nothing obliges continuous refresh in place of a capped number of scheduled refreshes a day, and no testable latency target exists.
adjudicator_note: Refresh cadence drives the whole reporting data architecture (streaming versus batch); needs a stated target.

rationale: Missing a responsiveness requirement making every dashboard usable on a smartphone through a URL without a dedicated app or laptop.
adjudicator_note: Applies to all of 8.7; better stated once as a non-functional row than per dashboard.

rationale: The matrix enumerates the dashboards the system must provide - sales, ticketing, membership, loyalty and others in 8.7 - which is the out-of-the-box default set.

8.7.11 requires self-service reporting and 8.7.12 drag-and-drop report creation, but both stop at reports; composing and saving a whole custom dashboard, and the explicit no-SQL/no-code bar, are not obliged.
adjudicator_note: 8.7.11 and 8.7.12 were returned as candidates on sibling rows (MOM-1476, MOM-1481) rather than here; the lexical search offered only the pre-built dashboard rows.

rationale: 8.9.8 requires real-time monitoring of each sales stream separately; no candidate requires them consolidated into one facility-wide total revenue figure on the command center.
adjudicator_note: Consolidation across ticketing, F&B and retail into a single revenue number is a data-aggregation ask, not a layout one.

rationale: 8.9.2 requires the command center to display current attendance and occupancy across parks and venues, which is the facility-wide visitor total.
adjudicator_note: 8.9.2 was returned as a candidate on sibling row MOM-1471 rather than on this one.

rationale: 8.9.8 requires real-time monitoring of transaction performance per sales stream but not a single facility-wide transaction count on the overview.
8.9.2 requires the command center to display occupancy levels and capacity utilization across parks and venues, which is occupancy expressed against configured capacity.
Entries and exits are reported and multi-tenancy exists as a platform concept, but no candidate requires the live operations view to break sales, entries and exits down per tenant or venue.
adjudicator_note: Per-tenant segmentation of operational reporting is a data-partitioning and access question, not a layout one.

rationale: 8.9.4 shows open/closed/maintenance status for attractions, rides and facilities, but not a gate-level open/closed/offline tile for access control, and offline is a device-health state it does not name.
adjudicator_note: Matrix row 8.7.7 requires access control dashboards generically; the quick-glance gate tile on the command center still needs specifying.

rationale: 8.2.25 only forecasts revenue by sales channel; nothing requires actual revenue reported by sales channel as a command center section.
adjudicator_note: The high-scoring candidate is a forecasting row; forecast by channel is not actuals by channel.

rationale: 8.9.2 covers capacity utilization for attractions and venues, but not utilization measured per inventory item.
adjudicator_note: Capacity by inventory item requires the inventory master (15.1.1) to carry a capacity attribute.

rationale: 8.9.8 monitors sales by stream, but no candidate requires channel-wise performance broken down to top-selling products within each channel.
Missing a conversion-rate metric tracking web site visits through to completed purchase; 8.5.37 optimises conversion via AI pricing and 8.9.10 is generic dashboard provision.
adjudicator_note: Depends on the web analytics integration in MOM-1470.

rationale: Missing cart abandonment reporting; 8.6.23 tracks recommendation conversions, which is a different funnel.
Missing an external web-analytics integration (Google Analytics) as the source of conversion and abandonment data for the command center.
adjudicator_note: Third-party integration with its own data-sharing and consent implications; no candidate domain owns it.

rationale: The command center rows enumerate what it displays - attendance, queues, asset status, staffing - and customer, membership and loyalty information is not among them.
adjudicator_note: 8.9.8 (real-time monitoring of ticket and membership sales) was returned on sibling rows and covers sales, not guest or loyalty profile information.

rationale: Multi-site revenue reporting and historical performance analysis are required, but no candidate obliges a like-for-like comparison of sites across periods such as month-on-month or same period last year.
Missing AI-generated diagnostic insight that proposes reasons behind a movement in attendance or revenue; the command center candidates all describe descriptive monitoring only.
adjudicator_note: Any such insight would fall under the AI governance and explainability rules in 8.1; worth linking.

rationale: Self-service and drag-and-drop report creation are required, but nothing obliges the business to be able to assemble whole new role-oriented dashboards such as separate finance, sales and operations boards.
adjudicator_note: Same gap as MOM-1458; the candidates offered here were only the pre-built dashboard rows.

rationale: Missing role-based visibility at the level of an individual dashboard; the role-based candidates cover AI experiences, developer permissions and sandbox access, none of them reporting.
adjudicator_note: Who may see which figures is an access-architecture decision and gates sign-off on finance and HR dashboards.

rationale: 8.7.12 requires drag-and-drop report creation but names no predefined data sets - revenue, sales quantity, sales channel, department - for the designer to drag from.
Drag-and-drop creation is required, but no candidate obliges the user to pick a visual format such as bar or pie for a metric without writing a query.
adjudicator_note: The top-scoring candidates here (seat map builder, Chart of Accounts) are false lexical neighbours on the words chart and builder.

rationale: KPI monitoring and KPI alerts are required, but nothing lets the business configure the normal, warning and critical bands that decide when a metric is in breach.
adjudicator_note: Threshold bands are what turn 8.7.22 alerts from an idea into something testable.

rationale: Missing configurable date and dimension filters on a dashboard - by sales channel, department or period; the candidates are forecasting rows that merely share the phrase sales channel.
adjudicator_note: 8.9.10 requires drill-down analytics on the command center, but no row requires filter configuration on a designed dashboard.

rationale: Missing an approval gate between designing a dashboard and publishing it; the candidates are the pre-built dashboards themselves.
adjudicator_note: Could arguably fall under 11.1.36 (configuration change approval) if a dashboard counts as configuration; confirm at sign-off rather than assume.

rationale: Missing the itemised launch catalogue of the designer's building blocks - which chart types, table components and status/rule widgets exist; the matrix names self-service reporting without ever enumerating components.
adjudicator_note: Raised in the minute as an action item for a written scope document; without it the dashboard designer has no bounded acceptance criteria.

rationale: Missing configurable limits on pages and boards per dashboard to stop designer scope expanding without bound.
Drag-and-drop creation is required, but no candidate describes the composition model itself - configurable prebuilt blocks laid out on a bounded single-page canvas.
adjudicator_note: Same underlying scope question as MOM-1481; the component catalogue and the canvas model should be specified together.

rationale: Missing per-component responsive behaviour rules for the dashboard building blocks; the candidates concern report types, not component behaviour at different breakpoints.
adjudicator_note: Extracted from an action item to produce an itemised component list; the testable part is that each component has defined responsive rules.

rationale: 6.1.16 allows finance-defined reports to be configured, but no candidate obliges a shipped library of standard day-to-day operations and finance reports.
adjudicator_note: 6.1.16 defers the finance report formats to a future Ticketing-Finance model; that dependency is still open.

rationale: 8.7.18 and 8.7.19 require report export to Excel and to PDF respectively, which is exactly this requirement.
8.7.12 requires drag-and-drop report creation and 8.7.11 self-service reporting, which together oblige the no-SQL custom report builder described.
adjudicator_note: Neither row spells out choosing which data-set fields become columns and which become rows; a minor detail under a covered capability.

rationale: The untruncated 6.1.78 adds drill-down and drill-through capability to 8.7.28, but neither fixes the path from yearly sales through month, day and channel to an individual transaction, nor that the terminal level names the customer and the ticket.
Drill-down and drill-through are obliged, but nothing constrains them to data with a genuine hierarchical relationship or requires the tables to carry a hierarchy-linked structure.

Missing a performance requirement that the drill-down interface stays responsive on very large result sets such as ten thousand transactions in a single day; the full 6.1.78 sets retention but no volume or latency limits.
Missing the architectural rule that reporting, analytics and AI queries run only against a separate replica database and never against the live transactional database.
adjudicator_note: This is the load-bearing decision under the entire reporting module and appears nowhere in the matrix.

rationale: Missing the requirement that the reporting replica be synchronised by the cloud provider's managed replication service rather than by custom-built sync logic.
Missing the isolation guarantee that reporting workload never contends with live guest transactions for database resources.
adjudicator_note: Consequence of MOM-1491; add as an acceptance criterion on the same matrix row.

rationale: Missing the strict division of use between the live transactional database and the reporting replica for reporting, analytics and AI.
adjudicator_note: Restates MOM-1491 from the data-model side; one matrix row can carry both.

rationale: 8.7.23 asks for real-time analytics but sets no replication latency target, so nothing obliges the replica to be seconds behind the transactional database.
adjudicator_note: The minute leaves this pending confirmation with the infrastructure specialist; it is a number the matrix should carry once agreed.

rationale: Sales dashboards and real-time analytics are required, but no candidate rules out periodic or end-of-day refresh as the delivery mode for them.
adjudicator_note: Restates the refresh-cadence gap in MOM-1455 from the management-need side.

rationale: 8.7.30 requires natural language reporting and 8.4.2 natural language interaction, which is the conversational report request described.
8.7.30 natural language reporting together with 8.4.14 AI-powered report generation obliges the AI to turn a stated request into a report without manual configuration.
adjudicator_note: 8.4.14 was returned as a candidate on MOM-1502 rather than here.

rationale: Missing guardrails on the AI report agent requiring it to ask for a missing timeframe, venue or metric instead of guessing; no candidate constrains AI behaviour in reporting.
Missing the multi-turn clarification behaviour - the agent keeps asking follow-ups until it has enough to generate - as opposed to single-shot generation.
adjudicator_note: Same conversational-design gap as MOM-1499; one matrix row can carry both.

rationale: Missing the requirement that AI-assisted product or ticket creation confirm key attributes - admission versus time-slot versus seat assignment, categories, discounts - before writing the configuration.
adjudicator_note: Same clarification-before-acting rule as MOM-1499, applied to catalogue creation rather than reporting.

rationale: Missing a cost and quality constraint on AI report generation limiting repeated regeneration cycles that raise token spend and hallucination risk; 8.4.14 requires the capability without bounding it.
adjudicator_note: 13.1.14 (access token management) is a false lexical neighbour on the word token.

rationale: Report scheduling, subscriptions and sharing together oblige scheduled automatic distribution to defined recipients.
5.9.7 requires the shift/closing summary report and 8.7.15 with 8.7.16 require scheduling and subscriptions, which together deliver it to operations, finance and sales recipients each morning.

Configurable email templates exist for ticketing confirmations and report scheduling exists, but no candidate requires the scheduled report to go out on a configurable template with the report attached.
Sales dashboards are required and revenue by channel is forecast, but nothing obliges actual product and attraction performance reported by sales channel.
adjudicator_note: The high scorers here are forecasting rows again; forecast by channel is not performance by channel.

rationale: Discounts exist as a sales feature and sales dashboards are required, but no candidate requires discounts applied to be reported as a measure on the sales board.
adjudicator_note: The two top candidates are bare bullet headings reading Discounts, not requirements.

rationale: 4.4.30 requires AI-driven upsell and cross-sell recommendations to be made, but nothing requires their results - take-up and incremental revenue - to be reported on the sales board.
5.12.2 requires deferred revenue accounting, 5.12.120 recognition schedules and 5.12.64 deferred revenue reports, which is the deferred-versus-realized detail asked for.
adjudicator_note: The matrix places this under Revenue Recognition; the minute wants it surfaced on the sales board.

rationale: Benchmark reporting and sales dashboards are required, but no candidate lets a sales target be set and then reported against the forecast.
adjudicator_note: Target setting - who sets it, at what grain - is not owned by any candidate domain.

rationale: Missing revenue reported by department and by cost center; the candidates give revenue by seat section and staffing forecasts by department, neither of which is a finance cost-center view.
adjudicator_note: A cost-center dimension has to exist on transactions before this board can be built; it is a data-model addition, not a report.

rationale: 5.9.1 requires end-of-day shift closing and register close-out, but nothing requires shift-closing detail to appear as a section of the finance board.
6.1.33 requires full reconciliation reporting against the payment gateway including refunds, used value and liability, which is the reconciliation this board shows.
Missing any statement of which visualisation types a board uses; no candidate names bar, pie or any other chart form.
adjudicator_note: Same underlying gap as MOM-1477 and MOM-1481 - the matrix never enumerates chart types.

rationale: 3.2.66 requires the in-park report of entries against exits and 8.7.7 requires access control dashboards, which together make a tester check entries, exits and the resulting in-park attendance on a board.
adjudicator_note: Attendance is not defined as a metric distinct from entries minus exits; confirm the definition at sign-off.

rationale: Turnstiles are listed as a device type and check-in at them is required, but no candidate obliges reporting broken down per individual turnstile.
adjudicator_note: Per-turnstile attribution requires every scan event to carry a device identifier.

rationale: 8.9.2 requires capacity utilization to be displayed on the operations command center, but the operations board's own composition is not specified anywhere.
adjudicator_note: 8.9.2 was returned as a candidate on sibling rows rather than here; the metric is obliged, its placement is not.

rationale: Visit history is required to exist and to survive portfolio merges, and is used as a campaign input, but no candidate requires it to be presented as membership and loyalty visit history on a CRM board.
adjudicator_note: 8.7.8 and 8.7.9 require membership and loyalty dashboards generically; neither specifies visit history as content.

rationale: Missing retention, visit-frequency and churn intelligence that detects a lapsing pass holder against a recency threshold and flags them for follow-up.
22.1.10 requires campaign performance dashboards covering sends, conversions, revenue generated, ROI and profitability, which is the campaign and marketing performance section.
Missing a customer behaviour analytics section for the CRM board; 8.6.13 uses behaviour to drive recommendations and 1.6.18 analyses behaviour only inside the resale marketplace.
AI-generated and AI analytics dashboards are required, but nothing obliges a diagnostic layer spanning every board that explains why a metric moved.
adjudicator_note: Same capability as MOM-1473 seen from the platform side; specify it once.

rationale: The matrix requires AI-generated dashboards but not prescriptive management action recommendations derived from sales, revenue and attendance trends.
adjudicator_note: Sits close to the boundary MOM-1562 draws around AI in approvals; keep the two rules consistent.

rationale: KPI monitoring and alerts are required, but no candidate provides an administration surface where each KPI's target, its data sources and its management rules are defined.
adjudicator_note: Pairs with MOM-1478; the KPI definition metadata is the missing piece in both.

rationale: A KPI can be monitored and can raise an alert, but nothing requires an explanation of why it is failing or a recommended action to recover it.
This is the chair's summary of scope - roughly ten boards - rather than a testable statement of system behaviour.
adjudicator_note: Useful as the scope envelope for the reporting module; capture it as a deliverable list of the named boards, not as a matrix row.

rationale: Missing the consolidation rule that all reporting live in one permission-based analytics module instead of dashboard screens repeated inside each functional module.
adjudicator_note: Shapes where every dashboard requirement in the matrix is implemented; if domains keep their own dashboards this is contradicted throughout.

rationale: Missing the single entry point whose contents are filtered by the viewer's access rights, so finance sees finance boards and an executive sees across sales, admissions and access control.
adjudicator_note: Same access-architecture gap as MOM-1475; 8.7.x enumerates dashboards by subject but never who may see them.

rationale: Missing the requirement that a user entitled to several domains gets one combined command center rather than separate per-module screens.
adjudicator_note: Consequence of MOM-1527 and MOM-1528; one matrix row on entitlement-driven composition can carry all three.

rationale: Missing the placement rule that dashboard configuration and settings sit inside the consolidated reporting and analytics area rather than in each module.
adjudicator_note: Follows directly from MOM-1527; can ride on the same matrix row.

rationale: Missing the counter-rule that simulation functionality stays embedded in its own module and is deliberately excluded from the consolidated reporting module.
adjudicator_note: This bounds the consolidation decision in MOM-1527; without it the two could be read as conflicting.

rationale: 8.7.14 requires cross-domain reporting, which is what accounting for reporting touchpoints spread across every other module amounts to.
adjudicator_note: Extracted from a caution raised in discussion rather than a decision; the matrix row nevertheless obliges the behaviour.

rationale: The matrix enumerates named approval workflows (configuration changes, policy changes, access permission changes) but does not require a configurable engine that can be pointed at any request type, including new product creation and website changes.
adjudicator_note: Generic configurable approval engine versus a fixed list of hard-coded workflows is an architecture decision; the matrix reads as the latter.

rationale: Missing the consolidated surface: an approval command center or inbox listing all pending, validated and renewal requests across workflow types; the candidates are individual per-type approval workflows.
18.6.1 gives users a read-only inbox of pending approvals; nothing obliges assigning or reassigning a request to another department or person from that inbox.
Missing SLA configuration on approvals - a deadline by which a request must be actioned; the candidates name approval workflows by request type but never a time bound.
adjudicator_note: SLA definition is the precondition for the escalation (MOM-1537) and reminder (MOM-1550) requirements.

rationale: Missing automatic escalation of a request to the next approval level when its SLA lapses, with the ability to investigate and reassign.
11.1.2 allows workflows to be configured per business process, but no row requires a builder that sets the number of approval levels and the specific approvers at each level.
adjudicator_note: 11.1.2 was returned as a candidate on sibling row MOM-1545, not on this one; verify the id when tracing.

rationale: Generic workflow configuration is required, but nothing obliges authority rules that route a request to a different approver according to monetary threshold and category.
adjudicator_note: A delegation-of-authority matrix keyed on amount bands appears nowhere in the candidates.

rationale: 11.1.42 requires a tenant-based approval matrix but stops at the tenant; the venue dimension of the approval matrix is not obliged anywhere.
adjudicator_note: Tenant plus venue is two axes; confirm whether venue-level variation is in scope.

rationale: The matrix defines separate workflows per request type but never requires approval groups as a first-class construct that can be bound to a request type.
Nothing in the candidates makes approval depth a function of the request's attributes such as amount or ticket quantity; workflows are configured per process, not per value band.
adjudicator_note: Overlaps the amount-based routing gap in MOM-1539; treat the two as one matrix addition.

rationale: Missing quorum rules - any N approvers from a group of M, with one named role mandatory among them; no candidate expresses approver counts at all.
Missing the execution and decision management board that tracks a request's full journey through approval; the candidates are per-type workflow rows and a versioning row.
Missing a business-context/evidence viewer that surfaces the supporting transaction detail - payment information and any logged customer complaint - next to the approval decision.
adjudicator_note: Implies the approval record can reach into payment and complaint data; an integration question, not just a screen.

rationale: Missing an approval timeline visualisation with initiation time and per-stage completed/pending timestamps; 11.1.80 versions workflow definitions, not instances.
adjudicator_note: Requires stage-level timestamps to be captured on every approval instance.

rationale: 11.1.60 requires MFA for sensitive approval actions, which is exactly this requirement.
11.1.60 requires MFA support for sensitive approvals but does not state that enabling it is a business-configurable switch rather than mandatory behaviour.
adjudicator_note: 11.1.60 was a candidate on MOM-1547, not on this row; the distinction here is a scoping clarification rather than new scope.

rationale: Missing delegation and approver-availability management - naming a substitute approver so a request does not stall while an approver is away.
Missing SLA monitoring with reminder notifications to the approver as the deadline approaches; no candidate covers approval reminders.
Missing a workload view showing the count of pending requests carried by each approver; the candidates define workflows but no load-by-approver reporting.

11.1.24 only prevents a user approving their own request and 3.3.31 enforces separation inside access policies; neither gives a governance surface where conflicting duty pairs are defined and managed.
adjudicator_note: Self-approval is the narrowest reading of segregation of duties; confirm the wider conflict matrix is in scope.

rationale: MFA on sensitive approvals is required, but not a governance board on which the MFA policy itself is set and maintained.
adjudicator_note: 11.1.60 was returned as a candidate on MOM-1547 rather than here.

rationale: 11.1.57 requires digital signature support for sensitive approvals but not the governance configuration deciding where signatures are applicable.
22.13.20 reports retention status on a consent-compliance dashboard, but no candidate lets the business define and manage the data retention policy itself from a governance surface.
adjudicator_note: Retention policy determines storage, archival and purge behaviour across the reporting data store; settle it before build.

rationale: 11.1.6 requires a complete history of approval requests, approvers, comments, timestamps and decisions, which is the audit trail this requirement asks for.
Missing identification and display of compliance risks on the governance board; the candidates are approval workflow rows with no risk register or risk surfacing.
adjudicator_note: Undefined what constitutes a compliance risk and who raises it; worth pinning down at sign-off.

rationale: 11.1.27 requires analytics on approval times and 11.1.68 specifically on approval processing times, which is per-request duration.
11.1.27 requires analytics on approval volumes, times and rejection rates across approvals, which is the overall turnaround performance view.

Approval time analytics are required, but neither bottleneck nor individual approver performance analytics are named, and no row imposes the boundary that AI must not recommend or influence an approve/reject outcome.
adjudicator_note: 11.1.37 (AI Recommendation Approval Workflow) sits in the same subdomain and could be read as contradicting this boundary; clarify at sign-off.

rationale: Missing the governance constraint that the approve/deny decision stays with a human approver and is never automated or AI-assisted.
adjudicator_note: Pairs with MOM-1562; both express the same human-in-the-loop boundary the matrix never states.

rationale: This is the open action item tracking the component list owed by the client, not a statement of system behaviour.
adjudicator_note: Duplicates MOM-1481 and MOM-1484, which carry the substantive gap; keep it on the action log.

rationale: Multi-tenancy is required generally but a tenant or system code stamped on every transaction is not.
A configurable operating day boundary, midnight-to-midnight or an alternative window, is missing.
Multi-venue operation and multi-site reporting are assumed but sites as uniquely identified entities under a tenant are never defined.
Operating-area rights are referenced for report access but operating areas are never defined as a configurable organisational level.
Role-based access and restriction by venue and POS terminal are required, but the operating-area level of the permission hierarchy is missing.
Roles and permissions are configurable but inheritance of site-level settings such as password policy and UI rights down to all users and workstations is not.
Operating areas exist as a rights and revenue-split dimension but the site to operating area to workstation containment is not modelled.
6.1.67 requires Revenue by Operating Area and Revenue by Workstation reports and 6.1.13 the matching operating-area report rights.
A user activity audit report is required but a per-workstation activity log is not.
7.1.12 requires configurable role-based access control with permissions grouped into roles and assigned to users.
Role-based access control and reports of users, roles and permissions are obliged but a side-by-side comparison of two roles is not.
2.12.35 requires cash, card, wallet, vouchers, gift cards and bank transfers as configurable payment methods.
Integrated card terminals and their capabilities are obliged but manual entry of an authorisation code returned by a standalone terminal is not.
This restates the benefit of the virtual credit card option already captured in MOM-1587 rather than stating testable system behaviour.
Extended guest information capture exists but a configurable custom-field framework applying at account, event, ticket and product level is not.
The untruncated 2.12.6 names the standard guest fields and requires them to be configurable, but fully user-defined custom fields alongside them are still not obliged.
Product-level qualifying questions such as a pregnancy declaration or weight range gating purchase are missing.
Automated background jobs are supported for revenue recognition but a platform task scheduler managing recurring jobs is not required.
7.4.47 requires inventory reserved at checkout to be released automatically when payment is not completed within a configurable timeout.
The configurable checkout-timeout release and automatic hold release cover returning abandoned-cart capacity to inventory.
Financial data export to ERP plus scheduled report generation and delivery to a location cover the scheduled export job.
Automatic movement of deferred revenue to earned and configurable recognition schedules are required, but an overnight job driven by actual ticket scans is not.
Drag-and-drop builders exist for reports, pages and newsletters but no candidate requires a POS button and layout designer placing products and system functions with configurable fonts and colours.

Old and new value tracking exists for product configuration and login and user activity audits are reported, but a platform-wide old-versus-new audit across every screen and transaction is not obliged.
In-system staff-to-staff task assignment and follow-up is missing.
Product categories are configurable but statistical groups driving website presentation and reporting are not.
The white-label CMS rows oblige theming only; automatic sync of backend product content such as title, terms, age limits and images to the live site is not required.
2.9.11 requires multiple tax rates and tax profiles per product, which is the tax package.
Tax-inclusive, tax-exclusive and tax-exempt handling and tax calculation are obliged but compound tax applied on a tax-inclusive base is not.
B2B and B2C account creation and guest checkout are required but the agent or child account hierarchy under a B2B main account is not.
B2B credit limits are covered but credit days and an account-specific price list on the financial tab are not.
Special B2B prices by segment are required but an account-specific price list assigned to an individual partner is not.
Transaction history is a required capability and 5.3.17 obliges full purchase and transaction history to be held against the profile.
5.3.17 requires guest profiles to carry purchase, refund and transaction history.
Products must carry a channel and segment tag and categories are configurable, but channel-specific setup of the same product as separate catalogue records is not obliged.
2.9.12 requires tax-inclusive, tax-exclusive and tax-exempt handling to be selectable per product alongside its price.
Stored-value entitlements are covered but the consolidated entitlement set of upgradeability, linked event, re-entry rules and linked performance is not defined on the product record.
2.1.3 requires pricing rules to be stored and applied per sales channel, which is multiple price lists per channel.
Season-dated price lists such as separate winter and summer pricing are missing from the candidates.
Ticket properties may differ by tier and age group, but a component-and-attribute model with each person type priced independently is not stated.
Roles and operating-area rights govern access to functions and reports, but who may sell a given product, scoped by site, operating area or workstation, is not obliged.
adjudicator_note: 6.1.67 lists site, operating area, cashier and workstation as reporting dimensions only, not as sales-permission scopes.

rationale: A partner self-registration form capturing company details and trade licence or VAT documents is missing.
Creation of a pending account record from a partner registration submission is missing.
Document validation with rejection and resubmission messaging for partner onboarding is missing.
Open-dated tickets and configurable events both exist but the rule that an event is needed only where date, time and capacity control apply is not stated.
Third-party channels and real-time availability are required but checking a third-party platform at the point of sale and issuing its QR code is not.
1.1.3 requires timeslot creation for a whole day or a period with capacity configuration and 1.3.3 sessions defined by date, time and capacity.
Late-entry expiry measured from the admission time is required but not a configurable early-entry opening window before the booked slot.
Timeslot capacity is configurable but multi-select bulk editing of performance capacity is not required.
Suspending, resuming and cancelling an individual performance is missing.
The rule that suspension is a reversible state change rather than a deletion is missing.
The disable-able state model for performance availability is missing.
adjudicator_note: Duplicates MOM-1653; it records confirmation of that decision rather than a separate requirement.

rationale: Channel and slot-based inventory controls exist to stop overselling but explicit per-channel capacity envelopes with numeric allocations are not required.
Channel-based inventory controls exist but showing each channel only its allocated share of availability is not obliged.
Re-entry may be allowed or not per product and a number of entries per park may be set, but the three-way choice of not allowed, once per day or unlimited is not obliged.
End-of-month, end-of-year and performance date/time expiry are required but end-of-week and first-use-based expiry are not.
3.2.1 requires one barcode to grant park entry, ride entitlement, vouchers and re-entry rights, which is one ticket linked to several entitlements.
3.6.16 and 4.1.10 require automatic buy-X-get-Y and added-value promotions that apply without a code.
The matrix carries a Resource Management subdomain requiring resource categorisation, APIs and linkage of resources to bookable experiences.
1.2.11 requires operational rosters showing resource availability and 1.2.6 a calendar view of resources and their time slots.
1.2.29 requires availability management and conflict detection and 1.2.28 resource time-slot availability at the point of booking.
22.2.9 requires duplicate guest records to be reviewed and merged while preserving complete transaction history.
Real-time capacity management and colour-coded booked capacity per time slot are required at the point of selection.
Guest information is captured on the order but a per-ticket owner distinct from the buyer is not modelled.
Ticket history with payment method and stored purchase data are obliged but a consolidated reservation view carrying applicable taxes and a post-purchase survey is not.
A unique, randomised ticket id per ticket is obliged but a media code shareable across several tickets scanned as one group is not modelled.
Revenue by user/cashier and sales dashboards are obliged but a POS Sales Summary scoped to the logged-in cashier with voids, refunds and an activity chart is not.
Sales dashboards are required but a time-based activity chart on the cashier summary is not.
adjudicator_note: The top lexical candidates matched chart of accounts, not charting.

rationale: Real-time in-park attendance figures and access-point statistics are required but not an Admission Summary dashboard showing scanned headcount per venue.
6.1.67 lists revenue reports by site, operating area, user or cashier and workstation, with 6.1.13 the matching access rights.
6.1.67 requires a Payment Summary, Transaction Journal and Product Sold and Paid report, which is the sales report described.
6.1.67 requires both a Payment Summary and a Revenue by User/Cashier report.
Custom reports from available fields and self-service reporting are required but SQL or scripting-level template authoring is not.
Report export to Excel is required but PDF export of reports is not.
Bronze, silver and gold options are acknowledged at the front gate but tiered packages each priced by adult, child and infant are not obliged.
A single barcode may carry re-entry rights and re-entry may be allowed per product, but a single-entry main gate combined with unlimited re-entry at named attractions is not modelled.
3.2.11 requires all access control rules, gates, access points and locations to be definable, which is the tier-to-gate mapping the client fills in.
adjudicator_note: The matrix template itself is a delivery artefact rather than system behaviour.

rationale: 3.2.11 requires locations, gates and access points to be configured as the access-control model, which is the chain described.
Access rules are configurable but explicit deny rules that block a ticket type at a gate it is not entitled to use are not required.
Multi-tenancy is asserted but the site, operating area and workstation hierarchy, the operating calendar and the five-level permission model are not.
Draft status and approval workflows are obliged, but no candidate requires a dashboard presenting counts of products sitting in draft, in approval and published.
The matrix has product lifecycle management but no lifecycle dashboard and therefore no venue or department filters on it.
1.4.6 obliges configurable approval workflows before a product can be published, which is the authorisation step asked for.
An AI configuration assistant is obliged for promotions and similar objects, but not a guided ticket-creation wizard that asks for type and fields and produces a draft for approval.
Multi-venue tickets are obliged but the product identity and classification field set, including product ID, main and sub-category and venue association, is not specified.
No candidate obliges a category hierarchy manager for grouping and sorting ticket types and packages under nested categories.
Age group and tier properties are configurable per ticket but ID-proof requirements with format validation or photo upload are not a configurable ticket attribute.
Eligibility rules cover residency and nationality but the ID-document set and its configurability per ticket and per region are not obliged.
Nothing obliges a preview of how the product will appear on the B2C front end as a step before publishing.
PDF and Apple or Google Wallet output formats are obliged, but previewing those renderings inside product configuration before publish is not.
1.1.1 obliges open-dated tickets and 1.1.9 and 1.1.78 their configurable, fixed validity period, which with name, description and price is this product.
Dated and special-day tickets are obliged but each such ticket carrying its own sales window is not.
1.1.19 obliges rescheduling within configurable rules, fees, blackout periods and availability constraints, which is the product-level reschedule policy described.

The previously cut tail of 1.1.3 requires pre and post buffer time against the performance start, worked through as scanning from 30 minutes before until a defined cut-off, which is this early/late entry window.
Date-range and number-of-days validity and multi-venue tickets are obliged, but the choice between consecutive-day use and flexible use inside a longer range is not.
2.14.19 obliges monthly, quarterly, annual and configurable membership periods and 2.14.20 automatic renewal with notices, which is the membership class and renewal ask.
Pricing may vary by guest category and residency, but nothing obliges product classification itself being built from configurable components rather than a fixed structure.
1.1.26 requires named, anonymous and partially assigned tickets with configurable ownership rules, which is exactly the anonymous versus captured-details choice.
adjudicator_note: 1.1.26 was not in this row's candidate list; its full text appears in another row of the same chunk.

rationale: 1.1.80 obliges date range validity, which is fixed date-range validity.
1.1.84 obliges first-use validity, which is a validity period that starts at first scan rather than at sale.
Weekday-based validity is obliged but differentiated pricing for weekday-only versus all-days products is not.
First-use validity is obliged but a fallback expiry for a ticket that is never scanned, without which the revenue cannot be recognised, is not.
Nothing obliges blockout dates that exclude a ticket type from use on holidays or special event days.
No candidate obliges capacity defaulting at event level, inheriting to every performance, with a per-performance override.
No candidate obliges forecast-driven recommendations to add or remove time slots.
Reservation modification notifications are obliged, but recommending a merge of under-sold adjacent slots and moving the affected guests is not.
8.5.1 obliges dynamic ticket pricing, 8.5.19 pricing thresholds and 8.5.8 time-slot pricing, which is a slot price moved by how much of it is sold.
The previously cut tail of 1.1.10 defines Admission Capacity alongside Sales Capacity, so the matrix does distinguish the two capacity types.
adjudicator_note: 1.1.10 expresses admission capacity as a cap on tickets sold against attraction capacity rather than a live scan-based occupancy count; the turnstile basis should be confirmed at sign-off.

rationale: 1.1.10's admission capacity limits how many tickets may be sold against attraction capacity; capping live on-site attendance independently of tickets sold is not required.
No candidate makes venue-level admission capacity supersede event-level capacity, nor requires a validation blocking configuration or sale beyond the remaining venue capacity.
No candidate obliges an authorisation-gated override of a capacity validation restricted to specific roles.
adjudicator_note: Depends on the platform-wide RBAC model that is itself missing (see MOM-0573 and MOM-0576).

rationale: Nothing obliges inventory pools that split a capacity by ticket type or by sales channel in configured proportions.
adjudicator_note: Same area as MOM-2581 and MOM-1788; one matrix addition should serve all three.

rationale: Capacity configurable at multiple levels is obliged, but not the specific global, attraction, product, variant and time-slot hierarchy or its precedence.
Capacity is auto-allotted back on cancellation, but the business choice of whether a cancelled, refunded or rescheduled slot returns to sale or is held is not configurable.
1.1.50 obliges multiple entitlements per ticket, 1.1.53 F&B entitlement management and 3.1.2 a unique QR per ticket, which is the combo redemption described.
1.1.11 obliges a configurable number of entitled accesses per ticket and 1.1.50 multiple entitlements per ticket, which is the entry cap asked for.
Nothing obliges a time-bound product entitlement whose window starts at first scan, such as a 60-minute activity.
1.1.55 and 1.1.106 oblige stored-value entitlement carried on a ticket and 4.3.22 the drawn-down cashless balance, which is the combo described.
The wallet holds campaign rewards, vouchers, credits and points but crediting a referral reward as currency or points, as a configurable alternative to a voucher, is not obliged.
Check-in and check-out entitlement control is obliged, but flagging an unmatched exit and blocking the next entry scan until it is reconciled is not.
Historical sales look-up by ticket number is obliged, but a consumption history bringing together scan count, expiry, wallet balance and F&B or retail spend on one screen is not.
1.1.38 obliges eligibility rules including residency and nationality, which is the restriction asked for.
1.1.125 obliges customer profile restrictions and 1.1.38 custom business conditions, which covers restricting a product to a guest category such as VIP.
1.1.38 obliges eligibility rules including loyalty status and membership and 5.4.31 spend thresholds for tier qualification, which is this rule.

Quantity limits exist for B2B partners and bulk thresholds and 'quantity restrictions' appears as a bare ticket property, but limits per order, per guest, per account category and per sales channel are not obliged.
adjudicator_note: 2.12.23, seen in other rows of this chunk, does oblige purchase frequency restrictions and B2B account restrictions per product, which covers part of this.

rationale: 1.1.114 and 1.1.115 oblige fixed and dynamic quantity group tickets and 2.16.7 the one-ticket versus N-ticket media options behind single or multiple QR codes.
The matrix is written at capability level and never says where configuration lives, so nothing obliges special product types and policies being managed on one unified screen.
