No candidate obliges duration-based hourly pricing of a bookable resource with the total calculated from the booked period.
1.2.29 obliges availability and conflict detection, which blocks a booked resource for its window against a second booking.
Nothing obliges a per-ticket-type setting that lets the guest choose a specific instructor or resource.
1.2.6 in full is a resource calendar for staff selection; nothing makes auto-assignment without exposing the instructor a per-ticket-type behaviour.
Group products and product variants both exist, but the matrix does not oblige private and group sessions being separate priced products rather than variants.
Nothing obliges a customer-initiated private session on a shared resource being a distinct, separately priced product rather than an ad hoc request.
adjudicator_note: Same modelling decision as MOM-2176.

rationale: Dynamic assignment at sale is obliged and advance reservations exist, but the pre-assigned model mapping resources to slots ahead of time is not required alongside it.
4.5.25 requires consolidated reporting across outlets and 4.5.20 inventory dashboards, but not a real-time retail dashboard carrying the named tiles and a day, week and month view.
Retail revenue is reported by site and channel, but the total retail sales tile on the retail dashboard is not obliged as such.
6.1.10 summarises daily transactions including units sold, but a total transactions figure on the retail dashboard is not obliged.
6.1.66 requires average spend per customer, which is close to but not the same as average transaction value on the retail dashboard.
adjudicator_note: Confirm at sign-off whether average spend per customer and average transaction value are intended to be the same metric.

rationale: 4.5.25 requires consolidated reporting across outlets but not a store performance snapshot tile on the retail dashboard.
Stock alerts are required, but a general system-alerts panel on the retail dashboard is not obliged.
4.4.17 requires out-of-stock and low-stock alerts on configurable thresholds, which is what the dashboard's out-of-stock indicator surfaces.
6.1.54 requires product reports on daily, weekly and monthly cycles, but the retail dashboard's day, week and month toggle is not obliged.
4.5.4 requires local in-store inventory to be recorded and 15.1.10 inventory across multiple locations, which is outlet-level stock management.
No candidate requires a count of total products per store on a retail catalogue dashboard.
No candidate requires products to be classified into catalogues and that classification surfaced on the dashboard.
6.1.67's report list includes best selling products, but a top-products-sold tile on the retail catalogue dashboard is not obliged.
Revenue accounts are held per item and item type but a product-by-category breakdown on the retail catalogue dashboard is not obliged.
4.4.11 requires variants such as size and colour with independent SKU, barcode, inventory and pricing, which is the product master described.
4.4.11 requires product variants such as size and colour to each carry independent SKU, barcode, inventory and pricing, which is stock tracked at variant level.
adjudicator_note: 4.4.11 surfaced on the product-master row rather than this one.

rationale: No candidate requires a multi-level product category, brand and subcategory hierarchy for the retail catalogue.
1.4.7 publishes products to selected sales channels, but channel assortment managed at catalogue level rather than product by product is not obliged.
2.3.1 requires configurable product types to remain sellable offline, but the rule that capacity-based dated and timed products are the ones blocked, with the rest syncing later, is not fixed.
No candidate requires the primary plus read-only reporting replica split; this is a data-architecture decision that governs how reporting loads are isolated from live transactions.
15.1.12 tracks available stock, but the screen contrasting stock on hand with available stock net of online purchases awaiting pickup or shipment is not obliged.
4.4.15 requires stock transfers between stores and warehouses including approval workflows and receiving confirmation, which is the inter-store requisition with approval before transfer.
4.4.15 requires transfers between stores and warehouses with shipment tracking and receiving confirmation, which covers all three directions named.
15.1.24 requires physical inventory counts and 18.7.2 that users perform them; the monthly or weekly cadence is an operating choice on top.
15.1.18 requires stock adjustments, which is how damage and loss are written off.
No candidate requires stock adjustment reasons to come from a user-extendable configured list rather than a hard-coded one.
15.1.13 requires reserved inventory to be tracked, which is stock held for a named customer.
No candidate requires stock to be allocated per sales channel and sold down independently against each channel's allocation.
4.5.26 requires physical stock taking with an RFID gun scanner and 16.8.43 handheld scanner integration, which is the bulk RFID count.
15.1.26 requires stock reconciliation, which is the comparison of recorded stock against a fresh count however it was captured.
adjudicator_note: 15.1.26 is reused from an adjacent inventory candidate set.

rationale: Refund approval workflows exist, but the online return path - approval team, courier pickup, then refund on verified receipt - is not obliged.
4.5.25 requires consolidated reporting across outlets and 6.1.66 revenue by site and product, which is sales and outlet performance reporting.
The untruncated 6.1.66 requires revenue by site and top performing products and sales channels, but not a ranking of top-performing stores.
Attendance forecasting from historical and real-time booking trends is required, but retail demand forecasting that blends retail sales history with those booking trends is not.
No candidate requires sales targets to be held and tracked against actuals with variance reporting per outlet; the only variance reporting in view is on stock.
This is meeting logistics - scheduling a dedicated CRM session - not a requirement on the system.
Time-slot and event pricing exist and early-bird pricing appears as an AI recommendation, but a rule raising price once venue capacity crosses a configured threshold is not obliged.
8.5.38 requires AI-generated pricing recommendations based on weather conditions, which is the factor-based component described.
12.1.2 requires accreditation applications to be submitted through configurable forms.
12.1.3 requires accreditation review and approval but does not oblige supporting documents to be collected with the application and assessed as part of it.
12.1.22, 12.1.24 and 12.1.17 require QR credentials, RFID credentials and holder photographs, which are the three badge forms named.
3.3.10 requires accreditation attributes to be evaluated when granting access and 12.1.5 venue access rights to be assigned by accreditation type.
12.1.47 requires accreditation dashboards, which is the registration overview this board asks for.
Accreditation dashboards are required but no total-registered count is named as one of their measures.
Review and approval and accreditation dashboards are both required, but no pending-review count is obliged on the dashboard.
Documents are stored and dashboards required, but no count of expired documents is obliged as a dashboard measure.
Applications and holder profiles must be held, but no searchable application directory across name, company and other submitted business fields is obliged.
Multi-level sub-accounts exist for financial and guest records, but no partner or company account structure inside accreditation with its own sub-accounts.
Applications through configurable forms are required and one authorised user may act for several people elsewhere, but no company account logs in and files accreditation requests for its own members.
22.10.24 requires a configurable form builder covering registrations and 22.10.4 the visual drag-and-drop construction for non-technical users.
Media, guest and staff accreditation types exist and forms are configurable, but nothing binds a distinct field set to each accreditation category.
12.1.38 and 12.1.39 require accreditations to be linked to specific events and to specific venues.
adjudicator_note: Neither row covers a season-long accreditation, which the source lists alongside event and venue.

rationale: Configurable application forms, document storage and venue- and event-specific accreditations exist, but no per-application-type requirement set stating what a contractor or other category must additionally provide.
Accreditation documents must be stored but nothing defines which documents each category is obliged to submit, so completeness cannot be judged.
Accreditation dashboards and document storage are required, but no submission-tracking view separating submitted, pending and applications missing required documents.
No candidate requires an uploaded identity document to be read by OCR and its values written into the application's fields.
12.1.18 obliges the document to be stored but not its contents to be held as structured fields that expiry checks could run against.
Expiry notifications and renewal workflows apply to the accreditation itself, not to the expiry date of an individual supporting document such as an Emirates ID.
12.1.16 requires detailed holder profiles, 12.1.17 the holder photograph and 12.1.3 the review step in which staff open and assess the application.
12.1.19 requires identity verification before accreditation approval and 12.1.3 the review step in which the submitted documents are judged.
Duplicate guest records are detected and merged on identifiers including passport number, but nothing blocks a duplicate accreditation submission at the point of entry.
Detailed accreditation holder profiles are required but no link from the holder to an organisation or company profile.
Internal approval dashboards and rejection and resubmission workflows exist, but no organisation-scoped view showing a company account the status of every application filed under it.
Single and multi-level approval chains are required, but nothing ties a different chain to each accreditation category.
11.1.4 requires approval requests to be routed by organisational hierarchy and user role, which is how each chain gets its own reviewers and approvers.
Configurable time thresholds exist for escalation, but no approval or rejection turnaround target is set per accreditation category as an SLA.
Nothing raises an alert when the volume of pending applications builds against a turnaround target, so a backlog of media passes would go unflagged.
11.1.5 requires pending approvals to be escalated automatically after configurable time thresholds and 11.1.47 escalation through successive organisational levels.
12.1.20, 12.1.22 and 12.1.24 require printed badges, QR credentials and RFID credentials, which are the media the approved applicant may be issued.
12.1.25 requires access rights to be assigned by venue zone and 12.1.5 by accreditation type, which is exactly the zone-by-category rule.
Zone rights are assigned in 12.1.25 and 3.3.10 requires accreditation attributes to be evaluated at the moment access is granted, which is enforcement at the scan.
12.1.32 requires accreditation lifecycle statuses and 12.1.34 and 12.1.37 the suspension and renewal transitions within them.
Resubmission workflows and expiry notifications exist, but nothing compares a submitted document's own expiry date with the event date to raise the resubmission request.
Suspension and immediate revocation of accreditation access are required, but neither is triggered by an unresolved document resubmission request.
12.1.44 requires applicants to be notified of approval decisions and 11.1.19 notification on approval, rejection and escalation.

12.1.54 requires bulk import and 12.1.3 requires review and approval, but neither obliges that a bulk-imported record still be routed through profile selection, document submission and approval rather than landing pre-approved.
The matrix asks only for accreditation dashboards and status reports; it does not specify the approvals, upcoming-expiry and per-portfolio/per-category breakdowns the minutes fix as the content.
Accreditation reporting is required in the abstract, but nothing obliges the issued-versus-scanned attendance comparison, which needs accreditation records joined to access-control scan events.
adjudicator_note: Cross-module data join (accreditation to access control) implied by this KPI; worth confirming at sign-off.

rationale: 12.1.7 obliges point-in-time accreditation status reports but nothing requires period-over-period or venue-over-venue comparison, which presupposes retained history and a venue dimension on accreditation usage.
adjudicator_note: Implies historical retention and a multi-venue dimension; an architecture question for sign-off.

rationale: No candidate requires a central entitlements dashboard listing customers, families, corporates and schools with the tickets, benefits and entitlements each holds; the candidates cover exchanges, transfers and group queueing only.

Missing an access/surface requirement that the same entitlements view serve both the guest in the mobile app and a customer-service agent handling an inquiry; the only mobile dashboard row (6.1.56) is about daily revenue alerts.

5.4.32 requires a single guest view combining membership status, wallet balances, vouchers, benefits, entitlements and reservations, which is the same consolidated profile picture this requirement asks for.
adjudicator_note: 5.4.32 does not mention restrictions explicitly; confirm restrictions are in scope of that view at sign-off.

rationale: The matrix requires family ticket composition rules and family portfolio structures but not a view that displays a family ticket's composition alongside the entitlements tied to each named dependent.

Corporate allocations and organisational hierarchies are required, but no candidate obliges an entitlement composition view for corporate bookings, and school bookings are not addressed at all outside virtual queueing.
adjudicator_note: School group entitlement structure appears only in the virtual-queue row 5.6.18; a school booking construct may be missing from the matrix.

rationale: 5.5.8 requires all entitlement types to be maintained but stops short of a consolidated per-visit list presenting admissions, fast passes, meal packages and parking together in one place.
5.5.19 covers assigning entitlements to portfolio members, but no candidate requires an assignment manager that defines who is eligible to receive and who is permitted to consume a given entitlement.
1.1.27 requires ticket ownership transfer between guests according to configurable policies, fees and approval workflows, which is exactly the transfer to another guest when the buyer cannot attend.
adjudicator_note: 1.1.27 is not among this row's own candidates; its full text appears as a candidate on MOM-0845 in the same chunk.

rationale: 1.5.4 requires a record of ticket status changes and 3.2.17 a displayable ticket history, but neither obliges retention of the original purchaser's identity and a full chain of transfer history after a transfer.
4.3.31 imposes spending and transfer restrictions inside the wallet module only; no candidate extends those permissions and spending controls to the entitlements portfolio.
Missing a data-model requirement that a ticket entitlement be associated with its credential/media inside the portfolio; 12.1.12 is press/media accreditation, a different sense of the word.
adjudicator_note: Ticketing Sales > Ticket Media rows (e.g. 2.16.10) may cover media association generally but were not offered here; check before logging as a true gap.

rationale: 2.13.43 is a bare CRM 360 View label under Front Gate Sales and 5.5.1 covers single-portfolio ownership; neither specifies a portfolio 360 view consolidating entitlements, permissions and credentials per customer.
adjudicator_note: 2.13.43 carries the highest lexical score purely on the phrase 360 View; it is a heading, not a specification.

rationale: No candidate requires an entitlements lifecycle/analytics view surfacing entitlements nearing expiry; the product-lifecycle rows offered concern product versioning and duplication, not entitlement expiry.
5.5.25 requires exactly these statuses to be maintained but does not oblige an analytics breakdown that counts entitlements by status.

5.5.25 requires the full status set (active, reserved, consumed, transferred, expired, refunded, cancelled) and 15.1.13 requires reserved inventory tracking, together obliging the lifecycle this requirement describes.
5.5.20 requires entitlement consumption to be tracked in real time across all channels, which is what the consumption monitor asks a tester to verify.
Missing the architectural requirement that accreditation-holder monitoring be a filtered view of one unified entitlement monitoring platform rather than a separate subsystem.
adjudicator_note: This is a design-consolidation decision; if the matrix keeps accreditation monitoring in domain 12 separately, the two may conflict.

rationale: Missing a segmentation/filter requirement letting staff distinguish and service large accredited groups against general guests inside one monitoring platform; the candidates are queue administration and device monitoring rows.
This records the workshop's design priority about how many screens a concept is explained across, not a behaviour the system must exhibit.
adjudicator_note: Worth carrying into UX acceptance criteria even though it is not a matrix-scorable requirement.

rationale: Configurable usage restrictions and consumption tracking are required, but the specific per-ticket parameters named here - allowed usage count and number of re-entries - are not called out.
No candidate requires upgrade status to be visible on the entitlements view; the access-control rows offered concern validation and post-issue rule changes, not upgrade lineage.
adjudicator_note: Matrix has a Ticket Upgrades subdomain (e.g. 2.11.4) not offered as a candidate; it may cover the upgrade transaction but not its visibility in the entitlement view.

rationale: 11.1.30 requires approval workflows for refund requests, which is exactly the operations/finance routing this requirement asks a tester to check.
2.12.18 already requires refunds to the original payment mode or as credits to the guest's wallet, matching both branches of this requirement.

5.6.1 requires Virtual Queue, Fast Pass and Express Queue types side by side and 5.6.21 requires reservations for rides and attractions, which together oblige the multi-ride park scenario with general-admission and express ticket holders.
The matrix names the queue types and asks the system to recommend ride allocation, but it never requires a per-ride hourly capacity pool split across express, virtual-queue and walk-in guests.
adjudicator_note: The allocation model is the core of the virtual queue engine; absent it, capacity, throughput and wait-time figures cannot be computed.

rationale: 5.6.27 only requires the system to recommend queue balancing; it does not oblige the allocation between lanes to adjust dynamically when one lane runs disproportionately busy.
5.6.7 requires real-time updates on remaining wait time and 5.6.36 requires wait times to be estimated, which is the per-ride wait time the app displays.
5.6.31 requires guests to reserve queue positions from the app and 5.6.19 requires linked profiles to reserve and manage positions together, which is the party reservation described.
adjudicator_note: 5.6.19 scopes group reservation to linked family profiles; confirm an ad-hoc party of unlinked guests is also in scope.

rationale: 5.6.16 requires the guest to see their live position and estimated service time, computed per 5.6.36 from real-time conditions, which is the estimated return window.
5.6.12 requires queue reservations to expire automatically after a configurable grace period, which is the same no-show release behaviour.
adjudicator_note: 5.6.12 stops at expiry and does not say the freed slot returns to the pool for other guests; confirm capacity reclaim is implied.

rationale: Missing a configuration requirement for enabling or disabling virtual queue per ride per operating day; the candidates cover queue types, privileges and disruption recovery only.
No candidate requires the queue/express split to be a configurable per-ride setting; 5.6.27 only asks the system to recommend allocation.
adjudicator_note: Configuration face of the same gap as MOM-2329; treat the two together at sign-off.

rationale: Wait times must be estimated and displayed, but no candidate makes a target wait time or a return-window duration a configurable queue rule.
Missing configuration for early and late arrival handling at the ride entry scanner check-in point ahead of the lane; no candidate addresses arrival-time tolerance.
adjudicator_note: Also implies a scanning device at each ride entry as a distinct check-in point.

rationale: Missing a non-smartphone channel requirement: an at-ride kiosk that books a queue slot from a wristband scan and prints or shows a return time; 5.6.31 assumes the mobile app.
adjudicator_note: A kiosk channel implies hardware, device management and an alternative identity route for guests without the app.

rationale: Missing the redemption half of the kiosk journey: admitting a guest at their assigned return time by scanning the wristband that holds the queue reservation; the candidates cover queue types and wait-time display only.
5.6.1 requires the queue types to exist in the system but not that walk-in, virtual-queue and VIP guests be operationally distinguishable at the ride itself.
Missing the negative constraint that virtual-queue guests must not be merged into the VIP physical lane so that the VIP guest's paid wait advantage is preserved.
adjudicator_note: A commercial rule protecting express-ticket value; worth stating explicitly before sign-off.

rationale: 5.6.4 gives premium guests a separate fast-track lane and QR-based entry into queues, but does not oblige a third dedicated handling path for virtual-queue arrivals within a specific arrival window.
5.6.36 requires estimates from historical and real-time operational data and 5.6.7 requires real-time updates, which together oblige a recalculating rather than static return-time estimate.
adjudicator_note: Neither row states the estimate must account for all three guest tiers together; confirm at sign-off.

rationale: The matrix requires wait times to be estimated from real-time operational data but never obliges an accurate real-time per-ride guest count as the input that makes those estimates reliable.
adjudicator_note: Accuracy of the count is the precondition for every wait-time and return-window figure shown to guests and on the operations board.

rationale: Missing an integration requirement naming the people-counting source - line-monitoring sensors or computer-vision/CCTV counting - and ruling out GPS/device-clustering estimation.
adjudicator_note: Implies a sensor or CCTV integration and its data pipeline; no candidate domain currently owns it.

rationale: Missing the design constraint that the counting mechanism be pluggable - sensor, camera or manual - behind an accurate per-ride count, so no vendor is baked in.
This is an open action item - a pending benchmarking check with a reference operator before the counting technology is chosen - not a statement of system behaviour.
adjudicator_note: Track as a decision item; its outcome will drive MOM-2347.

rationale: 5.6.7 requires real-time wait-time updates computed per 5.6.36, which is the per-ride current wait time the operations view displays.
adjudicator_note: Matrix rows 5.6.2 and 5.6.3 (staff real-time queue dashboard displaying wait times) were not offered as candidates here but cover the operations-view surface itself.

rationale: Wait times must be displayed and estimated, but no candidate requires them to be split into a general-queue figure and a virtual-queue figure for the same ride.
adjudicator_note: Two wait-time series per ride is a modelling decision, not just a display one.

rationale: Missing threshold-based operational alerting on the queue board - a growing express queue or abnormally high overall queue length; 5.6.14 covers guest-facing queue notifications, not staff alerts.
5.6.5 requires load balancing towards less busy rides and 5.6.2 a queue dashboard, but neither obliges a visual venue map that highlights congested rides against low-queue alternatives.
adjudicator_note: A venue map implies ride geo-coordinates or a floorplan asset that no candidate requires.

rationale: 5.6.8 requires the system to automatically recommend or redirect guests to alternative attractions or queues, which is the proactive redirection described.
Missing a queue-triggered commercial requirement: offering the guest an express/fast-lane upgrade at the moment a long wait is detected.
adjudicator_note: Bundles and Promotions has an Upsell and cross-sell subdomain (4.4) that was not offered as a candidate; it may cover POS upsell but not wait-time-triggered offers.

rationale: 1.5.3 filters tickets by adult and child properties, but senior, infant and people-of-determination-with-companion are not obliged guest categories in the booking flow.
Missing per-ticket guest-name capture driven by the selected quantity; the full 7.6.6 captures per-participant details only within the voucher-based rental flow.
This is an action item assigning screen consolidation to the design team, not a system requirement.
20.1.1 and 20.1.3 oblige self-service registration and an AI onboarding wizard but not a public TICVAI-website entry link into a structured needs self-assessment.
The matrix obliges self-service registration and venue templates but not capture of the named organization fields (venue name, industry, attraction type, currency, region, contact, business type).
20.1.4 obliges venue-type templates but does not require the onboarding assessment to capture the prospect's operating model.

The matrix licenses by venue count and auto-configures from onboarding selections but does not oblige capture of visitor capacity and operational-scale figures (visitors, entrances, POS and access points, users, transaction volume, growth).
20.1.5 configures from onboarding selections but the matrix does not require capture of sales channels of interest with volume estimates.
The matrix supports module installation and automatic configuration but does not oblige capture of the product/module types the prospect plans to sell.
20.1.3's AI setup wizard gestures at guided onboarding but the matrix does not oblige capture of the prospect's guest access/validation methods.
The matrix supports module browsing and configuration from onboarding selections but does not oblige capture of which additional modules the prospect needs.
The matrix obliges POS/device and tenant-specific payment integrations but not capture at onboarding of required gateways and devices from a supported list or as an unlisted provider.
The matrix configures the platform from onboarding selections and licenses by Venue Size Index but does not oblige the submitted assessment to be the basis of the proposed commercial/licensing model.
20.3.1 requires licensing based on the Venue Size Index, which obliges computing the composite VSI score from onboarding-captured factors.

20.3.1 names Venue Size Index licensing but does not enumerate the six input factors (annual attendance, POS terminals, access-control devices, venues, users, annual transaction volume) or their weighting.
20.3.1 obliges VSI-based licensing but not backend configuration of each VSI factor as mandatory or optional.

The matrix supports VSI licensing and configurable subscription plans but does not oblige tier threshold configuration mapping VSI score ranges to Essential, Professional, Enterprise and Enterprise Plus.
20.3.1 obliges VSI licensing but not configurable per-factor sub-thresholds assigning points to value bands.
20.3.1 requires VSI-based licensing and 20.8.1 requires the system to recommend the optimal subscription plan, together obliging automatic scoring and tier recommendation.
20.2.1 obliges configurable subscription plans and 20.2.2/20.2.3 monthly and annual subscriptions, which is what per-tier pricing payable monthly or annually asks for.
adjudicator_note: Advance payment by cheque or bank transfer rests on 20.7.3 payment method management rather than an explicit row.

rationale: 20.2.1 obliges configurable subscription plans but not tier-included allowances defining the usage ranges (POS devices, users) included at no extra cost.
The matrix monitors usage but does not oblige a flat tier price for any usage level inside the included allowance range.
20.6.8 requires usage threshold alerts, which is the configurable warning-threshold notification this requirement asks for.
adjudicator_note: The source also requires the alert to reach TICVAI as well as the customer; 20.6.8 names no recipients.

rationale: 20.2.1 obliges configurable subscription plans but the matrix does not name a tier-based flat-fee commercial model charged regardless of actual usage.
20.3.7 obliges hybrid licensing calculations but not a tier-plus-usage model charging a base subscription plus overage above the included allowance.
20.3.5 licenses by transaction volume but the matrix does not oblige a per-ticket commercial model charging an agreed rate per ticket sold.
Nothing in the candidates obliges configurable inclusion/exclusion rules removing complimentary, voided and refunded tickets from the billable count.
20.3.5 requires licensing based on transaction volumes, which is the per-transaction charging model this requirement asks for.
20.3.5 obliges transaction-volume-based licensing, which is the nearest commercial model, but not a revenue-share percentage of the client transaction value.
adjudicator_note: First pass called this Absent; 20.3.5 Transaction-Based Licensing is the right traceability anchor even though the percentage model itself is still uncovered.

rationale: No licensing-model row covers a minimum-guarantee floor payment owed regardless of sales performance.
20.3.7 requires hybrid licensing calculations, which obliges combining any of the supported pricing models for one client.
No licensing-model row covers a fixed-contract commercial model with a fixed total fee over a multi-year term.
adjudicator_note: 15.3.12 contract purchasing is procurement, not licensing.

rationale: The matrix monitors usage and raises threshold alerts but does not oblige configuration of the overage rate charged once included usage is exceeded.
20.5.4 obliges generic licensing enforcement but not enforcement of a configured minimum guarantee alongside billable/excludable ticket rules.
Nothing in the candidates obliges a commercial model simulator for testing and validating a proposed model before assigning it to a customer.
20.2.2 obliges monthly subscriptions but not per-ticket/per-transaction billing for self-hosted or offline clients based on monthly usage reporting instead of live metering.
20.6.7 obliges usage dashboards but not manual or automatic generation of usage reports inside a client-hosted environment TICVAI supports.
20.7.1 obliges subscription invoicing but not invoicing against monthly sales reports the client submits themselves.
20.8.1 requires the system to recommend optimal subscription plans and 20.1.5 to configure from onboarding selections, which together oblige a recommended model and tier package from onboarding data.
20.4.1 requires a marketplace of available modules and 20.4.2 that customers can browse them, which is what listing optional add-on modules asks for.
20.8.2 requires the system to recommend marketplace modules, which is the AI-driven module recommendation this requirement asks for.
The marketplace rows cover catalogue, discovery, pricing, activation and removal but nothing obliges module dependency and compatibility checking before allowing a combination.
20.1.1 requires self-service customer registration, which obliges creating the prospect's account credentials on submission so they can access their proposal.
Nothing obliges prospects to submit contact details and a trade license as proof they represent a real venue before portal access.
Nothing obliges TICVAI review and validation of a prospect's submitted documents before customer portal access is granted.
adjudicator_note: Source motivates this as protection of pricing strategy from competitors; worth a security/access ruling at sign-off.

rationale: The matrix obliges self-service onboarding and automatic configuration but not self-service visibility of pricing and subscription purchase without sales involvement.
Nothing obliges keeping large prospects on a sales-assisted path or withholding enterprise-tier pricing from self-service.
20.7.3 and 20.7.1 oblige payment method management and invoicing but not a purchase-agreement stage capturing billing cycle, contract period, invoicing frequency and legal entity information.
20.1.2 obliges automatic trial environment provisioning but not a pre-configured demo containing sample products, a working cash/card sales flow, performance and resource products, and reporting.
20.5.1 obliges license generation but not tenant provisioning triggered by finalisation of contractual terms.
19.1.13 requires enabling and disabling application modules and 20.1.5 automatic configuration from onboarding selections, which is the basic tenant setup reflecting tier and contracted modules.
Nothing obliges an end-to-end pre-go-live configuration validation covering product setup, pricing display and a full test transaction in the target environment.
20.6.7 requires usage dashboards, which obliges tracking a live client's actual usage against their subscribed tier and model.
20.6.7 obliges usage dashboards but not tracking of entitlement/license inventory consumption such as how many licensed POS terminals are actively in use.
20.8.4 recommends subscription upgrades and 20.6.8 raises threshold alerts, but neither obliges identifying overage requiring additional billing.
20.7.1 and 20.7.4 oblige invoicing and automated recurring billing but not consolidation of metered consumption and overage charges into the cycle invoice.
20.2.4 obliges automatic renewals and 20.5.7 license renewals, but a manual renewal/contract-review path is not required.
The matrix manages subscription plans and usage dashboards but obliges no licensing command-center overview board reporting total customers and active subscriptions by tier.
The matrix supports the individual licensing models but obliges no monthly-recurring-revenue breakdown by pricing model.
20.7.5 maintains billing history but the matrix obliges no per-customer billing view showing minimum billable volume month-to-date and variable/overage revenue.
The matrix holds licensing and billing data but obliges no consolidated customer profile view of a client's full commercial and licensing information.
The matrix obliges usage dashboards but no tier-distribution view showing customer count per tier.
The matrix obliges usage dashboards and configurable plans but no subscription-revenue-by-tier metric.
The matrix obliges usage dashboards but no tier and conversion trend series over time.
20.2.4 and 20.8.5 oblige renewals and cost-optimization recommendations but no renewal & retention center flagging upcoming renewals and at-risk accounts.
8.9.6 obliges monitoring of device and infrastructure health but does not settle whether server/infrastructure monitoring is a platform module or stays outside the product.
adjudicator_note: Recorded as an open decision in the source; needs a scope ruling at sign-off.

rationale: This is a delivery-phasing decision deferring forecasting AI out of phase one, not a requirement on the system.
adjudicator_note: It qualifies the delivery date of the matrix's forecasting rows (8.2.55, 8.2.56, 21.11.4); the phasing should be recorded against those rows at sign-off.

rationale: 2.7.35 requires use of the base system currency and 2.9.1 that sales are always finalised in local currency, which is storing and reconciling in the configured base currency.
Foreign currency may be accepted and settled locally with configured rates, but recording the local-currency equivalent at the rate in force at the moment of transaction is not obliged.
4.6.11 requires refunds and negative sales to be given in local currency while foreign currency is accepted, which is the change and refund rule stated.

adjudicator_note: The candidate text is truncated at 'Foreign Cu'; confirm that entry is the foreign-currency transactions report before closing this row.

rationale: Transactions are performed in the base currency and exchange rates are managed, but freezing the converted value at purchase against later rate movement is not stated.
22.10.22 requires a CMS for the mobile app and 1.4.7 publication to both Website and Mobile App, but nothing obliges the website and app to share one CMS and publishing back end.
Tenant-specific branding, content and features are required, but nothing obliges a per-tenant app carrying the tenant's full product and venue data end to end.
Modules are licensable and tenant-specific features are supported, but nothing obliges a tenant to hide an unused module such as Dining or Retail from the surfaces it appears on.
3.2.1 requires a single barcode that grants park entry and a meal voucher among other entitlements, which is the combined ticket-plus-meal code.
3.2.1 puts entry and meal voucher on one code and 3.2.76 validates that code in real time at entry points, so the same code is scanned at the gate and at the counter.
3.2.20 requires a ticket's status to be updated once redeemed so used tickets are tracked, and 2.16.8 requires validation and redemption control on vouchers.
adjudicator_note: 3.2.20 requires the status change but does not say in words that a second presentation is refused; worth stating explicitly at sign-off.

rationale: Group bookings are supported and every ticket gets a unique code, but a single shared group QR redeemed once for the whole party is not obliged.
Per-ticket codes and guest profiles both exist, but nothing requires a member of a group to link their own ticket to their own profile from the mobile app.
Entitlement consumption is tracked across ticketing, retail and F&B and a transaction may mix tenders, but one shared cart and checkout spanning the three modules is not obliged.
2.16.8 requires each order to generate a single QR code and 3.2.1 requires that one barcode to carry entry, meal and other entitlements, which is the unified receipt and code.
A unified wallet across channels and multi-location inventory are obliged but one venue-level inventory pool serving web, mobile, kiosk and POS is not.
Location-scoped stock and inter-venue transfers imply per-venue stock, but the default that stock is not shared across venues is never stated.
15.5.3 requires inter-venue transfers, which is exactly the capability to move stock between venues.
No candidate states that sale availability is gated on the destination venue's system-recorded stock rather than its physical count, which is the rule that keeps transfers safe to sell against.
Add-on purchases and a single barcode carrying several entitlements are required, but not the workflow of scanning an existing ticket to attach the add-on to the code the guest already holds.
The app is required to show real-time wait times, but consuming the venue's own external wait-time feed as the source of them is not obliged.
19.2.83 gives the app a digital companion mode, but no candidate requires a next-ride recommendation driven by live wait-time data.
adjudicator_note: The source itself defers this to a future phase.

rationale: 2.1.18 links POS and kiosk devices to device management for monitoring, but a workstation overview dashboard listing every configured workstation for a venue or across venues is not obliged.
Nothing requires the workstation list to be grouped by department and sub-department.
16.4.18 and 16.4.20 require device health and status monitoring and 2.1.18 requires connectivity to be monitored per workstation, which is the online/offline/health status.
Device Management monitors status, location, version, connectivity, errors, paper levels and assigned workstation, but the workstation's type is not among the attributes carried or displayed.
Workstations exist as an assignment on a device but a workstation setup capturing name, auto-generated ID, department and mode is not obliged.

Device status, location, software version and IP restriction exist separately, but the workstation detail view combining configuration, linked devices, operator and shift activity and sales totals is not obliged.
The POS may connect to a receipt printer, cash drawer and ticket printer but a management surface configuring each peripheral against a named workstation is not obliged.
16.4.20 requires device status monitoring, which is the device-level status shown on the hardware screen.
Device health is monitored per device but nothing aggregates it into a live department-level health overview.
2.1.18 captures device location but no candidate requires a graphical park-map plotting workstations with their live status.
No candidate requires manual drag-and-drop placement of workstations as a fallback where the venue cannot supply clean zone and region metadata.
adjudicator_note: Depends on the park-map view, which is itself not in the matrix.

rationale: 16.6.32 requires software version records and 16.6.33 software update management, which is version and pending or completed update tracking per workstation.
Shift reports carry totals per payment type, but a till and cash management view showing total cash and card transactions is not obliged as its own surface.
5.9.6 requires an alert when expected and actual till values differ and 5.9.2 requires over-shorts to be captured and recorded, which is variance tracking on the till.
5.8.8 requires mid-day withdrawal from a cashier's float to be traced and 5.8.4 modification of the initial fund, which is cash-in and cash-out for mid-shift pickups.
Employee shifts are managed and viewable, but shift assignment and scheduling organised by cashier and department for POS operation is not obliged.
1.2.80 makes staffing rules and approvals configurable but no candidate requires reusable shift templates or shift policies.
5.9.1 requires shift closing and register close-out and 5.9.5 automatic session closing, which is the opening and closing of shifts.
5.9.6 requires an alert on a till exception and 5.9.5 supervisor notification on session close, which is the exception and alert handling on shifts.
This records a suggestion to explore merging two screens to reduce dashboard count, not a requirement the system must meet.

rationale: No candidate requires a POS profile and layout surface linking each department to its workstation types and counts.

6.1.75 lists a daily operations summary report, but a venue-level dashboard aggregating the department views into one overview is not obliged.
This is instruction to the design team about how to treat the wireframes and the matrix, not behaviour required of the system.

rationale: Synchronisation of cross-region-valid entitlements between separate regional databases is a replication requirement no candidate carries.

This records a project deliverable - a hosted reference tool being built for the client to validate against - not behaviour required of the system.

rationale: No candidate obliges infrastructure monitoring or utilisation-based scale-up triggers; the utilisation rows are business reporting, not capacity management.

rationale: No candidate obliges a staged ticket configuration flow of basic information, ticket type configuration, validation and publish.

rationale: 1.1.1 obliges selling open-dated tickets and 1.1.9 the mandatory-use-by validity that makes them date-free, which is the ticket type asked for.

2.6.35 obliges the money card as a loadable wallet product and 5.12.23 to 5.12.25 its load, usage and cash-out accounting.

1.1.3 obliges creating timeslots for a whole day or a period with capacity each and 1.1.86 performance date-time validity, which is recurring performances.

rationale: Rescheduling to a policy is obliged, but configurable time windows within which upgrade, reschedule and cancellation are permitted are not.

The matrix does not oblige a demand versus supply chart plotting forecast demand, planned supply and actual usage by month.

The matrix generates stock shortage alerts but does not oblige a stockout-risk item list on the planning dashboard with a drill-down.
The matrix supports safety stock levels but does not oblige a below-safety-stock alert row with a drill-down on the planning dashboard.
The matrix requires demand forecasting but not an exception list of items with high forecast variance.

The matrix requires inventory demand forecasting but does not oblige the By Item Category, By Item and By Location views.

The matrix requires forecast accuracy measurement but not the Forecast Accuracy, Total Forecast (AED) and Total Forecast Qty tiles with period-on-period change.

The matrix requires reorder recommendations but not the KPI tiles Items Requiring Replenishment, Total Reorder Qty, Total Reorder Value and Avg Lead Time.

The matrix does not oblige the ROP alert bands, in particular the Near ROP band, or their counts.
The matrix does not oblige a drill-down from the summary to the full reorder point list.
No matrix row obliges a planning calendar; a scheduling surface for planning work is missing entirely.

No matrix row obliges scheduled planning events such as Forecast Run, Replenishment Review, Stock Review or Planning Cycle.
No matrix row obliges planning event types (Automated Job, Meeting, Review, Action) or their colour legend.
No matrix row obliges adding an event to a planning calendar.

rationale: No matrix row obliges scenario outputs - forecast demand, required supply, projected stockouts and additional investment measured against a base case.
No matrix row obliges a comparison of base, high-season and worst-case demand scenarios.
No matrix row obliges a scenario summary table or the scenario detail behind it.
The matrix provides generic approval dashboards but does not oblige replenishment plans as an approvable object with submitted, pending, approved and rejected counts.
The matrix does not specify a recent plans list with Plan No., Type, Total Value, Submitted On, Status and Action.
The matrix nowhere names the plan types Replenishment Plan, Seasonal Plan, Emergency Plan and Quarterly Plan.
11.1.16 requires approval dashboards showing pending, approved and rejected requests, which obliges those states on an approvable plan.
The matrix omits the actions to list all plans and to create a new plan.
8.2.18 requires forecast accuracy measurements, which is substantially this accuracy readout; the gauge and qualitative band are presentation.
The matrix requires forecast accuracy measurement but does not name the statistical measures MAPE, Bias, MAD and Tracking Signal.
The matrix does not oblige a monthly accuracy trend, which requires accuracy to be retained over time.
The matrix does not oblige accuracy broken down by category or the accuracy report behind it.
The matrix requires demand forecasting but not an AI demand intelligence surface with a generated insights panel.
The matrix forecasts demand and seasonal demand but does not oblige a forward insight combining historical trends with upcoming events over a 60-day horizon.
The matrix alerts on shortages but does not oblige a predictive run-out insight over a 10-day horizon.
No matrix row obliges price forecasting for purchased items; predicting a price increase over the next 30 days is a capability the matrix never asks for.
The matrix requires procurement recommendations but not an order consolidation insight quantified as a saving percentage.
The matrix does not oblige a view of all AI insights from this screen.
15.4.1 requires the system to forecast inventory demand, which is substantially this forward demand curve; the 60-day window is presentation detail.
The matrix requires demand forecasting but omits confidence level, risk level and a recommended action against the forecast.
adjudicator_note: Candidate 8.2.17 is attendance forecast confidence, a different forecast subject.

rationale: The matrix identifies slow-moving inventory and safety stock but does not oblige planning exceptions to be aggregated into a typed summary.

The matrix nowhere defines the planning exception classes Stockout Risk, Below Safety Stock, High Variance, Slow Moving Items and No Forecast.
The matrix does not oblige a High / Medium / Low priority on a planning exception.
Nothing among the candidates obliges a branded retail management application shell; the branding rows offered govern the guest mobile app, not an operator console.
A navigation section heading grouping the retail screens is presentation structure that no candidate requires and none plausibly would.
Configurable dashboards for sales and operations are obliged, but the matrix does not name a retail overview screen within the retail application.
No candidate obliges retail store configuration at all, so neither the capability nor its navigation entry is covered.
adjudicator_note: Store master configuration for retail looks genuinely missing from the matrix rather than merely unmatched by these candidates.

rationale: Product and pricing creation is obliged in the product lifecycle domain, but no row requires a retail products and pricing board reachable from this navigation rail.
POS selling is obliged in its own domains, but no row requires a POS and sales board within this retail application navigation.
In-store inventory recording and inventory lookup are obliged, but no row requires an inventory and stock board within this retail application navigation.
Retail promotions are obliged in their own domain, but no row requires a promotions and channels board within this retail application navigation.
Configurable dashboards for sales and operations are obliged, but no row requires an analytics and AI board within this retail application navigation.
A navigation section heading grouping the operational modules is presentation structure no candidate requires and none plausibly would.
F&B capability is obliged across its own domains, but no row requires an F&B Management module to be reachable from this application navigation rail.
adjudicator_note: The 20.4.x candidates are subscription module marketplace rows and match only on the word module; do not trace module navigation to them.

rationale: Missing: any requirement on the back-office navigation shell, that each functional module such as Ticketing is reachable as a named entry in a left navigation rail.
adjudicator_note: Candidates matched only on the word module from the licensing marketplace rows, which concern installing and activating modules, not navigating to them.

rationale: An entire resource management subdomain is obliged, so only its presence as a navigable module in this application is unstated.
Guest profile and preference management is obliged, but no row requires a Guest Management module to be reachable from this application navigation rail.
Loyalty and membership capability is obliged, but no row requires a Loyalty and Membership module to be reachable from this application navigation rail.
A navigation section heading grouping the administration screens is presentation structure no candidate requires and none plausibly would.

7.1.12 requires configurable role-based access control with permissions grouped into roles and assigned to users, and 7.1.28 requires reporting on users, roles and permissions, which is this administration screen.
adjudicator_note: 7.1.12 was offered on an earlier row rather than this one, but it is the governing obligation.

rationale: Configurable approval workflows are obliged but no row requires an approval centre inside the retail administration area.
Complete audit logs must be maintained, but the matrix does not oblige an administrative screen through which an operator can browse them.
No candidate obliges a general system settings administration screen; configuration obligations are scattered through the matrix feature by feature with no consolidated settings surface.
Users hold roles under 7.1.12, but the matrix does not require the signed-in user, their role title and an online presence indicator to be shown in the navigation rail.
8.9.1 requires a centralised real-time operational dashboard explicitly spanning retail and POS, and 8.9.8 requires real-time monitoring of retail sales and transaction performance.
7.1.53 requires per-tenant authorisation policies but nothing obliges a tenant selector on an operational board or the cross-tenant aggregation that an all-tenants default implies.
adjudicator_note: Same architectural question as MOM-6163: whether any role may view across tenants, and how all-tenants aggregates are computed.

rationale: 8.9.2 obliges display across parks and venues but does not require a park filter with an all-parks default on the board header.
Historical operational performance analysis is obliged, but the matrix does not require a business-date selector that re-bases a real-time board onto a chosen trading day.
Drill-down analytics are obliged but not a time-granularity selector offering a day-level aggregation on the command centre.
Real-time monitoring is obliged, but the matrix never states a refresh cadence or requires an operator-triggered refresh of the board.
adjudicator_note: Refresh behaviour is unstated across the whole board set and should be fixed once at sign-off.

rationale: The operational dashboard is obliged but not an AI insights entry point from it; 5.3.25 generates AI insights about guests, not retail operations.
Real-time retail sales monitoring is obliged, but no row requires the day-total tile or the prior-day baseline needed for a versus-yesterday percentage.
adjudicator_note: The versus-yesterday comparison recurs across every tile on this board; the retained prior-day figures behind it are obliged nowhere.

rationale: Transaction performance monitoring is obliged but not a transaction count tile with a versus-yesterday change.
Sales and transaction monitoring are obliged but not the derived average transaction value or its day-over-day movement.
6.1.10 reports units sold in the daily transaction summary, but the matrix does not require it as a live command-centre tile with a versus-yesterday change.
Open, closed and maintenance status of service locations is obliged, but not an aggregate count of open stores against yesterday.
Device information appears on the operational dashboard, but no row obliges an active-terminals-out-of-total POS availability tile.
Out-of-stock alerting is obliged, but the matrix does not require a stock-out item count surfaced as a command-centre tile with a daily movement.
Low-stock alerting against configurable thresholds is obliged, but not a low-stock item count tile with a daily movement.
Inventory and inter-venue transfers are obliged, but nothing requires outstanding transfers to be counted and shown on the command centre.
Operational alerts and KPI alerts are obliged, but no row requires an open-alert count tile on the retail command centre.
KPI monitoring is obliged but the matrix never fixes a comparison baseline, so the retained prior-day figures every tile is measured against, and their consistency across tiles, are unspecified.
adjudicator_note: This is the architectural form of the versus-yesterday deltas seen on MOM-4470 to MOM-4479 and on MOM-6078; settle the baseline once.

rationale: Retail sales monitoring and location status are obliged, but no row requires a per-store snapshot table carrying sales, transactions, average transaction value, active POS, stock health and status together.
In-store inventory is recorded per store, but the matrix has no concept of a store typology distinguishing gift shop, merchandise store, souvenir shop, retail kiosk and photo shop.
Low-stock and out-of-stock alerting exists per item, but the matrix does not roll those signals up into a healthy, warning or critical stock health state per store.
8.9.4 requires the operational status of service locations including open, closed, maintenance and restricted, which is this per-store status.
adjudicator_note: 8.9.4 was offered on neighbouring rows rather than this one but is plainly the governing obligation.

rationale: Consolidated retail reporting is obliged but no row requires an estate total and average footer aggregating sales, transactions, ATV and active POS across stores.
Nothing among the candidates obliges creation or maintenance of a store as a master-data entity, which is the same missing capability as MOM-4445.
adjudicator_note: Store master data underpins most of this board; confirm whether it sits in a part of the matrix these candidates never reach.

rationale: Devices can be assigned to users and locations and permissions can be scoped to a POS terminal, but registering a new terminal from the retail command centre is not obliged.
Device inventory and assignment are obliged in the device management domain, but not as an action available from this board.
In-store stock viewing and reconciliation are obliged, but no row requires a drill-through from the command centre into stock detail.
4.5.14 requires inventory transfers between locations with approval workflows, which is the transfer this action raises.
Alerts are obliged as part of operational dashboards but not a drill-through from the board into the alert list.
Operational alerts exist, but the matrix does not require a chronological alert feed on the board with per-alert timestamps and a count-bearing link to all alerts.
Device health monitoring and kiosk supervision exist, but no row obliges an operational alert when a named POS terminal drops offline.
Device health monitoring is obliged, but an alert on a payment device at a given store going offline is not required anywhere.
4.4.17 requires automatic out-of-stock alerts against configurable thresholds, which is this alert counting a store out-of-stock lines.
Inventory transfers with approval are obliged, but nothing requires transfers to be timed against an expectation and alerted when they run late.
Real-time or timed product synchronisation and integration health monitoring are obliged, but no row requires a failed inventory sync for a named store to raise an operational alert.
Product and price synchronisation and configurable alerting both exist, but a failed price sync raising an alert that counts the affected products at a named store is not obliged.
4.4.17 requires automatic low-stock alerts on configurable thresholds and 15.1.3 requires SKU management, so a tester would check exactly this product-level alert.
No candidate obliges store opening hours or a planned opening time, so there is nothing against which a delayed store opening could be detected or alerted.
Real-time retail sales monitoring and consolidated outlet reporting are obliged, but the matrix does not require an intraday actual-against-forecast sales curve for retail.
Drill-down analytics are obliged but not day, week and month period toggles on the sales trend chart.
adjudicator_note: The day-of-week access, pricing and forecasting candidates match only on the word day and are unrelated.

rationale: Sales monitoring is obliged but not point-level inspection of the chart returning actual and forecast values at a chosen time.
The matrix says nothing about chart axis treatment, so the currency value axis and the full twenty-four hour time axis are unobliged presentation detail.

The untruncated 4.4.9 obliges multi-store retailing with stores connected to each other's inventory, and 4.5.13 inventory across multiple locations, so stores do exist as first-class entities; what the matrix still omits is a management surface for stores and selling locations.
adjudicator_note: Verdict raised from Absent: the full 4.4.9 shows the matrix does require multi-store operation, not merely presume it.

rationale: With no store register obliged anywhere, free-text search across stores has nothing to search.
No candidate requires a store list, so filtering over it is unobliged.
The store register and therefore its columns (name, code, type, park or venue, status, actions) are required by no candidate row.
Nothing obliges a unique business code identifying each store, which is the key the rest of the retail board joins on.
adjudicator_note: 3.1.2 and 7.4.20 concern unique codes on tickets, not stores; do not trace store identity to them.

rationale: No candidate defines a store type taxonomy covering gift shop, merchandise store, souvenir shop, retail kiosk, photo shop, pop-up store and event store.
Parks and venues exist as concepts and multi-store retailing is obliged, but no candidate read in full requires a store to be associated with the park or venue that contains it.
8.9.4 requires service locations to carry an operational status including open and closed, which is the status shown against each store.
adjudicator_note: 8.9.4 was offered on other rows of this board rather than this one.

rationale: Viewing and editing a store record is unobliged because no candidate requires the store record itself.
No candidate requires a store list surface, so its pagination and the stated visible range and total have nothing behind them.
A selectable page size on the store list has no matrix obligation behind it.
Nothing among the candidates obliges a create or edit form for a retail store and its operational settings.
No candidate obliges the store record to carry general, inventory, commerce, channel and device sections.
A mandatory store name field is unobliged because the store entity itself is unobliged.
A mandatory store code field is unobliged; the same gap as the store code data item in MOM-4509.
A mandatory store type chosen from a controlled list is unobliged, since the matrix defines no store type list.
A free-text store description has no matrix obligation behind it.
Requiring the owning park on the store record is unobliged, as is the store-to-park association generally.
Capturing the venue within the park on a store record has no matrix obligation behind it.
Zones exist for access control and seating, but no candidate obliges a store to record the zone or area it occupies.
A mandatory active or inactive status on the store record is unobliged; 5.7.37 governs account status, not stores.
No candidate obliges an image to be held against a store record or replaced through the editor.
Saving or abandoning the store editor is unobliged because the editor itself is unobliged.
Reusable templates are obliged for tickets, policies, accreditations and devices but for no retail store equivalent, so a store type and template library is missing.
adjudicator_note: 1.1.16, 3.3.23 and 16.3.15 show the template pattern the matrix uses elsewhere; a store template row would sit naturally beside them.

rationale: Creating a new store template has no matrix obligation behind it, since store templates are not required at all.
Returns and exchanges, promotions and split payments are obliged individually, but the matrix does not let a store be provisioned from a full-store capability profile.
Barcode management and scanning are obliged, but no row defines a kiosk store profile limiting catalogue, payment types and inventory scope.
Mobile POS devices and mobile operations are obliged, but the matrix does not define a mobile cart profile combining limited inventory, cashless payment and assigned staff.
Date-driven product activation and retirement exist, but nothing obliges an event store profile with temporary pricing, temporary stock and operation confined to the event period.
Digital assets are catalogued and owned, but the matrix does not link a guest photo asset to a saleable print product or oblige print fulfilment at a photo shop.
Store templates are not required at all in the candidates, so a count of stores using each template has nothing to attach to.
Adding a further store template is unobliged because store templates themselves are unobliged.
Operating hours, blackout and special opening hours are configurable for venues and queues, but no row obliges a retail store to carry its own weekly schedule and special calendar.
The matrix does not separate a weekly recurring schedule, a special-date calendar and defined sales periods as distinct configurations for a store.
Operating hours are configurable in general, but the matrix never scopes a schedule to a chosen store.
adjudicator_note: Store scoping depends on the missing store master data flagged at MOM-4505.

rationale: Operating hours are configurable for queues and access rules, but no candidate obliges a store operating-hours schedule that can be copied to other stores.
Operating hours are configurable but the matrix does not specify a per-day open time, close time and trading status as the schedule model.
Day-specific opening configuration is illustrated for venue slots but not required for retail stores, so per-weekday opening and closing times are unobliged.
adjudicator_note: 3.3.16 and 8.5.7 score highest on the phrase day of week but govern access rules and pricing, not trading hours.

rationale: The matrix does not require individual days to be switched on or off within a store trading week.
Blackout periods are configurable for venue operations, but mid-day breaks or ad hoc closures within a store schedule are not obliged.
16.1.1 requires device registration, 16.2.10 assignment of devices to users and locations and 16.8.41 POS device integration, which together are this POS and device assignment surface.
Device categorisation is obliged, but the matrix does not require POS terminals and supporting peripherals to be managed as separate populations.
2.1.18 obliges monitoring of device status, location, software version and connectivity, but not a terminal register listing name, code, type, status and last synchronisation.

The untruncated 1.1.133 names Counter POS, Self-service kiosk and Mobile POS as channels, but they appear there as donation sales channels, not as a POS terminal type taxonomy the device record must carry.
16.4.19 requires device connectivity monitoring and 2.1.18 requires POS and kiosk connectivity to be visible to administrators, which is this online or offline state.
Device status monitoring is obliged, but the matrix does not require the time of each terminal last successful synchronisation to be recorded and shown.
A device inventory must be maintained, but no row obliges a drill-through from this board panel into the full POS and device list.
Products can be assigned to sales channels, but the matrix does not oblige a channel configuration surface governing how and where each channel sells.
Channel assignment exists, but a per-channel catalogue, price book, inventory source and fulfilment method are not part of any obliged data model.

The full 1.1.133 does enumerate counter POS, self-service kiosk, online portal, mobile POS and third-party channels, but it does not fix this retail channel set and Event POS in particular is unnamed.
Date-driven activation exists for products, but the matrix does not give a sales channel its own active or scheduled lifecycle state.
Products can be assigned to channels, but the matrix has no notion of distinct per-channel catalogues bound to a channel configuration.

rationale: Segment-specific prices are obliged, but the matrix does not define price books as objects bound to a sales channel.
In-store and multi-location inventory are obliged, but nothing requires a channel to be bound to a nominated inventory source, and event stock is not a recognised source at all.

The previously cut tail of 2.1.33 does oblige fulfilment workflows including pickup, delivery and collection at designated retail locations, but only for the kiosk channel and not as a fulfilment mode declared per sales channel.
adjudicator_note: Improved traceability: 2.1.33's fulfilment-workflow clause was hidden by the 260-character cut.

rationale: Sales channels are configurable and reportable but no row obliges a full channel management surface behind the board panel.
Automatic and warehouse replenishment are obliged, but the matrix does not require inventory sources and replenishment rules to be configured per store.
Stock is held per location, but nominating one location as a store primary stock source is not obliged.
Warehouse replenishment and warehouse locations are obliged, but the matrix does not require a store to be bound to the warehouse that replenishes it.
Replenishment is obliged from a warehouse, but a fallback or emergency stock source for a store is not required anywhere.
Replenishment and auto-replenishment are obliged but no row names a min/max replenishment strategy as a selectable mode.
4.5.6 requires requisitions to be raised automatically when stock reaches its minimum and 15.4.4 requires automatic replenishment, which is this switch.
Minimum stock, safety stock and reorder point management are each obliged and 4.5.6 adds par stock, so a tester would check exactly these replenishment rules.
adjudicator_note: Only the per-store scoping of these rules is assumed rather than stated; it follows from multi-location inventory at 15.1.10.

rationale: The full 7.1.12 makes roles configurable and 4.8.10 shows approval gates exist, but no row requires replenishment to be gated by an approval assigned to a store manager role.
Replenishment is managed but the matrix does not require a retained replenishment history viewable from the configuration screen.
Tenant-scoped authorisation policies are obliged, but nothing requires tenant-level retail configuration as a governed settings surface.

Retail configuration exists piecemeal across the matrix but no row groups it into commerce, returns, inventory, pricing, approvals, devices, notifications, offline and audit sections, nor requires those settings to exist as a set.
Multiple currencies are handled in transactions, reporting and refunds, but a tenant-level default currency setting is obliged nowhere.
2.9.12 obliges tax inclusive, exclusive and exempt treatment per product, but not a tenant-wide default tax handling setting.
No candidate obliges configurable price rounding or decimal precision for retail prices.
Printing a receipt and sharing it by email are obliged, but not a configurable default combination applied at every sale.
Unified guest identification is obliged, but the matrix does not let its strictness at the point of sale be configured as optional, required or skipped.
Offline POS operation is obliged and 2.3.1 even requires the offline feature set to be defined, but no row allows offline selling to be permitted or forbidden per tenant.
The full 2.3.1 defines the offline functional envelope and its reconciliation but sets no configurable ceiling on the number of transactions accepted while offline.
The matrix requires offline operation and local policy evaluation generally, but never obliges a local product cache on the retail POS as the mechanism.
Offline operation is required in the abstract but a local price cache, and the price-staleness question it raises, is not obliged anywhere in the candidates.
The matrix requires offline operation but omits a local inventory cache and therefore says nothing about stock accuracy while disconnected.
2.1.30 obliges remote management of device and POS settings but names no explicit save action that commits a global retail settings screen.
Missing: any requirement on how back-office boards are grouped and labelled in the navigation shell, here under an Overview heading.
Missing: the existence of a named Product and Catalog board as a navigable screen; the matrix describes catalogue capability but never the board that carries it.
adjudicator_note: The content of this board is adjudicated in its own rows; this row concerns only its presence in the navigation rail.

rationale: Missing: navigation-state behaviour, that the rail indicates which board the user is currently on.

The matrix obliges dashboards with drill-down but names no tenant, park, date and granularity scoping controls, which also determine how board data must be partitioned.
18.10.1 provides an employee AI assistant but does not oblige an assistant entry point embedded in the retail product and catalogue board.
Catalogue data and a central dashboard are obliged, but no candidate requires a Total Products KPI tile or the day-over-day comparison it displays.
adjudicator_note: Every vs-Yesterday delta on this pack implies day-level historical snapshots of catalogue counts; the matrix obliges no such retention.

rationale: SKU management is obliged by 4.4.10 but not an Active SKUs headline metric with a change-versus-yesterday figure.
The matrix obliges catalogue management but never a count of active catalogues surfaced as a board KPI tile.
4.4.10 obliges product status management but no candidate requires a published-product count to be surfaced as a board KPI tile with a daily delta.
Product status management is obliged but the matrix never requires draft products to be counted and shown on the catalogue board.
The matrix obliges pricing to be part of catalogue data but nowhere requires products without a price to be detected and counted as an exception KPI.
Pricing thresholds and retail margin analytics exist, but no candidate obliges a low-margin product count computed against a threshold and shown as a board tile.
11.1.67 obliges KPI dashboards for approval workflows generally but does not tie a pending-product-approval count to the retail catalogue board.
Future-dated pricing schedules are obliged, but the matrix requires no count of pending future-dated product changes surfaced as a board metric.
Centralised catalogue management is obliged but not a catalogue-level status table carrying name, type, scope, status, product count and last-updated.
The matrix obliges catalogue management but defines no catalogue typology of global, park, seasonal, event and segment catalogues.
The untruncated 4.4.9 obliges multi-store retailing and 4.4.10 centralised catalogue management, but nothing scopes a catalogue to all stores or to a named store group.
4.4.10 obliges product status management but not published/scheduled/draft states at catalogue level, and in particular not scheduled publication.
The matrix leaves out the per-catalogue product count and last-updated timestamp that the status table is required to display.
Catalogue management is obliged but not a drill-through from the board summary into the full catalogue list.
The matrix obliges the catalogue data fields but no configuration-health view that detects and counts outstanding catalogue data-quality issues.
adjudicator_note: Closest lexical candidate 8.9.6 is device and infrastructure health, a different subject from catalogue configuration health.

rationale: Barcode is obliged as a catalogue field but no candidate requires completeness to be checked or missing-barcode SKUs to be counted.
4.4.10 carries pricing on the product record but obliges no exception report counting products that hold no active price.
Centralised catalogue management is obliged but not the orphan check that counts products belonging to no catalogue.
No candidate obliges a product-to-inventory-item mapping to exist, let alone a count of products where that mapping is missing.
Margin analytics exist and 4.3.28 shows configurable thresholds are a matrix pattern, but no row obliges a margin floor whose breach count and threshold value are both displayed.
Pricing approval workflows and approval KPI dashboards are both obliged; only the specific count of scheduled price changes awaiting approval on this board is left out.
Images are obliged as a catalogue field but no candidate requires missing images to be detected and counted.
Nothing in the candidates obliges a data-quality issue list, so the drill-through from the health panel into it is unaddressed too.
4.4.23 obliges retail analytics covering revenue, margins, top-selling products and category performance, and 6.1.10 adds units sold, which together is exactly the table's five columns.
