adjudicator_note: The named products in the source are illustrative demo data, not a required product list.

rationale: Drill-down analytics are obliged in general but no candidate names a product-performance detail view reachable from the catalogue board.
4.4.23 covers category performance by sales, not catalogue composition, so the split of product counts by category with a total is not obliged.
Category is obliged as a catalogue field but the matrix fixes no retail category set and no requirement to report catalogue composition against it.
adjudicator_note: The seven category names in the source read as configured reference data rather than a fixed taxonomy.

rationale: The matrix obliges categories as catalogue data but not a navigable category list reached from the board.
4.4.10 requires centralised catalogue management of retail products and 15.1.3 requires SKU management, which is what this master screen is asked to do.
4.4.10 obliges centralised catalogue management including product lifecycle control, which necessarily includes creating a new product.
Barcode scanning and SKU management are obliged, but no candidate requires the master screen to be searchable by product name, SKU or barcode.
The matrix obliges catalogue management but names no filtering of the product list by its attributes.
The untruncated 7.4.12 gives product code and name and 4.4.10 gives category and status management, so only Brand is unnamed and would have to ride on configurable product attributes.
4.4.10 explicitly names images among the centrally managed retail product data.
4.4.11 requires size and colour variants each with independent SKU, barcode, inventory and pricing, and 15.1.8 adds status, which is the whole column set of this list.
15.1.8 requires active and inactive product statuses, which is exactly the status the SKU row carries.
Catalogue management is obliged but not the drill-through from the summary card into the full product detail record.
15.1.5 and 15.1.6 together require configurable product attributes and product variants, which is what this screen is asked to define.
Attributes, variants and RFID are each obliged separately but the matrix says nothing about presenting them as three tabs of one configuration screen.
15.1.5 requires configurable product attributes and 4.4.11 names size explicitly as a variant axis, so a Size attribute group with its value list is required.
4.4.11 names colour as a supported variant axis and 15.1.5 makes its value list configurable.
15.1.5 requires configurable product attributes, which is precisely what an Adult/Kids gender grouping is an instance of.
4.4.11 names material explicitly among the supported variant attributes.
Attributes being configurable under 15.1.5 means new attribute groups can be added, which is the whole of this requirement.
Variant SKUs and automatic SKU generation are obliged but no row requires a colour-by-size matrix as the surface that generates the full combination set.
4.4.12 obliges barcode assignment, printing and scanning but never lets the barcode symbology, such as EAN-13, be chosen per SKU.
4.4.11 gives each variant an independent barcode and 4.4.12 obliges its assignment, which is this requirement.
RFID integration is obliged at warehouse level but nothing makes RFID a per-SKU switch, so mixed tagged and untagged catalogues are unaddressed.
RFID integration is required but no row defines an EPC identifier stored against the SKU, leaving the tag encoding scheme undetermined.
Variant and attribute management is obliged but not a drill-through to it from the summary configuration panel.
4.4.10 gives products a category but the matrix nowhere obliges a multi-level category and brand hierarchy for merchandise.
adjudicator_note: The candidates matched the word hierarchy from the Accounting chart-of-accounts rows, which are unrelated to product categorisation.

rationale: Category exists as a product field but the matrix obliges neither a category tree maintenance view nor brand as a managed entity alongside supplier.
The matrix requires no nested category structure and no rolled-up product count per node, so the tree view has no requirement behind it.
4.4.10 obliges category as centrally managed catalogue data, which necessarily carries a category name.
The matrix obliges categories but gives them no stable code of their own, which matters for integration and reporting keys.
A parent-category pointer is what makes the hierarchy real, and no candidate obliges one for retail categories.
adjudicator_note: Candidate 5.7.41 is parent-child accounts in the chart of accounts, not product categories.

rationale: The matrix names no descriptive text field on the category record.
Margin analytics and pricing thresholds exist, but the matrix does not let a target margin be set per category, which is what the board's low-margin exception counts against.
No candidate obliges a merchandising display order on the category, so presentation sequence is left to implementation.
15.1.8 gives products an active/inactive status but nothing gives the category record its own activation state.
Category data is obliged but not a dedicated category management workspace reached from this panel.
The matrix obliges centralised catalogue management and multi-store retailing but never the assortment decision of which products are sellable at which store or channel.
No candidate treats a catalogue as a selectable editable object, so choosing one to work on is unaddressed.
Catalogue management as an action on a named catalogue is not obliged; 4.4.10 covers only the product data inside it.
The matrix leaves out any product-by-location assortment grid, and with it the notion that a product is stocked at some selling locations and not others.
Nothing in the candidates obliges an include/exclude flag per product per selling location, which is the underlying assortment data model.
With no assortment requirement in the matrix, the drill-through into the full assortment has nothing behind it either.
The matrix obliges channel-based and customer-segment pricing but not a price-book screen that manages prices per store alongside channel and segment.
Dynamic Pricing rows gesture at pricing configuration but no candidate obliges a named, currency-scoped price book that can be selected as the working set.
The matrix requires pricing approval workflows but no candidate obliges create/edit/retire management of price books as first-class objects.
Channel and segment pricing exist as separate rows, but the matrix nowhere fixes the five-level precedence of base, park, store, channel and customer/member that decides which price wins.
adjudicator_note: Price resolution order is a data-model decision and is worth settling explicitly at sign-off rather than leaving to implementation.

rationale: Segment pricing, price lists and effective-from/to validity all appear separately, but no candidate obliges a per-SKU price grid carrying channel/store, segment, price, effective-from and status together.
5.12.11 gives validity periods to F&B revenue-recognition rules only; the matrix does not give price records themselves a status and an effective-from date.
Pricing thresholds and performance reporting are obliged, but the matrix does not require cost, current margin and proposed margin to be shown side by side when repricing a SKU.
adjudicator_note: Margin display depends on landed cost being available to the pricing screen; confirm the cost source at sign-off.

rationale: The matrix covers pricing management as a capability but not a drill-through from the summary pricing panel into the full pricing workspace.
4.4.20 requires combo products, bundles and kits with component-level inventory, and 3.5.8 requires per-component rules, which is exactly a bundle builder with component management.
Bundles are obliged as groupings of products but the matrix never gives the bundle its own price and status distinct from its components.
Component-level inventory and rules are obliged, but component quantity, component type and per-component price impact are not.
3.5.8 governs component availability and redemption but says nothing about components being required versus optional, which changes how a bundle is sold.
4.4.20 fixes component-level inventory consumption as the behaviour but does not make inventory behaviour a configurable choice per bundle.
Component availability is obliged but nothing sets the bundle's own availability across stores and online channels.
Bundles are obliged but not a bundle management workspace reachable from the builder summary.
4.4.10 obliges product data including images but no candidate obliges merchandising control over how a product is presented in a storefront.
Configurable attributes could carry the flag but the matrix nowhere obliges a featured-product marker or the merchandising behaviour it drives.
Configurable attributes could hold the flag, but no candidate obliges a bestseller marker or what it changes in the storefront.
The matrix names no new-arrival marker, nor any rule for how long a product keeps it.
A staff-pick merchandising flag is not obliged anywhere in the candidates.
4.4.11 knows edition as a variant axis but the matrix obliges no limited-edition merchandising flag on the product.
No candidate obliges a merchandising sequence for products, so display order is left undefined.
4.4.10 obliges product images but not a managed gallery with multiple images, ordering and a primary image.
The matrix obliges algorithmic cross-sell recommendations but never manually curated cross-sell products attached to a specific product record.
With no merchandising configuration obliged, the drill-through into a merchandising workspace is unaddressed as well.
1.4.7, 1.4.16 and 1.4.17 together require channel publishing, pre-change impact identification and a full publishing audit trail, which is what controlling availability and publishing safely means.
adjudicator_note: The 1.4.x Product Lifecycle rows sit under Ticketing Catalogue; confirm at sign-off that they bind retail merchandise as well as ticketing products.

rationale: 7.4.45 requires Draft, Review, Approval, Published, Suspended and Archived statuses with publishing blocked without approval, which is the same state machine as the source's five states.
An audit trail of publishing is obliged but not a versioned publication object that can be summarised and referred to by version number.
1.4.16 obliges impact identification before a product change but does not require it to be quantified as affected products, SKUs, stores and channels.
The matrix leaves out the composition of the publication, namely how many price changes and how many new products it carries.
1.4.8 requires future publication and activation based on configurable dates and times, which is the effective date and time this summary states.
Impact identification is obliged but not an explicit pre-flight validation step run against a pending publication before it is submitted.
7.4.45 prevents publishing without required approvals and 1.4.17 audits approvals, which together require a submit-for-approval step on a pending publication.
1.4.8 requires future publication on configurable dates and times, which is exactly scheduling a publication for a future effective date.
1.4.3 covers product import and export between environments, but no candidate obliges bulk retail product import with data-quality validation on the way in.
Import and an AI assistant exist separately, but the matrix obliges no data-quality area and no single governance screen joining the three.
8.4.2 and 8.7.30 require natural-language interaction and natural-language reporting, which is what answering a margin question in plain English is.
adjudicator_note: The 55% target the question compares against is itself not obliged anywhere; see the category default margin target gap.

rationale: 18.10.3 requires operational information to be retrieved through the AI, which covers returning a count of products under a threshold and offering the list.
AI retrieval is obliged but not a suggested action from the assistant that navigates the user into a filtered product list.
The AI rows oblige querying and natural-language pricing rules, but not the assistant creating catalogue objects such as a seasonal collection, nor the approval that write should pass through.
adjudicator_note: AI writing to the catalogue is a governance question; 8.3.66 AI approval workflows would need to be bound to it explicitly.

rationale: Nothing obliges the assistant to produce a draft collection, let alone report back its product count, SKU count and proposed pricing.
With no AI-generated draft collection obliged, the action that opens it for review is unaddressed too.
AI approval, configuration and policy management exist as separate rows but the matrix obliges no single governance centre to navigate into from the catalogue tools.
The matrix asserts real-time monitoring but never requires a board to state the as-of time of the data it shows, nor fixes a refresh cadence or staleness rule.
adjudicator_note: Refresh cadence and as-of semantics apply to every board in this pack and should be settled once, architecturally, rather than per screen.

rationale: 8.9.6 obliges device and infrastructure monitoring but not a rolled-up health badge shown on each functional board.
Missing: the existence and navigation state of a named POS and Sales board in the back-office rail.
8.9.8 requires real-time monitoring of retail sales and transaction performance and 8.9.1 a centralised dashboard spanning POS and retail, which is this command centre.
Dashboards and drill-down are obliged but not tenant, park, date and granularity scoping controls, which also dictate how sales data must be partitioned.
AI capability is obliged in general but no candidate places an AI insights entry point on the retail sales board.
Real-time retail sales monitoring is obliged but the matrix never distinguishes gross from net sales nor requires a comparison against the previous day.
The matrix obliges retail sales monitoring but defines no net sales measure, so what is deducted from gross is left open.
adjudicator_note: Gross versus net definition, in particular whether tax, discounts and refunds are netted, should be pinned down at sign-off.

rationale: Transaction performance monitoring and daily transaction reporting are obliged but not a live transaction count with a day-over-day change.
6.1.10 names units sold in daily reporting but not as a live board metric carrying a change against yesterday.
Average transaction value is derivable from obliged sales and transaction figures but is named as a metric nowhere in the candidates.
6.1.28 reports active workstations and 8.9.6 monitors POS devices, but neither obliges a live active-out-of-total terminal ratio on the sales board.
8.9.8 names refunds but never returns as a distinct measure, so returned merchandise value and its day-over-day change are not obliged.
adjudicator_note: Returns and refunds are shown as two separate tiles in the source; the matrix has only one concept, which should be reconciled at sign-off.

rationale: Real-time refund monitoring is obliged but not a refund value tile carrying a comparison against the previous day.
The matrix monitors sales and transactions but obliges no notion of a retail order left pending, nor a count of them.
4.4.21 obliges buy-online-collect-in-store but not the operational count of click-and-collect orders on the board.
Alerts and KPI alerts are obliged but not a headline count of open operational alerts on the retail board.
Real-time retail sales monitoring is obliged but not a per-store comparison carrying sales, transactions, ATV, returns, active terminals and health in one row.
Nothing in the candidates recognises a temporary or event merchandise store as a selling location reported alongside the permanent estate.
Operational status exists for facilities and devices, but no candidate defines a three-level store health rating or the thresholds that set it.
The matrix obliges the per-store figures nowhere, and the estate-level totals and averages that close the table even less so.
Drill-down analytics are obliged generically but not a route from the board summary into the full store list.
Sales monitoring is obliged but no candidate requires retail sales to be decomposed by sales channel with a total.
The full 1.1.133 names the channels and 8.9.8 obliges real-time retail sales monitoring, but no row fixes channel as a reporting dimension for retail sales with share and value per channel.
With channel-level sales reporting unobliged, the drill-through into a channel breakdown has nothing behind it.
Alerts are obliged as a dashboard feature but not a timestamped alert feed on the retail board with a route to the full alert list.
POS device monitoring is obliged but no candidate sets an offline-duration threshold that raises an alert, nor requires the elapsed time to be stated.
Click-and-collect is obliged as a fulfilment option but nothing alerts staff when orders are queueing unprepared.
6.1.57 gives exception reporting when a KPI leaves its range, but no candidate establishes a normal refund baseline per store or an alert on deviation from it.
4.4.17 obliges automatic out-of-stock alerts on configurable thresholds but does not scope them to a named SKU at a named selling location.
Offline mode is obliged but the matrix never requires the unsynchronised transaction backlog to be visible or alerted on, which is what makes offline safe to run.
8.9.6 monitors device and network health but stops short of alerting when a store's payment device drops offline.
Discount reporting exists but the matrix sets no manual-discount threshold and raises no loss-prevention alert when it is exceeded.
16.4.21 obliges battery monitoring but not a low-battery alert threshold or the surfacing of the charge level to retail operations.
The underlying transaction attributes are obliged for reporting, but not a live recent-transactions feed showing number, store, amount, channel, status and time.
No candidate defines a transaction status set for retail sales, so completed, voided and pending states are left undefined.
Sales channel is a reporting attribute but nothing obliges every retail transaction to be stamped with an originating channel drawn from a defined channel set.
Historical sales lookup and full transaction history are obliged, but not the route into them from the board's recent-transaction panel.
The candidates cover reporting and access control around the retail POS but none of them obliges the selling workspace itself.
adjudicator_note: The matrix carries a whole Retail POS domain; the lexical search surfaced only its auth and reporting rows, so the selling screen is probably obliged elsewhere.

rationale: Permissions can be scoped to a POS terminal but no candidate binds a terminal to a store or lets the cashier see and choose which store they are selling for.
Terminals are identified for access control but the matrix never requires the terminal identifier to be shown in the selling workspace.
Sign-in and user activity logging are obliged but not the display of the signed-in cashier on the till, which is what makes the sale attributable on screen.
Shifts exist for till opening, closing and reporting, but nothing obliges the active shift and its start and end times to be shown in the POS workspace.
Offline mode is obliged but the matrix does not require the terminal's connectivity state to be visible to the operator, which is how they know which functions are available.
No candidate obliges a sale to be parked and resumed, nor a count of held carts at the terminal.
POS screen configurability is obliged in general but not a secondary actions menu grouping the less frequent till operations.
4.5.1 requires products to be synced to the till so they can be scanned or searched to complete the sale, and 4.5.19 requires barcode scanning, which is exactly this.
Configurable POS screens are obliged but not a product browser organised into categories, search, favourites and recent items.
Categories exist as catalogue data but nothing obliges them to act as the till's product filters, nor names gift cards and packages among them.
4.5.1 and 10.1.4 require products to reach the till with their availability and pricing, and 7.4.17 fixes unit price and currency, which is what the tile displays.
4.6.2 requires sales to be recorded from the POS register using a manual product sale option, which is this manual entry action.
Barcode scanning and lookup of a product to complete a sale are obliged by 4.5.19 together with 4.5.1.
RFID readers at the POS are obliged for guest media and RFID for warehouse stock, but not scanning an RFID-tagged item of merchandise into a sale.
6.1.17 requires reporting on discount types by POS ID and staff member, which presupposes and therefore obliges discounts being applied at the till.
3.6.13 requires promo codes with location, usage and validity controls, which is the capability this till action exercises.
Quantity, price and discount appear as reportable fields, but no candidate specifies the live cart with its line count and per-line totals.
Recording a sale is obliged but abandoning one, clearing the cart in a single action, is not.
Receipt printing and receipt configuration are obliged but gift receipts, sale notes and personalisation are named nowhere.
Tax calculation and tax treatment per product are obliged but not the cart summary that breaks a sale into subtotal, discounts, tax at a stated rate and total.
Loyalty balance enquiry at the till presumes an identified guest, but no candidate obliges a POS panel that attaches a guest or member to the retail sale in progress.
With guest attachment itself unstated, detaching the guest from the sale in progress is not obliged either.
Guest contact attributes are stored and shown on the loyalty card, but the matrix does not require name and mobile to be shown to the cashier on the POS guest panel.
Tier is obliged on the loyalty card but the member-since date is named nowhere, and neither is their display at the till.
Guest profiles exist but the matrix obliges no drill-through to the full profile from the POS workspace.
5.4.4 requires loyalty point balance enquiry at the till with the balance available on the receipt, which is the same obligation as showing the balance on the guest panel.
Wallet balance is obliged on the Customer 360 dashboard but not at the point of sale where it would be spent.
A voucher wallet is obliged in the guest app but no candidate surfaces a count of the guest's active vouchers to the cashier.
5.4.10 requires tier-specific benefits including discounts, free products, earning multipliers and birthday rewards, which is exactly the four benefit kinds listed here.
Loyalty history and benefits display are both obliged; only the drill-through into them from the POS guest panel is left out.
Promotions and discounts are obliged and reportable, but no candidate requires a panel at the till showing what is affecting the sale in progress.
The till retrieves real-time prices but the matrix obliges no best-price resolution across competing promotions, nor any indication to the cashier that it happened.
adjudicator_note: The top lexical candidate is best available seat selection, which shares only the phrase best available and has no bearing on retail pricing.

rationale: Promotion and discount data is obliged for reporting after the fact but not shown line by line in the cart as it is applied.
Promotions are configured with qualifying thresholds in the back office, but nothing obliges the till to list eligible unapplied promotions with a means to apply them.
The full 3.6.12 requires the cart to reflect the promotion applied, but not that the till distinguish an available promotion from one already applied to the sale.
Promotions are managed and reported on, but no candidate obliges a route from the till into the full promotion list.
Receipt issuance is obliged but not a payment panel that states the amount due before tender is taken.
Multiple currencies in one transaction and multi-method refunds are obliged, but split tender across card, cash and wallet on a single sale is not stated.
Spend per transaction is reportable but no candidate obliges the till to show amount tendered against amount due while payment is being taken.
4.5.1 requires the till to complete the sale and 4.6.2 to record it from the POS register, which is what processing payment does.
2.13.11 requires the POS to drive a receipt printer and 6.1.3 governs when a payment receipt is issued, which is this action.
Printed receipts and a multi-channel messaging engine both exist, but no candidate obliges a retail receipt to be delivered by email.
adjudicator_note: None of the three digital receipt channels in this pack, email, SMS and QR, is obliged anywhere in the candidates.

rationale: The matrix obliges printed receipts but never receipt delivery by SMS to the guest's mobile number.
A QR-delivered digital receipt, and the retrieval it implies, is obliged nowhere in the candidates.
6.1.9 requires historical sales lookup and 1.1.112 transaction history, which together is this search and history screen.

The untruncated 2.1.11 does allow lookup by promotion code, booking number or mobile number at POS and Kiosk, but for ticket collection rather than retail transaction search by transaction or receipt number.
adjudicator_note: Improved traceability: 2.1.11's mobile-number lookup clause was hidden by the cut.

rationale: Transaction lookup is obliged but the matrix names no filter set over the transaction history.
Transaction history is obliged but not the specific columns of number, date and time, store, amount, status and channel.
Transaction detail exists in reporting but not as a drill-through from a history row into the full transaction.
Refunds are obliged for ticketing and stock returns for inventory, but no candidate obliges a retail returns, refunds and exchanges workflow joining the two.
Exchange as a distinct transaction type, separate from a return plus a new sale, is named nowhere in the candidates.
Historical lookup is obliged but not retrieval of the original sale by scanning its receipt as the first step of a return.
The matrix does not require the retrieved original transaction to be displayed with its number, date, store and total before the return is worked.
Stock returns are obliged but not a partial return in which specific lines are chosen with a quantity and a condition.
7.6.9 captures condition on rental returns, but nothing gives returned merchandise a resellable disposition deciding whether it re-enters sellable stock.
2.12.18 requires refunds in the original payment mode or another with supervisor override, which is exactly a selectable refund method defaulting to the original.

The untruncated 7.4.21 does compute refund amounts from split prices for packages, but no row requires the retail returns screen to compute the refund from the selected lines and show it before the return is committed.
Stock return and refund exist separately but nothing obliges one committed retail return that moves stock and issues the refund together.
Click-and-collect and delivery to a guest location are obliged as options, but no candidate obliges an order and fulfilment workspace to work them from.
The matrix obliges no fulfilment queue, so counted tabs across all orders, collect, delivery and ready have nothing behind them.
Orders exist but the matrix sets no fulfilment SLA against which an order can be judged late, which is the load-bearing column here.
Online ordering is obliged but the order's originating channel, app, web or QR, is not a recorded attribute anywhere in the candidates.
Pickup points and delivery to a guest location are obliged, but the order carries no fulfilment destination, and in-park destinations such as a numbered cabana are not modelled.
Picking exists as a warehouse operation but the matrix defines no fulfilment state machine for a retail order running from picking to accepted.
No candidate sets a fulfilment time target, so there is nothing for a per-order countdown to count down against.
Orders can be worked at a service desk but the matrix obliges no retail order list to navigate into from the board.
Mobile POS and offline mode are both obliged but no candidate provides a surface for supervising mobile devices and their offline transaction queue.
Battery and device monitoring are obliged but synchronisation state per mobile terminal is not, which is the column that matters for offline safety.
Offline mode is obliged but the matrix never requires the count of transactions held locally on a device to be visible.
Nothing in the candidates obliges the unsynchronised backlog to be measured, which is the exposure carried while a terminal is offline.
The matrix obliges no visibility of synchronisation in progress, so a count of items currently syncing is unaddressed.
The matrix says nothing about synchronisation failures, so neither their count nor what happens to a transaction that cannot be synced is obliged.
adjudicator_note: Failed offline synchronisation is a data-integrity question, since the sale exists on the device but not in the books; worth resolving at sign-off.

rationale: With no offline queue obliged, the drill-through into its full contents is unaddressed as well.
Exception logging and out-of-range KPI reporting exist, but no candidate obliges a triage surface where retail exceptions are listed and acted on.
22.9.6 gives notifications a priority scale but nothing applies severity to retail exceptions or requires them to be counted per level.
Exception reporting exists generically but no candidate sets a refund value threshold above which a single refund is escalated for review.
Device monitoring is obliged but a terminal going offline is not raised as a logged, severity-rated exception.
adjudicator_note: Near-duplicate of MOM-4727; the same offline-terminal condition appears once as an alert and once as an exception, which should be reconciled into one obligation.

rationale: Out-of-range KPI reporting is obliged but no store-level refund baseline exists for a high-refund exception to be measured against.
adjudicator_note: Near-duplicate of MOM-4729, which states the same condition as an alert with a percentage deviation.

rationale: 4.4.17 requires low-stock and out-of-stock alerts to be generated automatically against configurable thresholds, which is exactly this exception.
11.1.31 obliges an approval workflow for price overrides but not a threshold breach raised afterwards as an operational exception.
A priority scale and exception logging exist separately, but no candidate gives a retail exception a severity and a detection timestamp of its own.
Exception logging is obliged but not a full exception list reachable from the board summary.
Real-time monitoring and device health are obliged but neither an as-of timestamp for the board's data nor a rolled-up systems-operational indicator.
adjudicator_note: Same refresh and health obligation as MOM-4701 and MOM-4702 on the catalogue board; settle it once across all boards.

rationale: Nothing in the matrix defines the admin board set or the left navigation rail that reaches Board 1: Store & Ops Config.
Missing: the existence and navigation state of a named Inventory and Stock board in the back-office rail.
In-store stock recording and multi-location inventory are obliged, but no candidate requires a real-time operations board over retail inventory as a whole.
Multi-location inventory is obliged but not tenant, park, store and date scoping controls over an inventory board.
AI capability exists in the matrix but no candidate places an AI insights entry point on the inventory board.
Stock is recorded and reportable but no candidate obliges stock to be valued in currency, which requires a cost basis the matrix never fixes.
adjudicator_note: Valuation method, whether cost, weighted average or retail, is unstated and affects both this tile and the margin figures on the pricing board.

rationale: On-hand stock is obliged as recorded data but not as an estate-wide headline unit count with a day-over-day change.
15.1.12 obliges available stock tracking but not its presentation as a board KPI with a comparison against yesterday.
Reserved inventory tracking is obliged but not a reserved-units headline metric on the board.
Low-stock alerting against configurable thresholds is obliged but not a count of SKUs currently in that state shown as a tile.
Out-of-stock alerting is obliged but not an aggregate count of out-of-stock SKUs on the board.
15.1.15 obliges in-transit tracking but not the in-transit unit total as a board metric with a daily change.
Receiving confirmation is obliged within transfers but not a count of receipts still outstanding across the estate.
Stock counts and reconciliation are obliged but not the variance they produce, nor a count of open variances awaiting resolution.
15.1.16 obliges damaged inventory tracking but not its summary as a board KPI with a day-over-day movement.
Stock alerts are obliged but not a headline count of open inventory alerts on the board.
The individual measures exist across the inventory rows, but no candidate obliges a per-store stock health comparison carrying them in one row with a status.
The matrix obliges no composite stock health score, so neither its formula nor the thresholds separating healthy, warning and critical are defined.
adjudicator_note: A scored, colour-coded store ranking needs an agreed formula before it can be signed off.

rationale: Per-store inventory figures are not obliged as a table, and the estate-level totals and average health that close it even less so.
Stock recording and reconciliation are obliged but not a valuation of stock decomposed by merchandise category.
Categories exist as catalogue data but the matrix obliges no category-level stock value with share of total.
Available and reserved stock are tracked as current values, but nothing obliges them to be retained as a daily series so a trend can be plotted.
adjudicator_note: Trend charts across this pack all presume historical daily snapshots; the matrix states no retention or historisation requirement for inventory positions.

rationale: The matrix fixes no reporting window, so a rolling seven-day horizon for the inventory trend is unstated.
Stock alerts are obliged but not a ranked risk panel that grades inventory exposures by severity.
In-store stock visibility and threshold-based alerts are obliged, but nothing forecasts depletion, so a projected run-out time per store has no requirement behind it.
Transfers carry shipment tracking and receiving confirmation but no expected completion time, so nothing defines a transfer as overdue or measures by how long.
Physical counts and variance reporting are obliged but not a configurable tolerance whose breach flags the store for attention.
The matrix models stores and warehouses but not temporary event selling locations, so stock stranded at one after an event closes is detected by nothing.
adjudicator_note: Event and pop-up locations recur across this pack, in the store list and the assortment matrix; the matrix has no concept of them.

rationale: 4.4.17 obliges threshold-based low-stock alerts but does not scope them to a named product at a named store, which is what makes the alert actionable.
Stock alerts are obliged but not a consolidated alert list reachable from the risk panel with the open count on the link.
Multi-location inventory and drill-down analytics exist, but no candidate names the three destinations this board must route into.
15.1.10 requires inventory across multiple locations and 18.7.1 requires users to view inventory availability, which is stock visibility by SKU and location.
Inventory lookup and barcode scanning are obliged but not a stock search accepting SKU, barcode or product name interchangeably.
Inventory lookup is obliged but the matrix names no filter set over the stock list.
On-hand, available and reserved quantities are each tracked, but no candidate obliges them side by side per SKU per store with a status column.
Configurable stock thresholds exist for alerting but the matrix gives the SKU-at-location record no three-level status of its own.
Inventory lookup is obliged but not a drill-through from the board summary into the complete stock list.
15.2.17 and 15.4.4 require replenishment management and automatic replenishment, and 4.6.30 requires replenishment requests to be raised, which is this screen's purpose.
4.6.30 requires replenishment requests to be raised and 15.3.5 supports requisitions, which is what creating a new requisition is.
Requisitions are obliged but not a register showing number, store, item count, estimated value, priority and status.
No candidate gives a requisition a priority, so nothing governs which replenishment is worked first.
Approval exists for stock movements but the matrix defines no draft, submitted and approved lifecycle for a requisition.
Automatic replenishment and shortage alerts are obliged but not a forecast-backed recommendation stating the projected shortfall, the time by which it bites and a suggested order quantity.
Internal transfers are obliged but not their creation in one step from a replenishment recommendation with its quantities carried over.
Purchase requisitions are obliged but not a full requisition list reachable from the board panel.
4.4.15 requires stock transfers between stores and warehouses with approval, shipment tracking, receiving confirmation and audit logs, which is exactly this screen.
Raising a stock transfer between locations is obliged by 4.4.15 and 15.2.16, which is what this action does.
Transfers and their tracking are obliged but not a transfer register listing number, origin, destination, item and unit counts and status.

1.2.47 obliges predefined event resource templates but does not enumerate the shipped set of event types.
1.2.47 requires predefined event resource templates to be supported, which includes creating a new one.

1.2.50 calculates event resource costs but the matrix does not track them against a budget with committed cost, forecast cost and variance.
The matrix calculates event resource costs but does not require the split into staff, equipment, venue, services and setup and teardown.

rationale: No candidate requires a week-scoped event timeline/Gantt visualisation with per-event venue labelling and Confirmed/Needs Attention/Conflict/Optimized colour states.
The AI rows oblige alternatives and optimal-resource recommendations but omit the quantified estimated cost saving attached to each suggestion.
1.2.57 obliges automatic AI schedule optimisation, but the matrix does not require a bulk Apply All Recommendations action that commits every suggestion at once.
Configurable approval workflows are required, but the matrix does not oblige a readiness gate that performs final resource validation and blocks an event from going live until it passes.

Qualification validation, equipment allocation and reservation approvals exist individually, but no row requires a consolidated eight-item readiness checklist with per-item states such as Partial, Clear, None or Within Tolerance.
Resource utilisation dashboards are required, but the matrix omits an overall Resource Ready percentage and an outstanding-actions count as a gauge on the readiness gate.
Nothing among the candidates requires an outstanding-actions worklist with per-action priority and Resolve/Request controls; 1.2.52 is priority-based allocation, not an action queue.
Configurable and versioned approval workflows with audit tracking are obliged, but not the five named event-resource approver roles nor the per-step approver name and timestamp display.
Submit-for-approval and approval history are obliged by 1.2.76 and 11.1.26, but locking/freezing the approved resource plan against further change is not required anywhere.
The underlying AI optimisation and demand-forecast capabilities are obliged, but the matrix does not require them assembled as a named board deliverable for resource optimisation and forecasting.
Date-range filtering is obliged on the resource calendar, but not an all-venues scope selector, a clearable date range on a board header, or display of the signed-in user and their role.

AI services for forecasting, recommendations and assistant functions are required, but the matrix does not oblige an AI Intelligence navigation section nor the named surfaces AI Command Center, Optimization and Scenario Simulator.
18.10.1 obliges an AI assistant for employees on the mobile app, not a free-text operations copilot embedded in the resource board, nor a BETA labelling of it.

Rule-based approval conditions exist, but the matrix does not require the board to disclose that AI output is advisory, derived from current data and configured business rules, and subject to human approval.
Real-time analytics and an incident-oriented operations command centre are obliged, but neither requires a command centre whose subject is resource health and AI insight.

Staffing and overtime display and demand forecasting are obliged, but the matrix names none of the four tiles (Resource Readiness, Predicted Shortages, Overtime Risk, Optimization Opportunity) and does not require a prior-day baseline to compute the vs-yesterday delta.
adjudicator_note: The vs-yesterday delta implies retained daily KPI snapshots; no candidate row carries a retention or snapshot obligation.

rationale: Resource utilisation dashboards are required, but the matrix does not define the five health states (Fully Resourced, At Risk, Underutilized, Overutilized, Unavailable) or oblige a whole-estate split by count and percentage.

Staffing and resource demand forecasting exist separately, but no row obliges a next-day consolidated brief pulling attendance, staffing gaps, equipment shortages, maintenance risks and events needing attention into one panel.
AI recommendation explanations are required, but the matrix does not oblige surfacing a single highest-value reallocation with its zones and time window and a drill-through to details.
1.2.53 obliges the AI to recommend optimal resources, which is substantially the best-match recommendation engine described here.
The recommendation-engine rows do not specify the filter set (resource type, date, time, venue) or a More Filters expansion on the recommendation surface.
Recommendation explainability is required in principle, but the matrix omits restating the active requirement (experience, required certification level, language) as a persistent summary chip.
No candidate obliges the engine to present a separate Alternatives list alongside the Recommended list as switchable tabs.

Overtime and workforce utilisation are tracked, but the matrix does not require a numeric Match Score, the per-criterion satisfaction breakdown (certification, availability, same venue, no overtime, low workload) or a Select action that books the candidate.
adjudicator_note: 8.6.20 recommendation explainability, seen on sibling rows, is a closer anchor than the candidates offered here and should be considered at sign-off.

rationale: The matrix does not oblige a drill-through from the shortlist to the full eligible-resource pool with its count.
Staff scheduling and assignment are obliged but no row requires an AI matching surface scoped by role, event, date and time window.
Staff recommendation is obliged but not a proposed team roster showing each member with level, years of experience, languages spoken and a match percentage.

Skills matching, certification tracking, overtime monitoring and availability analytics all exist individually, but the matrix does not oblige a single team coverage readout that reports them together for a proposed team.

Alternative proposals are obliged, but the matrix does not require a ranked alternate-candidate list with match percentages, a count-bearing drill-through, or a Build Full Team action that composes an entire crew.
1.2.55 obliges AI forecasting of resource demand but not a user-parameterised forecast run with subject, horizon and granularity selectors executed on demand.

Staffing and event resource forecasting are obliged, but the matrix omits the forecast summary KPIs: expected visitors, identified peak day with its volume, a confidence percentage with a qualitative band, and event count over the horizon.

Forecasting and attendance confidence levels are required, but the matrix does not oblige a per-day table carrying instructors required, instructors available, the resulting gap and a confidence value.

Confidence levels are obliged for attendance forecasts but not per forecast day for resources, and the signed surplus or shortfall gap between instructors required and available is not required anywhere.
adjudicator_note: Overlaps MOM-6094; both trace to the same forecast table and can be signed off together.

rationale: The matrix obliges resource demand forecasting but not a drill-through from the summary to a detailed forecast view.
adjudicator_note: The offered candidates forecast F&B, retail and membership revenue and queue demand, none of which concerns resources; 1.2.55 is the correct anchor.

rationale: 8.2.47 requires staffing requirements to be forecast from attendance forecasts and 1.2.82 requires staffing gap detection from demand forecasts, which is exactly this conversion of demand into staffing need.
Coverage rules and gap detection are obliged, but the matrix does not require the applied rule or ratio to be displayed per role alongside required, available, gap and a priority ranking.

1.2.82 obliges configurable role coverage rules and staffing thresholds, so these specific instructor, assistant, customer service and supervisor ratios are configuration values the matrix permits but does not itself record.
Staffing forecasts and AI recommendation explanations are obliged, but the matrix does not require the recommendation to carry an estimated labour saving or a one-click apply onto the roster.
1.2.29 requires conflict detection and 1.2.56 requires the AI to propose alternatives for scheduling conflicts, together the same obligation as an AI conflict resolution assistant.

Conflict detection and staff scheduling are obliged, but the matrix does not require the conflict to be surfaced as a banner naming the staff member, the overlap count and each clashing assignment with its experience, venue and time.
The matrix detects conflicts but does not oblige a ranked AI resolution with supporting reasons plus alternative options each carrying an impact statement and a Not Recommended flag.
Conflict detection is required but the matrix does not oblige an Apply Resolution action that commits the chosen option, nor a view of the full option set.

1.2.57 obliges automatic schedule optimisation but omits the operator controls around it: a selectable optimisation objective such as labour cost, a scope and date range, and locking named assignments against change.

Labour cost and utilisation calculation are obliged, but the matrix does not require a current versus AI-optimised versus improvement comparison across coverage, conflicts, overtime hours, cross-venue transfers, labour cost and staff utilisation.
8.3.68 obliges explanations for AI recommendations but not a plain-language account of how an optimised schedule was arrived at on the optimisation screen itself.
adjudicator_note: 8.3.68 was not among the candidates offered here; the candidate set (notifications, multilingual SEO) is off-target.

rationale: 1.2.56 scopes AI alternatives to scheduling conflicts and does not oblige alternatives for an unavailable asset, nor the display of the requested resource with its unavailability reason such as under maintenance.
The matrix leaves out the ranked alternatives list with a Match percentage and spec, venue and availability comparison tags such as Same Spec, Different Venue or Lower Spec.
No matrix row obliges a drill-through from the shortlist to the full alternatives pool with its count.
1.2.58 requires the AI to simulate future operational scenarios, which is substantially the what-if scenario simulator described here.

Scenario simulation is obliged, but the matrix does not require a library of predefined scenarios (attendance uplift, instructor loss, venue closure, added event, labour-cost reduction) nor authoring of custom scenarios.

Labour cost and overtime calculation are obliged, but the matrix does not require a side-by-side comparison of Current Plan, Scenario Impact, AI Optimized Plan and Difference across the six named metrics.
Scenario simulation is required but not the scenario-linked AI recommendation list with a projected monetary saving attached to it.
adjudicator_note: Candidates offered were pricing-scenario and access-review rows; 1.2.58 from the sibling row is the honest anchor.

rationale: Scenario simulation is obliged, but the matrix does not require comparison of several saved scenarios side by side nor an action that commits the AI optimised plan to the live schedule.
8.4.1 requires a conversational AI assistant across all modules and 1.2.59 requires users to manage resources through conversational AI commands, which is this copilot.

Forecasting and conversational resource commands exist, but the matrix does not oblige the assistant to answer a shortage question by naming the at-risk events, their venues and the exact resource shortfalls, or to offer remediation.

AI alternatives and optimal-resource recommendations are obliged, but the matrix does not require named candidates with a match percentage nor committing a multi-person assignment from inside the conversation.
Optimal-resource recommendations are obliged but not an action list rated by impact (High, Medium, Low, Preventive) with a drill-through to all recommendations.
adjudicator_note: Candidates offered were promotion-simulation and dynamic-pricing impact rows; 22.9.6 shares the High/Medium/Low words but governs notification delivery priority, not action impact.

rationale: Conversational resource commands are obliged, but nothing requires recent queries to be retained and replayed or a persisted conversation history to be viewable.
adjudicator_note: Stored copilot conversation history is a data-retention and privacy obligation with no matrix row behind it; raise at sign-off.

rationale: The matrix has an employee mobile app with an AI assistant but does not oblige a real-time mobile resource operations and employee self-service board for frontline staff as a deliverable.
adjudicator_note: All four candidates are 19.2.x guest-app self-service rows; they concern guests, not employees, and must not be traced to this board.

rationale: The header tag row and strapline are presentation-pack chrome carrying no system obligation, so they should not be scored against the matrix.

Mobile home screens, widgets and personalised content blocks are configurable for the guest app, but no row obliges an employee operations home personalised with the signed-in worker name, role and department.

Employees receiving assignments on mobile is obliged, but the matrix omits a live current-assignment card carrying In Progress status, time window, zone, booking reference and participant count with a drill-through.
Assignment delivery to mobile is obliged but not a look-ahead next-assignment card with its time window, zone and participant count.
Quick actions and navigation are configurable in principle, but the matrix does not name the employee quick tiles My Schedule, Resources and Requests.
Demand forecasting and an employee AI assistant exist, but nothing obliges a forecast-derived readiness insight to be pushed to the frontline worker home screen for a named peak window.
1.2.18 obliges a central resource calendar with daily, weekly and monthly views, but not an employee-facing personal schedule on mobile with those view modes and day navigation.
adjudicator_note: The offered candidates (day-of-week access rules, day-of-week pricing, GPS navigation) match only on the phrase day of week and are unrelated.

rationale: 1.2.3 manages staff schedules including breaks, but the matrix does not oblige the employee-facing day list showing each entry with its zone and participant count alongside break and lunch entries.

Resources required for an event can be defined but no row obliges a per-assignment required-resource list with a readiness chip distinguishing items ready from items still to collect.

rationale: Shift viewing is obliged, but no candidate requires staff attendance capture (check-in and check-out against the rostered shift window and venue) on the employee app.
adjudicator_note: The candidate check-in rows are all guest ticket or rental-resource rows; a genuine staff attendance obligation may exist elsewhere in subdomain 18.9 and should be confirmed.

rationale: Scan-based check-in exists for guests at turnstiles, but the matrix does not oblige an employee attendance QR presented on the device, a checkpoint tap, or a manual check-in fallback when scanning fails.

rationale: Leave, shift-change and incident reporting exist as separate obligations, but the matrix does not require a single employee request intake typed as resource issue, replacement, support, shift change, leave or other.
Photo capture and note recording are obliged, but the structured fault report (the specific resource, an issue type, a severity level) is not required anywhere.
Submission is obliged for incident and hazard reports only, not for the general employee request created on this form.

1.2.80 validates qualifications on a shift request but does not oblige each open shift to be listed with role, venue, duration and a pre-computed eligibility chip before the employee requests it.
Approval workflows are obliged, but the matrix does not require the requesting employee to see their own submitted requests with current status.
1.2.80 requires employees to raise shift swap requests, which is exactly this action.
1.2.65 requires managers to approve requests from the mobile app and 18.6.1 and 18.6.2 require a pending-approval inbox with approve or reject actions, which is this approval centre.
Swap requests and an approval inbox are obliged, but the matrix does not require the approval card to carry a priority chip or to show both parties shifts side by side.

Qualification, certification, minimum-staffing and overtime-limit validation are all obliged, but the matrix does not require the validation outcome to be presented to the approver on the request card, including the overtime consequence for the accepting employee.
Approve and reject on mobile are obliged, but the matrix has no send-back Request Changes outcome and does not require the pending queue to be worked through item by item.
Push, emergency and approval notifications are obliged individually, but no row requires a consolidated employee notification centre filterable by assignments, resources and system.
adjudicator_note: 19.2.64 carries the same words Operational Notifications but belongs to the guest app, not the employee app.

rationale: Notification priority levels are defined, but the matrix does not require each employee notification to be rendered with title, detail, relative age and a severity chip.
adjudicator_note: The source uses Critical/High/Info while 22.9.6 defines Critical/High/Medium/Low; the severity vocabularies should be reconciled at sign-off.

rationale: AI recommendations and push notifications exist, but nothing obliges AI recommendation and maintenance-window notices to be pushed to frontline staff as notification categories.
Offline operation and post-outage reconciliation are obliged, but no row requires a visible app status showing the online or offline state and the last successful synchronisation time.
The matrix does not require the pending-sync backlog or active operation count to be exposed, which presumes a queued offline operation store.

The previously hidden bullet in 2.3.1 requires definition of which functionality is lost offline, but that row is scoped to POS and Kiosk; for the employee app no row fixes cached schedules, cached assignments, resource scanning and check-in/out, nor a user-controlled offline toggle.
adjudicator_note: Better traceability: 2.3.1's functional-envelope bullet is the nearest analogue but sits in the Ticketing Sales domain, not the employee app.

rationale: No row obliges a manual Sync Now action to force reconciliation of queued offline work.
Cost and availability analytics are obliged, but the matrix does not require them assembled with governance, audit and integration health as a single analytics and control board.
Date-range filtering exists on the resource calendar, but nothing obliges an all-tenants selector, so cross-tenant aggregation and the access rules governing it are unspecified.
adjudicator_note: Cross-tenant aggregation implies a data and access architecture decision that should be settled before sign-off.

rationale: Dashboards with drill-down analytics are obliged, but the matrix does not require an Analytics and Control navigation section grouping the ten named surfaces.
Resource categorisation exists, but the matrix does not prescribe the top-level navigation inventory of the resource management application.
This is a banner of operating principles on the board cover, not a testable obligation; the underlying properties it gestures at are scored on their own rows.
Resource utilisation dashboards and real-time analytics are both obliged; what the matrix does not require is their assembly into a single resource performance and health command centre.
No row defines a composite resource health score out of 100 with a qualitative band, nor the week-over-week baseline needed for its delta.

Utilisation dashboards and staffing displays are obliged, but the matrix names none of the six tiles (total resources, assigned now, utilisation, readiness, conflicts, overtime hours) nor their period-on-period deltas.

Executive dashboards and demand forecasting exist, but nothing obliges an AI-written weekly narrative brief carrying attendance movement, predicted recurring staffing gaps and a monetised optimisation opportunity.
Dashboards and cost analytics are obliged but not a drill-through from the command centre into the full underlying report.
1.2.67 requires resource utilisation dashboards and 1.2.71 requires utilisation heatmaps, which together are this utilisation and capacity analytics screen including its heatmap view.
Utilisation dashboards are obliged, but the matrix does not define overall, under- and over-utilisation as reported measures or the thresholds that separate them.
Trend analysis is obliged, but the matrix does not require a thirty-day utilisation trend plotted against a configurable utilisation target line.
The matrix does not oblige a ranked worst-performers table of underutilised resources carrying type, venue, utilisation and a direction-of-travel trend.
Resource typing and equipment allocation are obliged so the classification is largely inferable; the matrix simply does not require the utilisation report to be cut by resource type and venue.
Utilisation dashboards are obliged but not a drill-through link from the summary panel into the full utilisation analytics surface.
adjudicator_note: 21.12.5 scores highest but is seat utilisation analytics in the venue-mapping domain, a different subject.

rationale: 1.2.68 obliges resource cost analytics but not revenue contribution attributed to resources, efficiency metrics, or the by-resource, by-venue and by-department cuts.

Cost analytics are obliged, but attributing revenue to resources and reporting a cost-to-revenue ratio against a prior-week baseline is nowhere required and needs a data linkage from revenue to resource usage.
adjudicator_note: Revenue attribution to resources is the architectural dependency behind several tiles on this board; raise it once at sign-off.

rationale: Labour and overtime costs are calculated, but the matrix does not define the wider cost taxonomy of maintenance, rental, external and other costs needed for the breakdown.
The matrix does not oblige the derived efficiency ratios revenue per resource hour, labour cost per participant and revenue-to-cost ratio.
1.2.68 would make a tester open a resource cost report, but the efficiency half of this report has no matrix obligation behind it.
8.2.18 requires forecast accuracy measurements, which is exactly the forecast-versus-actual accuracy screen described.
8.2.18 obliges forecast accuracy measurement and the attendance, demand and staffing forecasts it measures are each separately required, so a tester would check these three accuracy figures.
Forecast-versus-actual comparison is obliged for attendance and revenue only; the matrix does not require the same comparison for staff required, equipment required or event participants.
Accuracy measurement is obliged, but the matrix does not require a ranked variance table giving forecast, actual, signed variance and accuracy per metric.
No row obliges a drill-through from the accuracy summary into a full forecast performance view.
KPI monitoring and alerting exist and SLAs are configurable for support cases, but the matrix does not oblige operational resource SLAs or user authoring of KPI definitions.
adjudicator_note: 22.3.5 governs case-management SLAs in Marketing & CRM; resource SLAs are a different subject sharing the term.

rationale: KPI monitoring and trend analysis are obliged, but the matrix does not require each KPI to be shown as target against actual with a status and a trend.
Utilisation and asset availability are tracked, but the matrix sets none of these five targets, and assignment fulfilment and maintenance downtime are not measured anywhere.
Forecast accuracy and resource status are tracked, but critical replacement time and customer impact events are not measured by any row, so three of these five targets have no source metric.
KPI monitoring, alerts and trends are obliged, but the matrix does not require a red-amber-green status and directional trend indicator against each KPI target.
AI policy management exists, but the matrix does not oblige a governance centre for the policies that control resource operations, with a policy hierarchy and an effective-dated calendar.

Versioned policy management exists only for cookie policy content; the matrix does not oblige a resource policy register listing name, area, scope, status, version and owner with area filtering and policy authoring.

Policy management and reusable templates are obliged in general, but the matrix names none of the eight resource policies, notably AI Autonomy Policy and Override Governance which bound what the AI may decide unaided.
Nothing obliges a policy to be scoped global, all-venues or tenant, nor to carry an accountable owning team, which together define the policy resolution and access model.
adjudicator_note: Tenant-level policy scoping is an architectural commitment with no matrix row behind it; confirm at sign-off whether policies are tenant-scoped.

rationale: Policy version history is required only for published cookie policies; resource policy versioning, an active status lifecycle and a full policy listing are not obliged.

Configurable approval workflows and a pending inbox exist, but the matrix does not require a single queue combining approvals, exceptions and overrides with pending, mine and history tabs, counts, type filtering and priority sorting.

Overtime and shift swap approvals are obliged, but a resource override request (using an asset that is under maintenance) is not an obliged approval type, nor are the priority chip and requested-at timestamp.
Approve and reject are obliged, but the matrix omits an intermediate Review step on an item and a drill-through to the full approvals queue.
1.2.75 requires complete audit logs and 8.3.59 an AI decision history, but neither obliges the record to be immutable or tamper-evident as the source states.
adjudicator_note: 1.2.75 was offered only on the neighbouring row; immutability of the resource decision record should be confirmed explicitly.

rationale: Complete audit logs are obliged but not their searchability by resource, user, action or identifier, nor filtering by action type.
Audit trails elsewhere in the matrix do enumerate date/time, identity and source, but no row obliges those columns for a resource-management audit trail.
adjudicator_note: The audit field sets in 22.12.20 and 22.13.6 could be reused as the pattern for resource auditing.

rationale: 8.1.6 requires a history of AI-generated actions, but the matrix does not oblige every audit entry to carry channel attribution across backend, AI engine, mobile, integration and API.
The matrix obliges audit logs but does not enumerate the auditable action types (assignment changed, recommendation, check-in, resource status, deposit adjusted).
Audit logs are maintained but the matrix does not oblige an export of the resource audit trail or a full-log view for evidence.
13.1.43 obliges integration health monitoring but not an estate roll-up counting total integrations against healthy, warning and offline states.
Health monitoring is obliged without defining the measures, so last sync time, records processed, error counts and latency per integration are not required.

Integration health monitoring is generic; the matrix does not oblige the eight named integrations themselves, and HRMS, payroll, equipment IoT and ERP are substantial external interfaces with no row requiring them.
adjudicator_note: Whether these eight integrations are in scope is a commercial and architectural question the matrix does not settle.

rationale: Integration health monitoring is obliged but the matrix does not fix the health states (healthy, warning, offline) or require error counts and latency to be reported per integration.
adjudicator_note: Same underlying gap as MOM-6208; the two rows describe the table and its values and can be closed together.

The matrix obliges capacity alerts and AI risk identification but not an oversell-risk alert counting affected timeslots.
