No candidate obliges detection or alerting of broken links between products and their inventory pools.
The matrix obliges AI anomaly identification but not a thresholded abnormal-utilisation alert at under 50 or over 95 per cent.
The matrix obliges capacity utilisation display and forecasting but not a ranked top-products-by-utilisation list.
8.9.10 requires the operations command centre to provide dashboards, reports and drill-down analytics, which is this link through to full capacity analytics.
1.1.10 explicitly requires sales capacity limiting how many tickets may be sold.
The matrix obliges configurable sales capacity but not its split into setup, limits-and-rules and messaging views.
The full texts cover fixed sales capacity, unlimited capacity and capacity derived from the attraction, but a pooled model shared across products is not obliged.
1.1.127 'Maximum sellable quantity controls' with 1.1.10 requires a total sellable quantity to be set.
The full text of 1.1.10 requires capacity to be allocated per day ('only 200 tickets to be sold per day for Ski Park'), which is the per-day allocation method.
Configurable capacity is obliged and effective from/to dates exist for revenue rules, but an effective period on a capacity definition is not required.
The matrix obliges quotas and sales limits per channel but not a limits model with scope, type, max quantity and unit.
'Maximum sellable quantity controls' does not fix the per-order scope of the limit.
Per-day and per-month quantity limits are obliged for B2B guests and quantity restrictions exist generally, but a per-guest-per-day retail limit is not.
1.1.30 requires corporate allocations and quotas and 2.7.38 per-month quantity limits for account holders.
2.1.2 requires quotas and sales limits to be configured for each sales channel, which is this per-channel daily cap.
The full text of 1.1.10 allows only a fixed number of tickets to be sold and reopens sale on cancellation or refund, which is the stop-sale behaviour when the limit is reached.
A Sold Out state is obliged but a configurable customer-facing sold-out message per selected date is not.
1.3.16 explicitly requires capacity to be automatically allotted back in case of cancellations.
3.3.19 requires access restrictions based on capacity utilisation, which is protecting venue and attraction operating limits.
The matrix obliges capacity-based access restrictions but not configuration, allocation and validation-outcome views on the admission capacity editor.
The full text of 1.1.10 defines Admission Capacity as tickets sold against the capacity of the attraction, which is the Attraction Capacity source type selected here.
3.2.21 requires capacity counts for a specific attraction or location, so binding the capacity to an attraction is obliged.
3.2.21 requires access control systems to be grouped to give a capacity count for a specific location and 3.3.19 restricts access on that utilisation.
Capacity is configurable and dynamically adjustable but a named, shared capacity pool that a rule draws from is not modelled.
Fixed capacity and capacity derived from the attraction are both obliged by 1.1.10's full text, but a shared-pool allocation model is not.
1.1.3 explicitly requires capacity to be configured for each timeslot.
1.4.19 requires assignment to all or specific venues, which is this rule's venue scope.
Ticket tiers and age groups are obliged but scoping an admission capacity rule to specific guest categories is not.
The matrix obliges a single inventory source across channels and product variants but not inventory pools that ticket products and variants are associated to.
The matrix omits associations, pool details and impact views on inventory pool configuration.
The matrix omits selecting the named inventory pool a ticket product draws from.
Units of measure and stock consumption are obliged for physical stock but a ticket-to-entry consumption ratio against a capacity pool is not.
One inventory source across channels is obliged but pooled, nested, exclusive and shared-across-channels association types are not defined.
The matrix obliges product variants but not an associated-products table carrying an allocation percentage and status.
adjudicator_note: The quoted header lists both 'Product / Variant' and 'Variant' as columns, which looks like a duplicated column in the source pack.

rationale: Variants may hold independent inventory and 7.1.10 obliges percentage allocation across channels, but percentage allocation of one pool across product variants is not required.
1.4.16 requires affected tickets, reservations and integrations to be identified before a product change is applied, which is this warning.
1.1.30 requires corporate allocations and quotas and 2.7.54 allocation of inventory and quotas across partners and channels.
The matrix obliges allocations and quotas but not their split into allocation, hold-rule and quota-rule views.
Creating an allocation is the direct operator action behind the allocations and quotas 1.1.30 requires.
AI recommendations for optimal allocation and dynamic capacity adjustment are obliged but an operator action that rebalances allocated capacity is not.
Automatic release of expired cart holds is obliged but a manual release of allocated capacity back to general sale is not.
No candidate describes an allocations register; the matrix lacks any requirement for an allocation record carrying name, scope, pool, quantity, validity dates and status.

The full text of 7.1.10 requires each capacity slot to support 'configurable capacity allocation by percentage across channels, including B2B, B2C online, at-gate purchases, call center bookings, and annual pass reservations', which is this channel-scoped allocation drawn from a park capacity pool.
adjudicator_note: The matrix expresses the allocation as a percentage while the board shows an absolute quantity (2,000); confirm both forms are supported.

rationale: 1.1.30 requires corporate ticket allocations with quotas and corporate account management, which is exactly an account-scoped allocation of a fixed quantity.
2.7.54 has AI recommend allocation of inventory and quotas across B2B partners, but nothing obliges a stored partner-scoped allocation with quantity, validity window and status.
The matrix requires approval workflows for complimentary and sponsor allocations but not a segment-scoped allocation pool holding a fixed complimentary quantity against venue capacity.
A promotion engine with draft promotions is required, but no row provides for a promotion-scoped inventory allocation that can itself be placed on hold.
Hold inventory reporting and active/inactive product status exist, but no row defines an allocation lifecycle status of Active versus On Hold.
Capacity is configurable and dynamically adjustable but a Total Allocated summary across allocations is not obliged.
Hold inventory reporting and temporary grants are required, but no row obliges a Total Held (Temporary) capacity figure on the allocations view.
3.5.8 requires availability to be maintained and validated per component, but the matrix never asks for capacity remaining for general sale net of allocations and holds.
Capacity is obliged at multiple levels but the precedence between those levels, which is what this frame exists to resolve, is not defined.
No candidate concerns capacity at all, so the Hierarchy / Precedence / Simulation tab structure of this frame has no matrix anchor.
adjudicator_note: Candidates 5.7.41, 5.7.46 and 5.7.48 are chart-of-account hierarchies matched on the word hierarchy alone.

rationale: Multi-level capacity configuration is required, but the matrix does not enumerate the seven levels (Global, Venue, Attraction, Product, Variant, Date, Timeslot) nor fix their precedence order.

Nothing in the candidates requires a capacity-limit simulation, so its inputs of date, timeslot, channel and guest category are unanchored; 2.1.23 uses those attributes for pricing, not for capacity resolution.
No candidate requires a simulation result set, so the columns Level, Configured Capacity, Effective Limit and Source have no matrix equivalent.

Per-day and per-timeslot sale limits and multi-level capacity are obliged, but attributing an effective limit to its originating level (Global, Venue, Attraction, Product, Variant, Date, Timeslot) is not.
No candidate requires the system to compute and report the binding capacity value together with the hierarchy level that imposes it.
Capacity may be configured at multiple levels, but the matrix does not state the enforcement rule that the lowest applicable level binds.
There is no matrix requirement for a capacity simulator, hence none for re-running a simulation.
The full text of 1.1.10 requires the system to reopen sale automatically in case of any cancellation or refund, which is returning eligible inventory after reversals.
Audit history and policy audit logs are required generally, but not a reopen-rules frame split into Reopen Rules, Policy Mapping and Audit History.
Automatic reopening after cancellation or refund is obliged, but a configurable reopen-rule table keyed by event type with a reopen behaviour and an approval flag is not.
Inventory approval workflows exist, but the matrix does not specify that a pre-visit cancellation reopens inventory immediately and without approval.
Refund approval workflows are required, but nothing obliges immediate, approval-free reopening of the inventory a pre-visit refund releases.
Reopening on cancellation or refund is obliged but a date exchange as an event that immediately reopens the original slot without approval is not.
No-show tracking is required, but the matrix omits the timed reopen window that returns no-show inventory to sale after the slot starts.
Inventory approval workflows are required, but the event-type to approval mapping that makes operational cancellation approval-gated is not specified.
Inventory approvals exist generically; the matrix does not oblige approval specifically before a manual void reopens inventory.
1.1.32 requires dynamic adjustment of ticket inventory and capacity based on demand forecasts, operational capacity and business rules, which is the capability this frame presents.
Forecasting and dynamic capacity adjustment are required, but the Forecast / Recommendations / History organisation of the frame is not.
Forecasting from historical booking trends is required, but booking pace with a week-on-week variance as an explicit forecast input signal is not.
8.2.1 requires forecasting based on historical attendance patterns, which is precisely this input signal.
No-show tracking and capacity forecasting each exist, but the matrix does not require the no-show rate to feed the capacity forecast.
1.1.32 explicitly bases dynamic capacity adjustment on operational capacity, so current operating capacity as a forecast input is already required.
The matrix forecasts staffing requirements as an output but does not require staffing availability to be consumed as an input to the capacity forecast.
8.2.11 requires attendance forecasting based on weather conditions, which is the weather input signal asked for.
Capacity and utilisation forecasting are obliged but a special-events calendar taken as a forecast input signal is not.
AI recommendations and their approval are required, but not a dated capacity-increase recommendation carrying a Recommended status flag.
Confidence scoring on recommendations is required, but the recommended delta and the resulting new capacity are not obliged fields.
8.3.68 requires AI recommendation explanations and 8.1.5 requires reasoning indicators, which is the plain-language reason asked for.
Utilisation forecasting and recommendation explanations exist, but the before and after utilisation impact of accepting a recommendation is not required.
Dynamic capacity adjustment is required, but the matrix sets no minimum and maximum safety bounds constraining what the automated adjustment may propose.
Forecasting and capacity adjustment are required, but the explicit Run Forecast and Review Recommendation operator actions are not.
Emergency override of access restrictions with justification, approval and audit logging is required, but not the temporary override of configured capacity itself.
Override governance exists, but nothing obliges a Create Override / Active Overrides / Audit organisation nor a live count of active overrides.
Price and discount override approval workflows are obliged but an Increase Capacity override type is not among them.
Capacity is configurable at multiple levels, but the matrix does not require an override to declare the level at which capacity is consumed.
adjudicator_note: Candidates 15.4.2 and 15.1.19 match on 'consumption' in the stock-movement sense, not the capacity sense.

rationale: Capacity and pricing already recognise venue, date and timeslot, but no row requires an override to be targeted at a specific venue-date-timeslot combination.
Capacity may be adjusted, but the matrix does not require the change to be expressed as a seat delta with the resulting new capacity shown.
Override expiration and effective-from/to validity periods exist for access and revenue rules, but no row requires a capacity override to carry its own effective window.
Justification is obliged for emergency access overrides but a mandatory reason on every capacity override is not.
Supporting-evidence attachments are required on service cases only; nothing extends attachments to capacity override records.
No candidate requires a pre-commit impact assessment showing the downstream effect of a capacity change on sales availability, reservations, access control, staffing and safety controls.
Override expiration is required for access overrides, but not the automatic expiry of a capacity override with an explicit statement of the capacity it reverts to.
Configurable approval workflows for sensitive actions and role-based access control are obliged, but a capacity override gated on a named approving role is not.
Submission for approval is required for price and discount overrides, but capacity override is not one of the matrix's approval workflow types.
Utilisation analytics and KPI alerts are required, but reconciliation of capacity data across the contributing systems is not obliged anywhere.
Utilisation and alert analytics exist, but the Utilization / Alerts / Reconciliation / Investigations tab structure, and investigations in particular, are not required.
1.1.40 requires analytics and dashboards covering ticket sales and capacity utilisation, which is what a sales utilisation percentage against capacity measures.
Capacity utilisation analytics are required, but utilisation measured specifically on reservations against capacity is not named.
1.1.40 requires analytics covering attendance and capacity utilisation, which is admission utilisation against capacity.
8.2.19 requires forecast attendance to be compared against actual attendance, so an actual attendance count is already obliged.
Trend analysis is required, but not a utilisation trend chart carrying the three distinct series Sales, Reservations and Admission over a period.
Capacity and KPI alerts must be generated, but no row requires an open-alert queue with type, scope, severity, detection time and status.
Capacity alerts are required generically, but an Oversell Risk alert type carrying a severity and scoped to a named timeslot is not.
Capacity alerts are required generically, but no row obliges detection of negative availability at an attraction as a high-severity alert.
Capacity alerting and reservation integration exist, but an orphan-reservation alert against a timeslot is not a required detection.
Stock discrepancy reporting and physical counts cover retail inventory, but a count-divergence alert against a ticketing capacity pool is not required.
Capacity alerts must be generated but no alert lifecycle status such as Open or Investigating is defined.
Alerts and reconciliation reporting exist separately, but there is no requirement for a combined alerts-and-reconciliation view to navigate to.
A severity taxonomy exists for notifications, but the board's Information / Warning / Critical / Good status legend is not defined anywhere in the matrix.
adjudicator_note: The matrix taxonomy (Critical/High/Medium/Low) and the board legend (Information/Warning/Critical/Good) differ; worth aligning at sign-off.

rationale: Immutable audit logging is required for resale marketplace and AI actions, but no row extends it to capacity changes.

Cross-channel synchronisation is required for upsell recommendations and access rules consume capacity, but nothing obliges capacity data to be synchronised across POS, Kiosk, App, Access Control, CRM, Inventory and Finance.
Real-time capacity updates are obliged but the board's data-freshness timestamp and explicit Refresh All action, and hence its refresh contract, are not.
The matrix requires entitlements to be configured and assigned, but not a single consolidated entitlements and rights configuration board.
This is the design pack's own traceability annotation naming the matrix items the board claims to satisfy, not something the system must do.
adjudicator_note: The pack asserts coverage of 1.1.11 and 1.1.50-64; worth checking that claim against this adjudication at sign-off.

rationale: Multi-tenancy and venue/attraction scoping of rules exist, but a board-level context selector spanning tenant, brand, venue, attraction, language and effective date is not required.
Configurable navigation labels are required, but no row specifies an Entitlements screen in the administrative left navigation.
Entitlement configuration is required, but neither reusable entitlement templates nor a shortcut to them appear in the matrix.
adjudicator_note: Entitlement templates as a concept are unanchored in the matrix; if the client expects them they need their own requirement.

rationale: Access areas, gates and locations are configurable per 3.2.11, but the matrix says nothing about board navigation shortcuts to that configuration.
Wallets and stored-value balances are required, but a wallets shortcut from the entitlements board is not.
Loyalty programs are extensively required, but navigation from the entitlements board to loyalty program administration is not specified.
Loyalty redemption is required, but a managed register of redemption locations reachable from this board is not.
1.1.50 requires multiple entitlements to be configured per ticket, which is composing one ticket from several independently consumable rights.
Entitlement configuration and validity validation are required, but the Entitlements / Templates / Validation / Preview tab structure is not.
Multiple entitlements per ticket are configurable, but each entitlement carrying a quantity and a unit type is not specified.
1.1.51 requires admission entitlement management and 1.1.64 requires entry quantity control, which is a number of entries into a named zone set.
1.1.53 requires F&B entitlement management and 5.5.10 requires stored value and promotional credits to be maintained, which together are a monetary F&B credit entitlement.
1.1.54 requires merchandise entitlement management and 19.2.39 requires voucher storage, which is a merchandise voucher entitlement of a stated value.
1.1.55 requires stored value entitlement management and 4.3.22 requires stored-value wallet balances, which is a wallet credit entitlement.
4.1.22 requires loyalty points to be earned through purchases and 5.4.7 requires points to be created for configured transaction types, which is a points grant attached to a ticket.
1.1.59 requires complimentary entitlement redemption and 5.5.8 names parking among the entitlements maintained, which is a complimentary parking entitlement.
Entitlements must be configurable per ticket, but the builder interaction of adding them by button or by dragging from a library is not a matrix concern.
Draft saving and entitlement validation exist elsewhere but the builder's Clear All, Save as Draft and Validate & Continue actions are not required.
1.1.51 requires admission entitlement management and 3.2.11 requires configuration of access areas, gates and locations, which together are what this frame does.
Entitlement management and capacity-based access rules exist, but the Configuration / Access Rules / Capacity Link organisation of the frame is not specified.
Admission entitlements and grouped access areas are required, but the entitlement's access scope as an explicit single-venue versus multiple/group setting is not.
Entitlement management is required, but the editable list of covered venues and attractions with add and remove controls is not specified.
Entitlement management and area-based validity rules exist, but the composite access behaviour of N entries across Y areas is not an obliged configuration pattern.
1.1.64 requires entry quantity control and 3.2.72 requires tickets configured to allow n admissions, which is the maximum entries setting.
3.2.11 requires access areas and locations to be definable and 3.2.7 requires entitlements to be configured by area/attraction, which is scoping entries to named areas.
7.4.29 requires re-entry to be allowed or not per product and 3.2.1 includes re-entry rights, so a re-entry toggle is already obliged.
No candidate requires anti-passback, that is preventing a ticket already used for entry from being passed back to another guest.
Adult-child pairing rules exist for child protection, but an accompaniment entitlement granting a named number of free companions is not required.
Nothing in the candidates requires an ordered entry sequence constraining the order in which gates and zones may be used.
1.1.52 requires redeemable product entitlement management, which is granting redemption of a product or service through the ticket.
Redeemable product entitlement management is required, but the Configuration / Rules / Locations / Preview organisation of the frame is not.
Redeemable product entitlements are managed but identifying the redeemable item by product code and allowing it to be changed is not specified.
Redeemable entitlements and quantity restrictions exist, but the unit basis of the quantity, such as per ticket versus per guest, is not defined.
Redeemable product entitlements are managed but a substitution policy governing which alternative products may be taken instead is not required.
1.1.24 requires products that need a reservation before attendance and 5.5.21 requires entitlements to be reservable before use, which is this reservation-required setting.
Reserving entitlements before use is obliged but a configurable lead-time window such as up to two hours before use is not.
Entitlement validity validation is required, but an expiry rule tying the entitlement's life to the parent ticket's validity is not specified.
Redeemable product entitlements are managed, but the fulfilment locations at which the item may be collected are not part of any requirement.
1.1.50 requires multiple entitlements per ticket and 1.1.53 and 1.1.54 require F&B and merchandise entitlement management, which is exactly bundling these benefits into the ticket.
F&B and merchandise entitlement management are required, but the Configuration / Outlets / Modifiers / Preview organisation, and modifiers in particular, are not.
F&B and stored-value entitlements are required, but the benefit's data model of amount, allowance count and currency is not specified.
F&B entitlement management is required, but restricting where the credit may be spent to a configured list of eligible outlets is not.
Merchandise and stored-value entitlements are required, but the benefit's amount, voucher count and currency fields are not specified.
Merchandise entitlement management is required, but the list of eligible stores at which the voucher may be redeemed is not obliged.
Redeemable entitlements and quantity restrictions exist, but the three redemption types of one-time, multiple by quantity and allowance are not defined.
1.1.55 requires stored value entitlement management and 5.5.10 requires a single place maintaining stored value, loyalty points and credits, which is what this frame grants against.
adjudicator_note: The pack's non-duplication of ledgers is an architectural constraint the matrix implies but never states; worth confirming at sign-off.

rationale: Stored value entitlement management and configurable policies exist, but the Configuration / Policy / Ledger Link / Preview tabs, and an explicit ledger link in particular, are not required.
Stored-value entitlements and wallet balances are required, but directing an entitlement at one named wallet and currency among several is not.
1.1.55 requires stored value entitlement management and 4.3.22 requires funded stored-value balances, so setting the entitlement's initial value and currency is already in scope.
1.1.107 requires balance top-up, so whether top-up is permitted on a stored-value entitlement is a setting the matrix already obliges.
4.3.6 requires a configurable expiry period for all types of credit held in the wallet, which is this stored-value expiry setting.
Stored value is managed and funded, but restricting where that value may be spent, such as to a subset of outlets, is not required.
Multiple loyalty programs are required, but binding a points entitlement to one named program is not specified.
5.4.12 requires configurable points earning rules across ticketing, which includes setting how many points a ticket grants.
Expiring points are acknowledged in notifications and wallet credits have configurable expiry, but a configurable expiry period for granted loyalty points is not stated.
5.4.12 requires configurable earning rules with exclusions, which is what an earning-eligible switch on the entitlement expresses.
No candidate requires the financial liability created by stored-value and loyalty grants to be estimated and shown at the point of configuration.
adjudicator_note: The matrix has a Revenue Recognition subdomain that may carry a liability requirement not surfaced by these candidates; worth a targeted check.

rationale: Referral, earned and complimentary benefit entitlement management are each required, which is exactly the non-purchased benefits this frame configures.
Referral benefits and approval audit trails exist, but the Configuration / Approval / Audit / Preview organisation of the frame is not required.
The matrix separately requires referral and earned benefit entitlement management, so classifying a benefit by type is already obliged.
5.4.15 requires referral rules defining eligibility, reward type and reward timing, which is the trigger that awards the benefit.
Referral rewards are required, but the matrix assumes the referrer is rewarded and never makes the beneficiary a configurable choice.
F&B entitlements and voucher storage are obliged but granting a fixed-value F&B voucher as the configured entitlement is not stated.
Reward timing is part of referral rules, but a claim window in days after which an unclaimed benefit lapses is not specified.
Referral fraud prevention controls are required in general, but a maximum number of awards per referrer is not named as one of them.
11.1.33 requires approval workflows for complimentary issuance, which is what this approval-required switch turns on.
11.1.3 requires single and multi-level approval chains and 2.12.4 requires a configurable supervisor access level, which is setting the required approval level.
Service recovery compensation and complimentary benefits exist but a configurable set of reason codes recorded against each granted benefit is not required.
1.1.64 requires entry quantity control and 3.2.11 requires access areas and rules to be configurable, which together are where and how many times rights may be used.
Access rule configuration and policy simulation exist, but the Access Map / Rules / Sequence / Simulation organisation of the frame is not required.
3.2.64 requires a graphical map of access control points and 19.2.55 requires interactive venue maps, which is the numbered access-area map asked for.
3.2.11 requires all access-control areas, gates and locations to be definable and configurable; the named areas are client data within that requirement.

The full text of 3.2.7 configures per-area entitlements including Area/Attraction, Quantity Entry and Anti-pass Back - 'time elapse required between an exit and a re-entry' - which is exactly Area, Max Entries and Re-entry Cooldown.

3.2.7 makes entries per area configurable with Anti-pass Back as an optional elapse rule, and 1.1.11 allows unlimited access for an attraction, so unlimited main-gate entry with no cooldown is required.

3.2.7's full text obliges a configurable entry quantity per area plus Anti-pass Back, the time that must elapse between an exit and a re-entry, which is two Waterpark entries with a 30-minute cooldown.

3.2.7's full text obliges a configurable entry quantity per area plus Anti-pass Back, the time that must elapse between an exit and a re-entry, which is two Wave Pool entries with a 30-minute cooldown.
12.1.25 requires access rights to be assigned by venue zone and 3.2.7 requires area-level entitlements, which necessarily allows a zone to be excluded.
3.2.7's full text obliges entry quantity per area and Anti-pass Back as the elapsed time between exit and re-entry, covering one VIP Area entry with a 60-minute cooldown.
3.3.25 requires simulation and testing of access policies prior to deployment, which is this Simulate Access action.
1.1.60 requires check-in / check-out entitlement control, which is exactly entitlements needing paired arrival and departure.
Check-in/out control and offline validity checking exist, but the Configuration / Devices / Corrections / Offline Sync organisation of the frame is not specified.
Check-in / check-out entitlement control plus device check-in scanning make a check-in-required setting a thing a tester would verify.
1.1.60 requires check-in / check-out entitlement control, which includes requiring a check-out on the entitlement.
Length of stay is reported and access can vary by time, but no row requires a configurable maximum stay duration on an entitlement.
A visual policy builder and reusable policy templates are obliged but an open-session policy that automatically closes a session at maximum stay is not.
Check-in control exists, but session-aware behaviour that rejects a second check-in while a session is open is not specified.
Check-out control exists, but the behaviour on a double check-out with no active session is not defined by any row.
Check-in / check-out control is required, but the ability to correct an erroneous check-in or check-out record is not.
Approval workflows exist for policy changes, but no row makes a check-in or check-out correction approval-gated.
Role-based access control and approval levels exist for other operations but the approving role for a check-in/out correction is not named or configurable.
1.1.62 requires entitlement consumption tracking and 1.1.108 requires balance enquiry, which together are tracking use and presenting a remaining balance.
Consumption tracking and adjustments exist, but the Balance Overview / History / Adjustments / Guest View organisation, and a guest-facing view in particular, are not required.
Consumption tracking and entry quantity control are required, but showing the original issued quantity as a distinct figure is not.
1.1.62 requires entitlement consumption tracking, which is the consumed count this tile shows.
Entitlements may be reserved before use and reserved stock is tracked, but a held or reserved figure on the entitlement balance is not itself required.
1.1.108 requires balance enquiry, which is the available remaining balance this tile presents.
Consumption tracking and entitlement audit reporting are required, but not a per-event history carrying quantity, running balance, source channel and acting user.
Entitlement audit reporting is obliged but an issue event recording quantity issued, source channel and acting user is not specified.
Check-in scanning and entry events are required, but not a per-entitlement consumption ledger entry that decrements a remaining balance and records the gate and device.
Check-out and exit events are required, but the rule that a check-out is recorded without decrementing the entitlement balance is not stated.
Consumption tracking exists, but a refund event that credits consumed quantity back to the entitlement balance is not required.
Duplicate scan prevention is required at validation, but idempotent consumption across all channels and retries - the guarantee that the same request cannot double-decrement a balance - is not.
Configurable approval requirements exist for refunds, wallet adjustments and overrides, but entitlement quantity adjustment is not among the actions the matrix gates.
The integrity rule that an entitlement balance may never fall below zero is missing.
1.1.63 requires entitlement audit reporting and 7.5.9 requires secure offline validation data, which is what this frame governs.
Audit reporting and device audit logs exist, but the Keys & Security tab rests on signing-key management that the matrix nowhere requires.
adjudicator_note: Same underlying gap as the offline payload signing requirement (MOM-7038): no matrix row covers key management.

rationale: 1.1.63 requires entitlement audit reporting, which covers auditing issue and grant events.
3.3.37 requires audit logs of access decisions and 13.3.6 covers access validation and entry/exit events, which is auditing validation and access events.
Entitlement consumption tracking together with entitlement audit reporting covers auditing redemption and consumption events.
5.5.18 requires a complete audit trail for transfers, ownership changes and entitlement assignments, which is this audit type.
Entitlement audit reporting covers reversal and refund events against an entitlement.
Entitlement audit reporting plus expiry management make expiry events auditable, which is what this asks for.
Entitlement audit reporting covers adjustment events made against an entitlement.
Balance inquiry is supported and entitlement audit reporting is required, but auditing read-only balance inquiries as an event type is not obliged.
Offline validity checking is required, but a named and versioned offline payload profile that can be selected per deployment is not.
3.1.10 requires ticket type to be embeddable in the secure token, which is this payload field.
3.1.10 requires venue access rights to be embedded in the token, which is the access areas carried in the payload.
3.1.10 names timeslot among the entitlement information embedded in the token.
3.1.10 names seat assignment among the embedded entitlement information, which covers seat and zone in the payload.
Token embedding and offline validity checking are required, but the validity window is not named among the fields the token must carry.
3.1.10 requires entitlement information to be embedded within the secure token, which is the entitlements summary in the payload.
No candidate requires cryptographic signing of the offline payload or a configurable signing algorithm, leaving the offline trust model unspecified.
Version tracking exists for software and content, but versioning of the offline access payload schema itself is not required anywhere.
A severity taxonomy exists for notifications, but the board's Healthy / Warning / Critical status legend is not defined by any requirement.
adjudicator_note: Third distinct status taxonomy seen across these packs; the boards should agree on one before sign-off.

rationale: The matrix governs permissioned access to CRM, wallet, loyalty, financial and inventory data, but nowhere requires the entitlements board to be fed from those eight named sources.
A data-freshness timestamp with timezone and an explicit refresh action, i.e. the board's refresh contract, are missing.
The individual eligibility and restriction capabilities are required, but a single board consolidating their management is not.
This is the design pack's own traceability annotation naming the matrix items the board claims to satisfy, not a behaviour of the system.
adjudicator_note: The pack asserts coverage of 1.1.38 and 1.1.121-127; that claim should be reconciled with this adjudication.

rationale: Channel-based restrictions and per-channel eligibility rules are required, but a board-level channel context selector defaulting to all channels is not.
Nothing in the candidates requires a global search control in the administrative application chrome; 22.10.26 is CMS site search for guests.
Eligibility rules are configurable, but a reusable rule library - and navigation to it - is not a matrix requirement.
Sandbox test data management exists, but saved eligibility test scenarios reachable from this board are not required.
Incident and exception logging exists at front gate sales, but a worked exception queue for eligibility decisions is not required.
Audit history of configuration and rule changes is required, but a shortcut to it from this board is not specified.
1.1.38 requires configuration of ticket eligibility rules across age, height, residency, nationality, membership, loyalty, entitlement and custom conditions, which is what this authoring frame does.
